articleTitle: Passivity-Based Stability Criterion for Small Signal Stability Analysis of DC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of converter-interfaced generation, ensuring the small-signal stability of the interconnected system becomes crucial. It is important to specify local grid-connectivity criteria whenever an individual converter is connected to or disconnected from the system, without necessarily obtaining the entire model of the microgrid system. To address this issue, this article introduces the concepts of passivity and a passivity-based stability criterion (PBSC). The article provides a proof of the criterion and applies a comprehensive PBSC to study the stability of DC microgrids (MGs). This criterion ensures the stability of a DC MG, as long as each individual converter adheres to it. Additionally, a simulation model with an interface converter is implemented in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the effectiveness of the comprehensive passivity-based stability criterion.

articleTitle: LVRT During-fault-stage Equilibrium Point is Unnecessary for Renewable Grid-tied Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Transient synchronous stability of renewable grid- tied systems is of paramount importance. Most of previous studies focused on the grid-tied converter in the low voltage ride through (LVRT) during-fault stage and performed stability analysis based on the belief that if the system has (or has no) a stable equilibrium point in the during-fault stage, the system will be stable (or unstable). Therefore, it has been broadly accepted that the existence and/or stability of equilibrium point in the during-fault stage is necessary. However, the whole LVRT contains four different stages and the during-fault stage is only one among them. The transient synchronous stability of whole system should be determined by the initial state in the late post-fault stage and the attraction basin of its equilibrium point. The late post-fault stage is essential for stability and all four stages are important. Clearly treating the during-fault stage as the whole LVRT stages makes the nonlinear switched dynamics problem be greatly simplified and, certainly, is incomplete. In order to clarify this point, this paper analyzes the influence of existence (or nonexistence) of equilibrium point in the during-fault stage on the transient synchronous stability of permanent magnet synchronous generator grid-tied system. We can find that the existence of an equilibrium point in the during-fault stage is only a sufficient condition, rather than a necessary condition. The theoretical analysis is also verified in the hardware-in-the-loop experiment Therefore, a large number of previous studies and results on the transient synchronous stability of renewable grid-tied systems are incomplete and questionable.

articleTitle: Insulator String Defect Detection in Substation Based on Joint Learning and YOLOv4
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The integrity of substation insulator strings has been attached great importance, which will have a direct impact on the reliability and safety of substations. A joint learning and YOLOv4-based defect monitoring method is proposed in this thesis for substation insulator string defects to better train the insulator defect detection model by utilizing insulator data subject to communication and privacy constraints. The method is designed with asynchronous joint learning and further scheduling algorithms, which are simulated and optimized for real complex scenarios. Model training and performance testing were completed using the Chinese transmission line insulator dataset. And the experimental results indicate that the detection model trained by federated learning is effective and the performance is comparable to that of centralized YOLOv4. In addition, federated learning protects the security of power data belonging to different organizations, breaks the industry data silos, and makes the utilization of more insulator data possible.

articleTitle: Short-term Prediction of Wind Power by TCN-SA Model Based on Dual Feature Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To solve the problem of low accuracy of current wind power output prediction models, a short-term wind power prediction model based on Pearson coefficient, Gradient boosting decision tree (GBDT), dual feature extractor (DFE), temporal convolutional network (TCN) and self-attention (SA) mechanism was proposed. Firstly, dual feature extractor is used to extract important features; Secondly, the extracted important features are used as the input of the TCN-SA combined model for short-term prediction of wind power. Finally, a 200MW wind power station in China is verified by a numerical example, and the prediction accuracy of the combined model is better.

articleTitle: Intelligent Selective Aggregation Method for Offshore Wind, Thermal Power, and Energy Storage Systems Based on Set Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the integration of offshore wind power, thermal power, and energy storage systems to enhance energy efficiency and grid stability. Using set theory, we developed a framework for constructing and evaluating configurations of these energy sources. The study shows that energy storage mitigates the intermittency of offshore wind power by storing excess energy during high output and releasing it during low output, optimizing wind energy use and supporting thermal power regulation. Our method provided a systematic approach to evaluate potential configurations, revealing specific setups that achieve high wind power consumption, economic benefits, and effective thermal power synergy. This research offers valuable insights for integrating renewable energy sources, supporting a low-carbon, renewable energy-driven future in China's Southeast coastal regions.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation Of Park Integrated Energy System Considering Supply-Demand Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In view of the fact that the existing reliability evaluation method of integrated energy system(IES) does not consider supply-demand uncertainty, this project studies the reliability evaluation method of integrated energy system in the park considering both supply and demand uncertainties. Firstly, the energy center is considered, and its modeling and simulation are carried out. Secondly, combined with the network capacity reduction model and the electricity price response strategy, the influence of uncertain factors in supply and demand on the output of the device is quantitatively described. On this basis, a variety of indicators were used to quantify the stability of IES. Finally, an example is given to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Design of PMSM Sliding Mode Controller Based on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In addition to reduce the system cost, the permanent magnet synchronous motor(PMSM) about sensorless control technology heightens the system reliability. The estimation of nonlinear velocity/angle algorithm ground on an adaptive sliding mode observer can realize sensorless sensor operation of PMSM motors. According to PMSM about the mathematical model, the difference between the gauged current and the reckoned current is used to form the sliding mode surface, and the estimated value of inmotive momentum is fed back to the motor current for observation. At present, the mainstream design is based on the architecture of DSP + FPGA. DSP has limited resources, and the sliding control algorithm has a large amount of calculation, so DSP cannot meet the design of the whole control system algorithm. Therefore, this paper uses the Zynq series FPGA provided by Xilinx to design the PMSM control system and extend the design of the subsequent algorithms.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization Configuration of Shared Energy Storage and Transmission Lines Considering Multi-time Scale Demand
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Collaborative optimization configuration of shared energy storage (SES) and transmission lines can satisfy the multi-timescale power balancing demand of high percentage new energy grids while delaying transmission lines expansion and saving cost. A bi-level collaborative optimization configuration model of SES and transmission lines which considers multi-timescale demand is proposed to improve the economics of collaborative configuration. Firstly, the collaborative optimization configuration of SES and transmission lines consider the multi-timescale power balancing demand of high percentage new energy grids. Secondly, a bi-level collaborative optimization configuration model of SES and transmission lines is established. The upper level model aims to minimize the total cost of SES investment and transmission lines expansion to realize the investment decision of SES and transmission lines. The lower level model is based on upper level investment planning scheme and multi-timescale demand, aiming to minimize the integrated system operation cost for optimizing the SES charging and discharging strategies. Finally, the validity of the model is verified by simulation using the improved IEEE RTS24-Bus system.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Prediction of Distributed PV based on Normalized Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a probabilistic forecasting model for distributed photovoltaic (PV) power generation systems based on normalizing flows and spatio-temporal information coupling. The efficiency and power generation of distributed PV systems are significantly affected by geographic location, with spatial correlations between locations having a major impact on the power distribution. Thus, this paper introduces a time-lag correlation matrix as a representation of spatial information, compresses it using an auto-encoder, and couples it with a gated recurrent unit (GRU) to form a point prediction model. Additionally, considering the uncertainties in PV output, the paper employs a normalizing flow method to infer the probability density function, combining it with the point prediction model's temporal relationship capturing ability to form the final probabilistic forecasting model.

articleTitle: The Influence of Tree Branch Structure and Position on Tree Flash Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: One of the main reasons for large-scale shutdown of transmission lines caused by tree flash faults. A large amount of research has been conducted on the hazards of mountain fires after tree flash faults occur both domestically and internationally, but there is little research on the process and causes of tree flash faults. In order to understand the correlation between transmission line tree flash faults and tree branch parameters, tree flash fault tests were conducted under different tree branch structures, tree branch moisture content, tree line distance and other influencing factors. The impact of each factor on the occurrence of tree flash faults was analyzed, and the equivalent relationship between the probability of fault occurrence and tree branch parameters was obtained. The conclusion is as follows: The branch structure does not objectively have a significant impact on the occurrence of tree flash problems; For the distance between tree lines, as the distance between tree lines increases, the probability of tree flashing increases significantly after reaching the threshold; For the moisture content of tree branches, the higher the moisture content of the branches, the lower the probability of tree flash occurrence. The research conclusion can provide reference for the assessment of the occurrence status of tree flash faults in transmission lines and the implementation of forest fire warning systems.

articleTitle: Dynamic Synchronous Phasor Measurement Algorithm Considering out of Band Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Due to the significant errors caused by out of band interference in fundamental wave measurement, its impact cannot be ignored. However, the signal models in existing measurement methods cannot fully characterize the dynamic characteristics of out of band components and signals. This article proposes a dynamic phasor measurement algorithm that considers out of band interference to address this issue. Firstly, a mixed phasor model containing out of band interference and fundamental signals is established. Then, rough fundamental and out of band phasors are estimated through discrete Fourier transform, and based on this, estimated values of fundamental and out of band frequencies are obtained. Then determine whether the signal contains out of band interference and call the corresponding offline matrix to solve for the unknown Taylor derivative. Finally, use Monte Carlo simulation in Matlab to establish an ideal signal testing algorithm performance.

articleTitle: A Novel DC Fault Clearing Strategy for HVDC based on Hybrid MMC
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Hybrid modular multilevel converter-based high voltage direct current transmission system has the ability to clear DC fault current, however, this converter-based strategy will lead to the overvoltage problem in the full-bridge submodules (FBSMs), which will cause damage to the capacitors and ultimately affect safe operation of the system. Otherwise, the overvoltage problem also increases the voltage difference between the FBSMs and the half-bridge submodules (HBSMs), which prolongs the restart time of the converter. Therefore, this paper has proposed a novel DC fault clearing strategy which further reduces the overvoltage in the FBSMs compared to strategies in other literature. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy has been validated in simulation results.

articleTitle: Optimal Configuration of Active Distribution Network Based on Soft Open Point
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: At present, the distribution network is still in the state of “closed design loop, yet functioning in an open loop.”. As the load increases and a large number of distributed photovoltaic systems are connected, the distribution grid becomes vulnerable to voltage instability, reduced voltage levels, the challenge of making full use of new energy sources, and increased transmission line losses.To enhance the existing conditions of the distribution network, this study introduces a Soft Open Point (SOP) planning strategy.Firstly, the k-means clustering technique is employed to create representative scenarios for photovoltaic (PV) output, derived from data pertaining to PV power generation. In order to ensure maximum absorption of new energy, scenarios with maximum PV output are selected as the substitute, and SOP double-layer planning model is established. The upper layer takes economic indicators as the target for SOP location determination and capacity determination, and the lower layer takes loss and voltage offset as the target for optimization. The optimization results are then returned to the upper layer. Finally, the method is analyzed and verified by an example of IEEE33 nodes.

articleTitle: Synergetic Controller Design for Two-stage Cascaded Hydropower Stations with Regulating Reservoir
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Realizing the stability control of cascaded hydropower stations is the basis for guaranteeing the safe development of hydropower resources in the basin. This paper introduces synergetic control theory to enhance the stability and operational safety of the regulation system in two-stage cascaded hydropower stations. Firstly, a mathematical model is developed for cascaded hydropower stations, incorporating the regulating reservoir, and then based on the synergetic control theory, the synergetic control law of cascaded hydropower station unit controllers is deduced, and a synergetic controller (SC) taking into account the unit speed regulation and regulating reservoir level regulation is designed. Finally, through the simulation experiments, the dynamic response performances of the proposed SC and the classical PID controller are compared. The results show that the proposed synergistic controller can realize the simultaneous regulation of unit speed and regulating reservoir level in cascaded hydropower stations, which is better than the classical PID controller. The SC improves the stability of cascaded hydropower stations operation under the load disturbance condition.

articleTitle: Short Term Load Forecasting for Users Based on Homomorphic Encryption and Dual Model Data-driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: An analysis was conducted on the characteristics of the new power system, and a dual model deep learning algorithm based on linear decomposition was proposed to address the issues of strong user data volatility and protection of data privacy in short-term load forecasting. A short-term load forecasting model based on this algorithm was established. Firstly, the data is divided into linear and nonlinear components using the moving average algorithm. The linear components are trained using the BiGRU model, while the nonlinear components are trained using the LSTM model. After training, the data is merged to achieve dual data driving; During data transmission, Paillier homomorphic encryption algorithm is used to ensure data privacy; Using real data to calculate relevant indicators and conducting comparative experiments with previous methods, the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm was verified.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Islanded PV-battery DC Microgrid Considering Different Operating Points of PV Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the development of renewable energy and power electronics technology, DC loads and DC power supplies are in sustainable growth. Over AC microgrid, DC microgrid features advantages such as lower losses and simpler control. Its stability is worth studying. This paper discusses the relative size of stability margin of an islanded PV-battery DC microgrid. For PV array, when its output power is smaller than its maximum output power, there are two control strategies to make steady-state operating points respectively located in the left half and right half of PV characteristic curve. By establishing small-signal model, getting output impedance and input impedance of correlated converters and obtaining the stability margin of the studied DC microgrid under two control strategies when the controller parameters, converter parameters and PV output power are the same, the conclusion is drawn: the control strategy positioning the steady-state operating point in left half of PV curve makes the studied DC microgrid more stable.

articleTitle: A Fault Risk Assessment Method for Security Control Systems Based on Control Strategy Influence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The security control system is an important facility to ensure the safe operation of the power grid in the event of serious faults. The failure of its device will cause serious consequences to the operation and maintenance of the power grid. Based on the analysis of the structure and function chain of the security control system, this paper proposes a quantitative assessment method for fault risk based on the influence of control strategies. Construct a risk assessment indicator system from three perspectives: the proportion of control strategies, the substitutability of control strategies, and the degree of control loss. Finally, combined with a simulation case, the correctness and feasibility of the evaluation method were verified.

articleTitle: Frequency-Voltage Coordinated Support Control Strategy for MMC-HVDC Connected Offshore Wind Farms Based on Voltage Situation Partition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the swift expansion of wind farms, the share of renewable energy has steadily risen, leading to a prominent issue of insufficient frequency and voltage support capability. Current control strategies are typically designed for either frequency or voltage support separately, but in practice, these two disturbances are often intertwined. Therefore, a coordinated support control strategy needs to be investigated. In this paper, a full electromagnetic transient model of MMC-HVDC connected offshore wind farms is built first. Then, the active and reactive power margin of MMC-HVDC is analyzed with mainstream frequency regulation and voltage regulation control methods. Employing the active and reactive power priority control logic, a frequency-voltage coordinated support control strategy based on voltage situation partition is proposed. Through the PSCAD/EMTDC simulation platform, three different scenarios under voltage and load disturbance were simulated to verify the proposed strategy. The simulation results indicate that the proposed coordinated control strategy can effectively improve the frequency and voltage support capability of the offshore wind system and enhance the grid's frequency-voltage resilience.

articleTitle: A Review On The Connotation And Supporting Requirements Of Virtual Inertia In Active Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The active distribution network has poor disturbance resistance, and the network security boundary is difficult to characterize and evaluate. It is necessary to characterize the virtual inertia, and the distributed source load support ability in the distribution network is limited and difficult to coordinate control under various disturbances. It is urgent to establish a virtual inertia adaptive allocation and collaborative control method for the self governance area of the distribution network. This article first introduces the connotation of virtual inertia, and based on this, proposes the support capacity of virtual inertia in distribution systems and the evaluation of system inertia requirements. Finally, it elaborates on the allocation and control of virtual inertia in distribution systems, and summarizes the research in the field of inertia related to distribution systems.

articleTitle: Unit Commitment Optimization for High-Proportion Clean Energy Grids with Both Power Supply and Demand Considering Frequency Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: New energy power electronic equipment, characterized by lack of inertia, low disturbance resistance, and weak support, poses significant challenges to the power grid. When faults such as DC blocking occur, high-proportion clean energy grids with both generation and consumption will face greater pressure on grid frequency stability. However, with the rising amount of new energy, it is essential not only to enhance grid operational stability but also to accommodate the integration of new energy. Against the backdrop of regions rich in hydropower resources, this paper proposes a cascade hydropower unit commitment optimization strategy for high-proportion clean energy grids with both generation and consumption, considering frequency stability. First, the main entities for regulation on the power supply side are modeled. Then, a unit combination optimization model is presented. In the end, the strategy's effectiveness is confirmed by a case study of cascade hydropower in a particular basin.

articleTitle: Strategies for Suppressing Overvoltages at Distributed New Energy Stations in the Receiving-End Grid Following Fault Clearance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Due to the large-scale integration of distributed new energy stations into the receiving end power grid, overvoltage issues caused by faults in the receiving system will be significantly exacerbated. It threatening the safe and stable operation of the power system. This paper analyzes the voltage controllable resources of receiving-end new energy stations and proposes a coordinated overvoltage suppression strategy based on distributed new energy stations. Furthermore, a simulation project is constructed, and simulation verification is conducted using the PSCAD-MATLAB co-simulation method. The results indicate that the proposed strategy can effectively suppress the overvoltage issue at receiving-end new energy stations after commutation failure, ensuring the safe and stable operation of the system.

articleTitle: Error Compensation Method for DC Shunt
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the energy metering circuit of non-vehicle-mounted chargers, voltage is collected through a voltage divider network, and current is collected through a shunt. A shunt, typically made of manganese copper, generates heat when current passes through it. The resistance value of the shunt changes with its temperature, leading to a nonlinear relationship between the voltage output at both ends of the shunt and the current flowing through it before thermal equilibrium is reached. In this study, two commonly used shunts were selected, and their voltage-time curves at different currents were tested to analyze the relationship between measurement error and time. The least squares fitting method was applied to compensate for the error of one of the shunts. This approach improved the accuracy of DC current measurement and ensured the accuracy and reliability of trade settlement data for charging facilities.

articleTitle: Real-Time Simulation Modeling Method for UHVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: China has built dozens of ultra-high-voltage direct-current(UHVDC) projects to achieve trans-regional electricity transmission. Accurate modeling is crucial for analyzing power grids with UHVDC projects. However, the widely used UHVDC model based on the electromagnetic transient simulation platform has difficulty meeting the demand for fast simulation due to large calculation amounts and low efficiency. To improve the simulation efficiency, This paper presents a method for modeling UHVDC systems using the real-time simulation platform RT-LAB. First, the structure and control strategy of the UHVDC system are analyzed. Then, combined with the software configuration process, A real-time simulation model of the UHVDC system was developed using the RT-LAB platform. Finally, the response characteristics of the established model are analyzed through case studies. By comparing with the Simulink-based electromagnetic transient model, it is proved that the established model has significantly higher efficiency.

articleTitle: Study on the Value of Lost Load of Three Provinces in China Based on Production Function Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In recent years, there have been many power outages in China due to power shortage and other problems, and it is urgent to formulate power rationing policies that can minimize economic losses in the case of power shortage. The order and period of power rationing should be selected according to the value of lost load (VOLL) in electricity markets. However, VOLL of different industries in different provinces of China is few. In order to solve this problem, this paper used the production function approach to calculate VOLL and marginal VOLL of different industries in Jiangsu, Ningxia and Xinjiang provinces. This allowed for the identification of high VOLL industries in each province and the analysis of the trends in marginal VOLL across these provinces. Furthermore, for the four major industries with substantial electricity consumption in Jiangsu, this paper compiled the average electricity consumption on weekday and weekend for different seasons throughout the year. This data was used to determine the hourly electricity values for various industries in different seasons. Finally, following the guidelines in the industry user's off-peak electrical power restriction manual [1], the paper calculated the economic losses for different industries at different times under varying degrees of electrical power restriction.

articleTitle: Analysis and Control of MMC with Zero-sequence Injection Fault-tolerant Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: For modular multilevel converter (MMC) without redundant submodules (SMs), it is necessary to use zero-sequence injection as a fault-tolerance strategy after SM faults. However, the internal operation of the MMC will be inevitably affected after injection for these two reasons: first, different number of operating SM in the upper and lower arms results in different capacitance for the whole arm. Secondly, the injection of zero-sequence components will affect the energy transfer between arms and between phases. This paper investigates how the above two reasons lead to the circulating current problem through rigorous calculations. In order to stabilize the internal operation of MMC, a circulating current control with feed-forward is established to enable faster control of the circulating current after fault. Simulations and experiments validate the proposed control.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Island Integrated Energy Systems Considering Demand Response and System Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Climate variability on the islands can lead to unstable new energy generation, and their volatility and uncertainty pose major challenges to the secure and flexible operation of the island integrated energy system (IES). To enhance the system operational flexibility of island IES, an scheduling method that considers system operational flexibility are presented in this paper. First, The objective function focuses on improving the economic efficiency. Then ensure stable power supply within the system by quantifying the flexibility within the island system and establishing its constraints. Moreover, we establish the balance constraints of electricity, heat, hydrogen, and fresh water to ensure the basic survival of the island. Finally, the proposed optimal scheduling model is simulated and verified. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can balance the island's energy supply and demand while effectively enhancing system flexibility.

articleTitle: A method for identifying familial defects in relay protection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The extraction of familial defects in relay protection equipment in this article plays an important role in identifying common safety hazards in the safe operation of the power grid. Starting from the defect characteristics of historical defect cases, this article extracts the defect characteristics of various types of relay protection equipment on site, forming a relay protection defect feature library, which helps to achieve precise characterization of different characteristics of relay protection defects. Based on this, a logic for identifying family defects in relay protection is proposed to identify family defects in relay protection and enhance the support level for the safe operation of the power grid.

articleTitle: A Hyperbolic Function Method for Repetitive Controller Construction Based on Magnetic Flux Controllable APF
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Repeating controller based on negative feedback can only compensate odd harmonics and can be applied to single-phase system, while in three-phase system, the number of harmonics is 6k±1(k=1, 2, 3…) times, so it is necessary to consider the structure of the repeatitive control applied to three-phase system. In this paper, a hyperbolic function construction method is proposed to construct the basic structure of repetitive controllers from mathematical principles, and the basic idea is to construct repetitive controllers with the pole positions located at ±j(6k±1)ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf>(k=0, 1, 2…), which can be applied in the crossover control of different harmonics when the series active power filter(SAPF) is applied to single-phase and three-phase systems. In this paper, the correctness and feasibility of the proposed hyperbolic function method for constructing the repetitive controllers are verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection of Transformer Based on NGO and DBSCAN
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The conventional anomaly detection techniques for transformers are inadequate for accurately identifying anomalous states. This paper proposes an anomaly detection method for big data analysis based on NGO (Northern Goshawk Optimization) and DBSCAN (Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise). DBSCAN is insensitive to noise and abnormal value, exhibits robust performance, and is capable of automatically adapting to data distribution and complexity. The DBSCAN unsupervised density clustering algorithm is employed for anomaly detection in big data analytic. The DBSCAN is characterized by its insensitivity to noise and outliers, its robustness, and its flexibility, which enables it to adapt to the distribution and complexity of data. The model optimizes the parameters ε (radius of the neighborhood) and MinPts (minimum number of points contained in the neighborhood) in DBSCAN using the NGO. Thereafter, the data is clustered by DBSCAN in order to differentiate between normal and abnormal data. The clustering results are combined with the abnormal state determination rules in order to judge that the transformer is in an abnormal state. Upon analyzing the example results express that the NGO-DBSCAN algorithm possesses higher clustering efficiency than the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Scatter Search (SS) optimized DBSCAN. In addition, the algorithm is able to detect anomalous states of the monitoring transformer earlier.

articleTitle: Considering Demand Response for Collaborative Optimization of Source and Load Operations in High Energy Consuming Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the advancement of China's "dual carbon" goals, high-energy-consuming enterprises have become primary energy consumers and key targets for energy conservation and carbon reduction. This paper explores their participation in demand response for electricity and heat loads. By leveraging their adjustable resources and optimizing coordination with the grid, we promote the integration of new energy sources, thereby reducing operational costs and providing economic compensation for enterprises. Firstly, electricity and heat loads are categorized into transferable, reducible, and substitutable loads. Secondly, an energy cost model is developed based on these characteristics. Lastly, an optimization model is constructed to minimize operational, energy consumption, and purchased electricity costs. Comparative analysis demonstrates that the proposed model effectively reduces operational costs and enhances new energy integration.

articleTitle: A Data-driven Method for Forecasting the Photovoltaic Substation Active Power
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing need for accuracy in PV active power prediction, a new model combining variational mode decomposition (VMD), sparrow search algorithm (SSA), and long short-term memory neural network (LSTM) was established, named VMD-SSA-LSTM. Initially, VMD was utilized to break down historical PV active power and environmental sequence data Afterwards, LSTM parameters were optimized using SSA, and each decomposition component was input into the LSTM neural network. The forecasted outputs of each component were summed to derive the predicted PV active power value for the substation, which was verified with data from a specific region. Results indicate that, in comparison to the LSTM and VMD-LSTM models, the VMD-SSA-LSTM model achieves superior prediction accuracy, offering a new choice for predicting PV active power in substations.

articleTitle: Modeling and Optimal Operation of Mobile Energy Storage Units Considering the Operation Safety of the Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Amid the global energy transition and climate change, the increasing integration of distributed wind and photovoltaic power generation presents significant challenges to power systems. Mobile energy storage technology can increase renewable energy consumption by altering the load demand on the distribution grids, while also refining the stability and reliability of the distribution networks. This paper proposes an optimized operation strategy for mobile energy storage units, considering the load regulation capability of the distribution networks. By analyzing the load regulation capabilities and characteristics of mobile energy storage units, a comprehensive operational framework is constructed. Additionally, a physical model for mobile energy storage that accounts for mobility constraints is developed. The dispatch center is dedicated to curtailing the operational expense of the distribution power network by devising an optimization problem grounded in the principles of optimal power flow. This framework is subsequently reformulated into a mixed-integer second-order cone optimization problem. The IEEE33-node based simulation outcomes demonstrate that mobile energy storage can alleviate grid congestion, reduce network losses, and enhance the integration and utilization of renewable sources.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Distribution System Operator and Prosumers Based on Mixed Game Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the development of residential photovoltaic (PV), the traditional end users in the distribution network are transformed into prosumers. However, the distribution network and prosumers belong to different stakeholders, and the traditional centralized holistic scheduling is difficult to reconcile heterogeneous interests in reality. A mixed game model is proposed to optimize the operation of the distribution system operator (DSO) and prosumers, which consists of two stages. The first stage is a Stackelberg game between the DSO and the prosumer coalition. In the second stage, the prosumer coalition plays a cooperative game with Nash bargaining. The mixed game model is solved by resorting to the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions, big M method, and strong duality theorem. Finally, the effectiveness of our proposed strategy is verified in a modified IEEE 33-bus distribution network with 3 prosumers.

articleTitle: An Improved Adaptive Virtual Impedance Current Limiting Strategy for Grid-Forming Inverters Under Symmetrical Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper presents an improved adaptive virtual impedance (ADVI) current limiting strategy in grid-forming (GFM) inverters utilizing single loop voltage magnitude (SLVM) control. The method includes two main improvements: introducing an exponential decay function model for the virtual resistance, which provides a large virtual resistance at the fault instance to limit transient overcurrent peaks and dampen current oscillations, and an inverse proportional model of the virtual reactance influenced by the voltage magnitude at the point of common coupling (PCC), which ensures a smaller reactance value during minor faults, thus enhancing the inverter’s overcurrent capability. The proposed strategy effectively improves transient current response at the fault instance and optimizes steady-state overcurrent utilization. The effectiveness of this strategy is validated through comprehensive simulations and experimental results.

articleTitle: Development of Beidou Tamed Rubidium Atomic Clock Device Based on FPGA Technology in Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Time synchronization is a prerequisite for the stable operation of the power system, and it provides a guarantee for the normal operation of the power system. In order to improve the accuracy and stability of the rubidium atomic clock frequency, equipment with multi output GNSS taming rubidium atomic frequency standard is designed based on FPGA technology. The taming and time tracking and synchronization of the rubidium atomic frequency are realized by the method of measuring the time interval using the rough and the fine measurements. Modular design and programming are used to improve the generality and transferability of the device. The data of rubidium atomic clock before and after taming were compared and tested many times taking the time and frequency of cesium atomic clock as reference. The results show that the accuracy of the device frequency reaches 1.5E-13 and stability runs up to 6.97E-13. Compared with before taming, the accuracy and stability of rubidium atomic clock frequency have been greatly improved. The device improves the key performance parameters of rubidium atomic clock, and provides more accurate, stable and reliable time and frequency signals for rubidium atomic clock as the standard source of time and frequency of power system, and guarantees the precision of time synchronization and timing of power system.

articleTitle: Performance Analyses and Optimization of Small-Scale Biogas Liquefaction System which is used in Biogas power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing demand of renewable electricity and hybrid configuration of multi-energy systems, biogas become more and more important in power system. For the purpose of reducing the humidity and increasing the methane concentration of raw biogas, a liquefaction process is needed. In this work, a kind of small-scale system used for biogas liquefaction was designed for biogas upgrading to solve the problems of transport and storage. Aspen HYSYS was used to study the effect of parameters of the working fluid. Exergy analysis was also carried out with the basic system referred as Case 1, the results from the simulation indicated that the compressor and heat exchanger are the most exergy destructive part of the system, which accounting for about 56.6% and 15.6% of the total exergy destruction. Then, an optimized system referred as Case 2 was designed and the comparison between Case 1 and Case 2 showed that Case 2 has a lower energy consumption and higher liquefaction rate.

articleTitle: Study of Micro-inverter-based PV Grid-connected Control Strategy Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the swift growth of our economy, our reliance on energy is escalating, underscoring the increasing significance of utilizing renewable green energy. The inverter is the central piece of equipment in a solar power system. In this paper, based on the interleaved flyback microinverter, the proposed current internal loop quasi-proportional resonance (Q-PR) control strategy reduces the total harmonic distortion rate of grid-connected currents, realizes static-free tracking, and achieves better grid-connection even under the disturbance of grid voltage. The MPPT optimized gradient method improves the conversion efficiency of PV cells to a greater extent, so that the microinverter can output at maximum power when grid-connected, overcoming the shortcomings of low energy utilization of traditional centralized inverters.

articleTitle: Optimized ESS Comprehensive Control Strategy for Primary Frequency Regulation of Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy sources in power systems causes significant security issues. Energy storage systems (ESSs) enhance system stability and reliability due to their fast response and bidirectional regulation. This paper proposes a self-adaptive comprehensive frequency regulation (FR) strategy for ESS in primary FR, considering the state of charge (SOC) of ESS. A self-adaptive control model for ESS charge/discharge coefficients and an optimized frequency control (OFC) strategy are developed for non-ideal SOC states. A weight coefficient model for virtual inertial and droop control is constructed for different FR stages. MATLAB/Simulink simulations validate the strategy's effectiveness in improving ESS primary FR performance under various disturbances.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Live Detection System for Porcelain Post Insulators Based on Vibration Principles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Porcelain post insulators are essential components of power plants and substations, extensively used in power systems to support conductors, circuit breakers, and high-voltage switches. However, existing detection methods for porcelain insulators require power outages, which are inefficient and cannot provide full coverage. There is still a gap in research on more efficient live detection technologies for porcelain insulators. This paper focuses on the design of a defect detection system for live detection technology. By extracting the spectral features of vibration signals using Fourier transform and establishing a defect feature library through finite element analysis, rapid identification of internal defects is achieved. A signal acquisition and processing system based on piezoelectric accelerometers was designed. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the design were verified through field tests.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven Risk Identification and Early Warning Model for Electricity Spot Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the vigorous development of electricity spot market and the rapid transformation of energy structure in China, market risks have significantly increased, making the risk early warning mechanism an essential tool for guaranteeing the safe operation of the market. This paper proposes a data-driven risk identification and comprehensive risk level early warning model for the electricity spot market. Firstly, based on the characteristics of the market, Latin hypercube sampling is utilized to construct a diverse set of scenarios which simulate the market operations. Multiple risk indicators are established, and risks are quantified through a market clearing model. Subsequently, the matter-element extension cloud model (MEECM) improved by the cloud entropy optimization algorithm is employed to classify the risks into five levels, ranging from I to V, for each time period. Finally, multiple deep neural networks are constructed to accurately predict single risk indicators for a single time period, and the MEECM is utilized to achieve an overall operational risk rating and early warning for the market. The results of case study demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed model in risk early warning.

articleTitle: Seamless Transition Strategy Based on Grid-Forming Energy Storage for Grid-Connected and Islanded Modes in Transformer Area Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a seamless transition strategy for transformer area microgrids based on grid-forming energy storage. A grid-forming control architecture is introduced for transformer area microgrid, and control strategy of grid-forming energy storage and microgrid on-grid and off-grid switching transition strategy based on grid-forming energy storage is designed. The strategy enhances the dynamic performance during transitions between grid-connected and islanded modes, addressing limitations in existing control methods. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed strategy in maintaining stable microgrid performance during mode transitions.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Electric Vehicle Charging Load Access on Distribution Network and Its Countermeasures
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The market penetration of electric vehicles(evs) as an important choice for green travel has increased rapidly. In order to explore the influence of electric vehicle access to distribution network in different seasons, this paper first proposed a method for forecasting charging demand considering Ev travel and charging behavior, taking into account the seasonal characteristics. Secondly, establish the load capacity evaluation model of distribution network including the load capacity of transformer and line. Finally, the actual operation data of charging facilities and the ownership data of electric vehicles in a certain range in Chongqing were used to predict the charging load of evs in different regions within the range. Based on the prediction results, carrying capacity of the distribution network within the range is analyzed and coping strategies are proposed.

articleTitle: A PV Hosting Capacity Assessment Method in Distribution Network Based on Successive Second-Order Cone Programming
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The excessive integration of photovoltaic (PV) in distribution network could result in technical problem, such as overvoltage problem, thermal overloading problem, etc. Consequently, how to evaluate the PV hosting capacity has emerged as a critical technology for the expansion planning of future distribution network. However, assessing the PV hosting capacity usually requires solving a non-convex optimization problem, although several relaxation methods have already been developed to relax the model, the exactness of these methods still remain a concern. To address this problem, a successive second-order cone programming (SOCP) approach with additional linearized error reduction constraints is proposed to reduce the relaxation gap introduced by the use of the SOCP relaxation in the PV hosting capacity problem. Moreover, a penalty item of the relaxation gap is added into the objective function to accelerate the convergence process. Simulations are conducted on an improved IEEE 33-bus system to validate the effectiveness of the successive SOCP approach.

articleTitle: Efficient and Lightweight: An Improved YOLOv8 Object Detector for Metal Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: A new lightweight metal surface defect detection model based on YOLOv8 is proposed to improve detection performance while meeting the practical needs of industrial deployment. The CSP Enhanced Convolutional-GLU Module (CECM) was designed to improve the neck network’s capability to extract and fuse complex defect features. Secondly, an efficient and lightweight asymmetric detection head (EADH) was implemented to improve detection precision. Thirdly, the Starnet backbone network was adopted to enhance feature extraction capabilities. Finally, a lightweight upsampling operator, the content-aware reassembly of features (CARAFE) module, was introduced to aggregate contextual information for feature processing. The mean average precision (mAP) on the NEU-DET dataset is 81.4%, which is an improvement of 12% and 6% over Faster R-CNN and the original YOLOv8 algorithm, respectively, with the FPS of 162.5. The results indicate that our algorithm offers an efficient and lightweight solution for the industrial application of metal defect detection.

articleTitle: A Novel Pulse Width Modulation for CLLC Resonant Converter under Light-Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The CLLC resonant converters are widely used in battery charging due to their bi-directional power flow and wide voltage range. However, the converter faces the problem of low efficiency under light load using pulse frequency modulation (PFM). Phase shift modulation (PSM) methods are usually used to solve the above problem, including dual-phase-shift (DPS) modulation, but PSM methods cause high circulating current. In this paper, a dual-side center-aligned pulse width modulation (DCPWM) method is proposed to enhance the light-load efficiency. To obtain the voltage gain and time-domain expressions of the main circuit variables, a time-domain model is first built. Based on the model, the soft-switching region and the constraint relationship between the control parameters can be further determined. Consequently, the circulating current of the proposed scheme can be lower compared to DPS, which reduces the switching and core losses. The simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Control Parameter Partition of Hydro-Turbine Regulation System Based on Regulation Oscillation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Ensuring the stability and rapid response of hydro-turbine regulation systems (HTRSs) is crucial in HTRS studies. In a fixed control structure, the adjustment of control parameters is a core optimization method. Therefore, this paper investigates the partition of control parameters based on oscillation characteristics, aiming to present the effect of control parameter adjustments on the system graphically. First, a state-space model of a dual-turbine HTRS is established and validated. Then, methods for determining the stability regions of control parameters and partitioning parameters based on oscillation characteristics are introduced. Building on these foundations, various boundaries of control parameters are determined, and the effect of main system parameters on various control parameter boundaries is analyzed. The results of parameter partitioning accurately reflect the effect of control parameter adjustments on oscillation characteristics and stabilization risk. An increase in Tw and a decrease in Ta significantly increase the risk of ultra-low-frequency oscillations. This paper provides reliable methods for regulation analysis and guidance for optimizing the operation of hydropower plants.

articleTitle: Economic and Low-carbon Dispatch of a Data Center Microgrid Considering Laddering Carbon Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the national integrated large data center system project, the construction of data centers in China has experienced rapid growth. However, the IT and cooling equipments in data centers consume large amounts of power. This poses significant challenges in terms of reducing power costs, energy consumption, and carbon emissions, thus affecting the sustainable development of data centers. Building data center microgrids is a good way to mitigate these issues. Then, this paper investigates the problem of energy dispatch for data center microgrids. Specifically, in this paper, we introduce the laddering carbon trading into the system cost of the data center microgrid. Then we minimize the total system cost by balancing the uncertainty of renewable energy, batch load, and energy storage. The case study verifies the proposed optimum yields an economic and low-carbon dispatch strategy, and reduces both carbon emission and costs.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Purchasing Strategy for Photovoltaic Prosumers Considering Demand Response under Multiple Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The rapid development of renewable energy, represented by distributed photovoltaics (PV), appears with deep interactions between flexible resources such as user-side controllable loads and the power grid. This trend is driving the transformation of traditional residential loads into prosumers, capable of both electricity generation and consumption. PV prosumers managed by aggregator, face multiple uncertainties and risks in day-ahead electricity purchasing and demand response scheduling. To address this, this paper proposes an optimal purchasing strategy tailored for PV prosumers, taking demand response into account. Initially, based on LSTM forecasting, it predicts electricity prices, load growth, and PV output, generating numerous scenarios within acceptable prediction margins. Subsequently, the K-medoids method is used to reduce scenario complexity. Then, a day-ahead purchasing model for aggregator is developed, aiming to minimize total costs while incorporating Conditional Value at Risk (CVaR) considerations. Finally, empirical validation through case studies demonstrates the effectiveness of this strategy in stabilizing aggregator purchasing costs across various scenarios, thereby enhancing their resilience in risk management.

articleTitle: A Locational Marginal Price Forecast Method Considering the Spatial Relation in Input Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Accurate locational marginal price (LMP) prediction is important for electricity market participants to form bidding strategies and improve profits. Machine-learning-based prediction models are attracting more attention for their advantages in capturing non-linear and complex relations between input features and LMPs. This paper proposes a framework to predict LMPs considering the spatial relation in input features by the graph attention network (GAT). Firstly, the spatial relation in input features with LMPs is analyzed. Then, a GAT-based LMP prediction framework is proposed. To validate the effectiveness, a simulation based on the Midcontinent Independent System Operator is implemented. The comparison result shows that the proposed framework can consider the spatial relation and achieve a higher prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Optimization for Wind Power Integration with Flywheel Energy Storage in Microgrid Systems based on Monte Carlo Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To address the issue of highly intermittent power output from wind energy conversion systems (WECS), a strategy involving backup generators and/or energy storage devices is suggested. When the installed capacity of WECS increases to the megawatt level, it becomes economically impractical to rely solely on backup generators, thus necessitating the use of energy storage devices to mitigate power output fluctuations. Short-term energy storage devices, particularly the Flywheel Energy Storage System (FESS), are favored due to their high-power density and suitability for small-scale systems. This paper proposes a combined system of wind power generator and energy storage device for microgrid applications, along with optimization of its install capacity and operation settings. Optimization is divided into two main sections: minimizing the installed capacity of the energy storage device and optimizing system settings. Through Monte Carlo simulations, optimal setting points are determined to minimize variations in system output.

articleTitle: Research on the Application Strategy of Electric Vehicle Participating in Peak-regulating Auxiliary Service Market
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The rapid development of new energy has promoted the large-scale application of electric vehicles in the power system, and many provinces in China have established a market mechanism adapted to the participation of electric vehicles in auxiliary services. At present, the participation of electric vehicle market mainly relies on online load forecast data and manual empirical forecast for declaration, and the deviation assessment is inefficient. By analyzing the typical domestic peak regulation market mechanism, this paper puts forward the electric vehicle load prediction model based on GA-BP neural network, and designs three kinds of declaration strategies for electric vehicle participation in the peak regulation market, and then verifies the accuracy and effectiveness of the proposed method through calculation examples, and puts forward the strategic suggestions for electric vehicles to participate in the peak regulation market.

articleTitle: Research on The Accuracy of New Energy Station Monitoring Data Based on Data Anomaly Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: New energy station monitoring data is becoming more and more important. This paper studies the accuracy evaluation method of new energy station monitoring data based on data anomaly identification. Firstly, real-time monitoring data collected by each monitoring node in the new energy station is obtained. Execute the pre-processing and cluster analysis of monitoring data in turn, define data monitoring standards, and preliminarily verify abnormal data in the monitoring process; Extract sample data from monitoring data, build anomaly identification model, comprehensively identify abnormal data in monitoring data, and dynamically optimize model identification performance based on incremental learning; Integrate all abnormal data in the monitoring process, and evaluate the accuracy of real-time monitoring data collected by new energy stations based on anomaly location and composition analysis. By integrating abnormal data for positioning and composition analysis, the accuracy of monitoring data of each monitoring node and station is comprehensively and accurately evaluated, to improve the reliability of data.

articleTitle: Repeated Low Voltage Ride-Through Phenomenon in New Energy Integration Systems and Its Mitigation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As new and renewable sources are increasingly integrated into the power grid on a large scale, the characteristics exhibited during low voltage ride-through (LVRT) have become increasingly noteworthy. This paper analyzes the mathematical relationship between the power output of renewable energy sources and the voltage at the point of grid connection, discovering the phenomenon of "repeated LVRT" caused by the transition of new energy operating points within the LVRT threshold. To address this novel type of voltage instability issue, the paper examines the positional relationship between the new energy operating points and the LVRT threshold curve. By reducing the LVRT threshold, thereby lowering the position of the LVRT threshold curve, and decreasing the active power generation from renewable energy sources to minimize the operating interval, the optimization strategy aims to prevent the intersection of the curve and the operating interval. This ensures that the control strategy of new energy does not change, thereby suppressing the voltage fluctuation phenomenon caused by "repeated LVRT." The feasibility of this strategy is validated using a simulation system.

articleTitle: Study on the Measurement of the Economics of Heavy Truck Electrification Transition and the Impact of Authorized Weight Amendment Policies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Both domestic and foreign countries have begun to pay attention to the electrification of heavy-duty trucks and actively carried out active deployment in policies and markets. To promote the zero-emission transition of heavy-duty trucks, this study employs the analysis of the total cost of ownership (TCO) measurement model, offering a quantitative analysis of the main challenges encountered in the electrification of heavy-duty trucks. Tonne-kilometer costs are assessed across three scenarios: 1C charging, conversion, and traditional fuel vehicles. The analysis concludes that, in the non-enclosed scenario, the economy of electric heavy trucks is slightly inferior to that of diesel heavy trucks due to the weight of the battery and the battery swapping mechanism resulting in a certain load loss. To expedite the promotion and advancement of electric heavy-duty trucks, it is imperative for the domestic government should formulate and implement the policy which increases the maximum authorized weight for zero-emission heavy trucks of 1-2 tonnes as soon as possible to provide better power support for the promotion and development of electric heavy trucks.

articleTitle: Design of an Indirect Carbon Emission Measurement Platform for the Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper presents the research and design of an indirect carbon emission measurement platform for the power system. The platform is structured across three layers: device, data, and application, integrating carbon emission monitoring, power transmission, and cloud computing. The principles and methodological models for the platform's measurement processes are introduced, with data correction and prediction performed using BP neural networks. An experimental simulation, using wind power generation as a case study, demonstrates a significant improvement in prediction accuracy. As technology advances and policies evolve, the application of the indirect carbon emission measurement platform is expected to make substantial contributions to achieving carbon neutrality and promoting sustainable development.

articleTitle: Wind-Storage Combined System Flexible Inertia Control Strategy Based On Minimum System Inertia Demand Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The inertia of power grid has decreased recently as a result of the widespread connection of wind power, which has negatively impacted the frequency stability of the system. This paper proposes an inertia demand-based wind-storage combined system inertia control strategy to overcome these issues. First, the minimum inertia demand of new energy is estimated based on system frequency safety constraints, then the inertia of synchronous generators and new energy is defined and calculated. Second, the inertia response process of the wind-storage combined system is analyzed and a frequency response model is built. Based on the inertia demand and characteristics of new energy, a wind-storage combined system flexible inertia control strategy is then suggested. This strategy takes the State of Charge (SOC) of energy storage into account. Finally, a PSCAD/EMTDC simulation model is constructed that validates the accuracy and efficacy of the suggested control strategy.

articleTitle: A Modified Ratio Braking Differential Current Protection Criterion for Energy Storage Station
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In current engineering practice, short circuit current of the energy storage is affected by the pre-fault charging and discharging state, and its active component is consistent with the pre-fault state. Therefore, when energy storage encounters an access line fault in the charging state, the phase difference between the short circuit current of it and that of the system on the other side of the line may be greater than 90°, which brings the risk of current differential protection refusal. In this paper, a modified ratio braking current differential criterion is proposed, which can effectively reduce the phase difference between the fault phase currents on the two sides of access line, avoid current differential protection refusal and improve the protection sensitivity. By simulation, this modified criterion is verified.

articleTitle: Dynamic Hierarchical Interpolation Method for Monthly Thermal Power Generation Forecasting Considering Long-period Localization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Thermal power generation forecasting becomes challenging due to the regulation of new energy sources, and time-based monthly forecasting methods suffer from cumulative error issues, in this paper, a dynamic hierarchical interpolation method for monthly thermal power generation forecasting considering long-period localization based on FFT and MLP is proposed. First, a long-period localization strategy is applied to the thermal power generation time series to calculate the period selection values and to constrain the monthly generation forecast model errors for different forecast capacity intervals. The dynamic hierarchical interpolation method is then utilized for power generation prediction, and the prediction results are returned to the dynamic hierarchical prediction results of the shifted step to correct them. Finally, an arithmetic example of the proposed method is analyzed to verify the accuracy of the results obtained by the prediction method.

articleTitle: Orderly Charging of Electric Vehicles Based on Hydrogen Microgrid in Zero Emission Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Addressing the charging requirements of electric vehicles (EVs) in a zero emission building (ZEB), this paper proposes an optimal control method of electric-hydrogen-electric vehicles in zero energy building systems. At first, the arrival time, departure time, and charging state of the EVs are collected. According to the user satisfaction index, the charging mode (fast charging or slow charging) of the EVs is selected, and an orderly charging scheduling method of EVs is developed based on the minimum peak-valley load difference. Then, a photovoltaic-hydrogen microgrid system considering EV load scheduling and building base load is constructed to ensure the maximum utilization of renewable energy to achieve ZEB. Monte Carlo simulation is used to simulate the randomness of EVs. Simulation results confirm that the proposed method can achieve the near-zero energy operation and effectively perform peak shaving and valley filling.

articleTitle: Knowledge Graph Enhanced Interactive Fault Diagnosis O&M Approach Based on Large Models of Electrical Power
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Power equipment operation and maintenance has accumulated a large amount of knowledge recorded in the form of text, which provides the basis for power equipment diagnosis and operation and maintenance. However, the huge amount of redundant knowledge makes it difficult for the relevant personnel to quickly access the information, and it is also impossible to integrate it into the existing diagnostic algorithms. For this reason, this paper proposes an interactive equipment diagnosis and operation and maintenance method based on knowledge graph and big model. First, the unstructured knowledge is transformed and constitutes the O&M (Operation and Maintenance) knowledge graph using entity extraction method; second, the conditional probability of the equipment feature quantity to the failure mode is fitted using graph convolution to realize the equipment failure diagnosis; subsequently, an intention recognition algorithm based on self-attention network is proposed and retrieval is realized; finally, the results are generated into natural language using the big language model. It is verified that the proposed diagnosis and intent recognition F1 values are improved by 9.77% and 17.48%, respectively, confirming the effectiveness of the system.

articleTitle: Grid Forming Hybrid Energy Storage System for Flexible Frequency Regulation in Islanded AC Microgrids
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Due to the widespread adoption of renewable energy sources like photovoltaic and wind power, the inertia of power grid systems has experienced a significant reduction. Consequently, the AC microgrid will experience increased frequency fluctuations and a larger frequency nadir, which may endanger the dynamic performance of the grid. In order to increase the inertia, the energy storage systems have been widely used. Based on the equivalent inertia model of the virtual synchronous machine, this paper designed a grid forming hybrid energy storage system (HESS) which consists of a supercapacitor (SC) and a battery, allocating low-frequency response of load power disturbance to battery and high-frequency response to SC, thereby increasing the inertia and providing flexible frequency regulation of the AC microgrid. In order to evaluate the effectiveness of frequency regulation provided by the HESS, simulation results are offered. According to the simulation results, the designed HESS can improve the frequency nadir of the AC microgrid and achieve reasonable power allocation.

Author Keywords: grid forming hybrid energy storage system

articleTitle: Electricity Theft Detection Method Based on User Consumption Patterns
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Electricity theft is the main cause of non-technical losses in the power grid. Most of the traditional electricity theft detection methods primarily focus on total electricity consumption at the station area or user aggregation level, making it difficult to detect individual behavioral anomalies and subtle changes, and ignoring key features such as consumption patterns or time series data. This paper proposes a method of electricity theft detection based on user consumption patterns. First, a non-intrusive load monitoring method based on modified cross-entropy is used to obtain the detailed usage of each load; then, detection indicators for electricity theft are proposed based on user consumption patterns; finally, for suspected users, the chi-square goodness-of-fit test is introduced to determine electricity theft behavior from the perspective of time-segmented. The simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Power Quality Disturbance Detection Algorithm Based on Distributed Compression Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing diversification of new energy generation and the trend of load equipment towards power electronics, the issue of power quality in data volume is becoming increasingly complex in the distribution network. In this paper, a compression storage method for power quality data based on distributed compression sensing and edge computing is proposed. An adaptive joint reconstruction algorithm is proposed in combination with a fast principal component analysis algorithm. In this paper, typical single and composite perturbation data are modelled, combining the sparse features of the perturbation data, the standard deviation and the number of principal frequencies as the classification features of the perturbation data. The compressed perception algorithm is used to detect various types of perturbations. Simulation results show that the detection accuracy of the algorithm is higher than existing algorithms and meets the accuracy requirements of M-class PMU measurements.

articleTitle: Current Compensation-Based Transient Stability Enhancement for an Islanded Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing incorporation of renewable energy via power electronic converters, islanded microgrids are susceptible to transient instability when faced with large disturbances, attributed to converters’ low inertia and high nonlinearity. This paper introduces a current compensation-based control strategy to enhance transient stability of an islanded MG. By incorporating frequency deviation between grid-following converter and grid-forming converter into current controller of grid-following converter, the balance between the system’s equivalent input and output torques can be accelerated. Compared with previous stability-enhanced method, the proposed strategy demonstrates superior performance in the aspect of small overshoot and fast convergence. Simulation results validate the analysis and effectiveness of this strategy.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Load Modeling Method for Power Systems Based on Particle Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This study introduces an approach for dynamic load modeling in power systems using the particle filter algorithm. Traditional state estimation methods have certain limitations when dealing with the nonlinear and non-Gaussian characteristics of sudden changes in motor loads. Therefore, this paper introduces the particle filter algorithm, which represents the posterior probability distribution of states through a collection of random specimens (particles) and can effectively handle nonlinear and non-Gaussian problems. By constructing a third-order state-space representation of the induction motor and combining it with the particle filter algorithm, real-time parameter estimation is performed. This study provides a new technical approach for dynamic load parameter identification in power systems. Experimental results show that this method has high estimation accuracy and robustness under conditions of sudden system changes.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Study of Solid Oxide Fuel Cell Cogeneration System Coupled with Electricity, Gas and Hydrogen
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) combined heat and power (CHP) systems offer the advantages of high efficiency, non-pollution, and good adaptability to a wide range of fuels, and thus can utilize hydrogen separated from a pipeline hydrogen-doped gas mixture as a fuel. However, the system is highly coupled, has many variables and is complex, and is prone to output fluctuations due to input variations. In order to ensure the stability of the cogeneration output of the SOFC cogeneration system and supply high-quality energy, a model predictive control method for this system is now proposed. Simulation results show that the control method exhibits excellent control effects under voltage perturbation and multiple setpoint perturbation.

articleTitle: An Active Disturbance Rejection Control Strategy For Direct-Drive Wave Energy Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In this paper, a proposal is made for the adaptation of a linear active disturbance rejection controller for a direct drive wave energy converter. The application of a direct drive wave energy converter (DDWEC) presents a simpler and efficient system as compared to the traditional wave energy converters.
