In order to suppress different disturbances and guarantee the current loop's steady state and dynamic performance, an active disturbance rejection controller is also integrated into it. By achieving this, an accurate current control and robust permanent magnet linear generator control are achieved.

articleTitle: Frequency Optimization Control of Microgrid Based on Liquid Hydrogen with SMES
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The frequency stability of microgrid is highlighted due to the uncertainty of renewable energy output and load volatility. Liquid Hydrogen with SMES (LIQHYSMES) is a new type hybrid energy storage system (HESS), which combining the advantages of large power with fast response and large capacity with long-time response. Therefore, it is a promising way to solve the frequency fluctuation problem of independent microgrid. This paper proposes LIQHYSMES’s coordinated optimal control strategy based on a group of adaptive variation of frequency control coefficients. Firstly, flexible dead zones of frequency modulation (FM) for SMES and Liquid Hydrogen (LH) are set according to their operational characteristics. The virtual inertia method and the virtual droop method, whose control coefficients are modified in real time based on the state of charge (SOC) and deviation of frequency, are used to SMES and Liquid Hydrogen respectively. Then the microgrid FM control model is established based on the proposed optimal control strategy. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation under typical load disturbances. In conclusion, the method proposed in this paper can realize the fast frequency support of independent microgrid to enhance operational reliability.

articleTitle: State of Charge and State of Energy Co-estimation for Lithium-ion Battery Based on PatchTST Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To optimize battery energy management, enhance battery safety performance, and improve its utilization efficiency, it is crucial to accurately estimate the State of Charge (SOC) and State of Energy (SOE) of lithium-ion batteries. Since the Transformer network is designed for natural language processing problems and has some drawbacks in long time series prediction tasks, this paper adopts a Transformer-based multivariate time series prediction model called Patch Time Series Transformer (PatchTST) to co-estimate battery SOC and SOE. The model uses Patch operations to extract local semantics from time series data, which makes its training faster and capable of handling longer input sequences. Compared with other Transformer-based models at room temperature, the proposed model improves SOC and SOE estimation by 36.8% and 41.1% respectively on the RMSE metric. The PatchTST was compared with several other algorithms, The algorithm demonstrates increased estimation accuracy for both SOC and SOE across various environmental temperature conditions.

articleTitle: Dynamic Reactive Power Allocation with Multi-source Coordination in the AC Collecting System of the Large Scale Renewable Energy Base
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The output of renewable energy power stations is typically characterized by volatility and randomness. In large scale renewable energy base, the issue of transient overvoltage following a system fault is more pronounced. The surplus of reactive power during the transient process is the main cause of the transient overvoltage problem. To address this, considering the performance of suppressing transient overvoltage peaks and reducing recovery time, a dynamic multi-reactive power source allocation scheme combining synchronous condensers and STATCOM is proposed. Firstly, by analyzing the reactive response time scales of synchronous condensers and STATCOM, theoretical support is provided for the allocation of dynamic multi-reactive power sources; secondly, during the allocation process, considering that the instantaneous reactive rate of reaction for synchronous condensers is faster than that of STATCOM, and in the control action link, the reactive rate of reaction for STATCOM is faster than that of excitation responses. It is suggested that synchronous condensers respond at the moment of the fault to offer immediate reactive power assistance, and during the fault recovery phase, STATCOM provide dynamic reactive power to accelerate the recovery of transient voltage; in conclusion, simulation is used to confirm the viability of the recommended distribution scheme. The research confirms that the dynamic multi-reactive power source allocation scheme combining synchronous condensers and STATCOM is more proficient in preventing transient overvoltage occurrences during transient process.

articleTitle: Short Term Wind Power Load Prediction Algorithm Based on MLE
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increasing penetration rate of new energy, short-term forecasting methods for wind solar load have become increasingly important. The regional level power system is the research object, and for regional level wind and photovoltaic forecasting, it refers to the method of predicting the output values of multiple wind/photovoltaic power plant clusters or the total upsampling value of wind/photovoltaic power in the entire region. Firstly, analyze and extract the correlation between the three predicted objects, and extract the coupling relationship between them. Then, a multi-layer extraction (MLE) MLE neural network is used as the prediction algorithm to further represent the coupling relationship between the predicted objects; Finally, the superiority of the proposed algorithm was verified through simulation. The experimental results indicate that the model has high prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: An Improved Fuzzy Logic Rule Based Energy Management Control for Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Energy management strategy is the major element to enhance the fuel economy of hybrid electric vehicles. Current energy management strategy still faces real-time application bottlenecks. To address this problem, this article proposes a deterministic rule according to vehicle demand torque, and battery SOC. In response to the limited fuel economy of this method, the rules were fuzzified, and then a particle swarm optimization algorithm was used to obtain the parameters of the optimized fuzzy logic method. This improved fuzzy rule based energy management method was used, and simulation results demonstrated that this method improved the fuel economy of the fuzzy rule method about 2.9%.

articleTitle: Impact and Analysis of Electric Vehicle Charging and Discharging on Distribution Network Power Quality Based on Synchronized Waveform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This study utilizes a synchronous waveform measuring instrument to investigate the impact of electric vehicle-to-grid (V2G) charging and discharging processes on distribution network power quality. Data collection and analysis were conducted on various parameters, including different charging power levels, discharging power levels, discharging duration, and the effects of charging and discharging transitions on distribution network voltage deviation, three-phase imbalance, frequency deviation, and voltage-current harmonic distortion. Through summarizing and analyzing the data, the study identifies the impact patterns of electric vehicle charging and discharging processes on distribution network power quality, providing effective support for optimizing power quality in areas where electric vehicles charge and discharge.

articleTitle: Detection of Moisture Content of Silicon Oil in High Voltage Cable Terminal based on Terahertz Time-Domain Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The water content detection of cable silicone oil is an important means to study the insulation status of the oil-filled terminals of high-voltage cables, and the insulating property of silicone oil decreases dramatically when the water content is too high, which in turn affects the normal operation of cables. In order to realize a fast and non-destructive detection method, this paper adopts terahertz time-domain spectroscopy, combined with the designed sample cell, to detect the silicone oil samples prepared under different humidity environments, and obtain the parameters of refractive index and absorption coefficient, and further analyze the dielectric properties of the silicone oil under different water contents. The experimental results show that water molecules have strong absorption of terahertz waves, which can effectively realize the detection and analysis of the water content of silicone oil. Through the terahertz technology can be rapid and nondestructive detection of the micro-water content of silicon oil, but this experiment is still in the initial stage, and the subsequent algorithm simulation can be added to achieve more accurate and efficient quantitative analysis of the micro-water content of silicon oil.

articleTitle: A Service Anomaly Detection and Root Cause Location Method for Complex Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the changes in the architecture of new power systems and the increase in system scale, functions and complexity, the difficulty of system operation and maintenance has increased significantly. This paper proposes an anomaly detection and root cause location method. By detecting anomalies in the total time-consuming of a business call and the time-consuming of key services, the fault time and fault service can be detected. Then use the root cause location algorithm to analyze the monitoring metrics of the server where the fault service is located, and locate metrics related to the cause of the fault. The effectiveness of the method was verified on dispatching and control systems in East and Northwest China.

articleTitle: Operational Risk Evaluation of Electricity Spot Market with High-Penetration Renewable Energy Using Sensitivity Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The establishment of the electricity spot market is a key aspect of the new round of electricity sector reforms in China. However, the operational situation of the electricity spot market is complex and ever-changing, making it very crucial to analyze the operational risks of electricity spot market and its influencing factors. This paper first establishes a spot market clearing model based on the security-constrained unit commitment optimization model and security-constrained economic dispatch optimization model. Then, this paper introduces operational risk indicators of the electricity market, such as the load-side average price. Using the case study of a power grid, this paper quantitatively studies the relationship between various influencing factors and operational risks of the electricity market based on sensitivity analysis. This paper provides a basis for decision-making by market operators and participants.

articleTitle: Short Term Multi Energy Load Forecasting for High Energy-Consuming Industrial Load Based on CNN-GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Industrial loads show strong randomness and volatility in shorter time scales, which brings challenges for power grid operation. In order to accurately forecast short-term industrial load with multi-energy coupling, a load forecasting method based on the CNN (Convolutional Neural Network)-GRU (Gated Recurrent Unit) hybrid neural network is proposed. The method is designed to address the specific challenges posed by typical high energy-consuming industrial processes with multiple energy loads. Firstly, a load feature set is classified and constructed based on the coupled energy sources. Secondly, various types of load information are extracted, taking into account production plans. CNN is employed to integrate various load characteristics within the same temporal context in a high-dimensional space, thereby forming a high-dimensional comprehensive load feature that incorporates the temporal sequence of each process load. This is subsequently input into the GRU, which ultimately generates the prediction result. A case study of a large domestic steel enterprise demonstrates that the proposed method has a mean forecasting accuracy of 93.00% and 95.07% for the steel rolling and the electric arc furnace, respectively. This verifies the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: A Pulse Power Compensation Strategy for More Electric Aircraft
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) grid in more electric aircraft (MEA), pulse power from electromechanical actuator (EMA) results in significant voltage drop at the DC bus, posing a challenge to the system stability. This paper proposes a pulse power compensation strategy (PPCS) to mitigate the voltage drop caused by EMA. In a application scenario of PPCS, a permanent magnetic synchronous generator (PMSG) and a permanent magnetic synchronous motor (PMSM) are linked to bus via converter, respectively. Additionally, a battery energy storage system (BESS) using PPCS is linked to bus via a bi-directional DC-DC converter, providing pulse power to mitigate the voltage drop. The relevant modeling and system validation have been carried out in simulation.

articleTitle: Fault Line Selection Based on Feature Fusion and Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Phase-to-ground faults are the most common in indirectly grounding power system. In order to protect the line and maintain the stability of power supply, it is very important to respond quickly after fault. In this paper, the zero-sequence current of single-phase-to-ground fault is analyzed and decomposed by CEEMDAN. The transient energy of modal components is calculated and the standard deviation of effective components is calculated by correlation analysis. Finally, The K-means clustering algorithm was used to classify the errors. Tests have shown that the algorithm can accurately select fault paths by considering external conditions such as fault starting phase angle, transient impedance, and fault location.

articleTitle: A Strategic Bidding Framework for Renewable Energy Providers Considering Renewable Energy Output Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Renewable energy provides a powerful tool for handling the climate problem. However, the uncertainty of renewable energy resources restricts their bidding strategies. To improve renewable energy providers’ profits and enable the sustainable renewable energy development, it is necessary to consider renewable energy resources’ uncertainty during strategic bidding process. This paper proposes a strategic bidding framework to solve this problem. A K-means-based scene set generation method is utilized to model the potential market environment of the day-ahead and real-time market. The scene set is used as the parameters of a stochastic optimization programming to maximize renewable energy providers’ profits in different scenes. Simulation results based on real market data from the Midcontinent Independent System Operator prove the practicality of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Operation Reserve Usage Cost Allocation Method Based on Prediction Deviation Influence Degree
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to accurately evaluate the difference of the influence of different factors on the operation reserve utilization, and reasonably apportion the operation reserve utilization cost generated by the operation of power grid, this paper proposed an operation reserve utilization cost allocation method based on the influence degree of prediction deviation. The ideal operation scheme will be constructed to eliminate the influence of a certain influencing factor on the power grid operation by adopting the control variable method. The predicted deviation influence degree is defined as the ratio of the expected operational reserve usage cost to the actual operational reserve usage cost under the ideal operation scheme. This index can measure the degree of influence of different influencing factors on the actual operation reserve usage cost. Different influencing factors correspond to market entities that will share the cost of operation reserve use, based on their predicted deviation influence index value. Finally, a numerical example based on the actual data of a provincial power grid was constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The example results show that, compared with the traditional evaluation method, the operating reserve usage cost shared by market members is directly related to the impact degree of forecast deviation, but not directly related to the degree of forecast deviation.

articleTitle: A Capacity Allocation Method for Integrated Energy Systems in Desert Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Desert regions are rich in wind and solar resources, but improper development can result in substantial resource wastage. To ensure effective utilization of these resources, this paper proposes an integrated energy system (IES) combining wind energy, solar energy, and a hydrogen production-storage-power generation system. Initially, an optimization model and a cost model are developed to maximize the overall revenue of the IES. The particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is then employed to optimize the capacity allocation within the IES. Finally, simulations validate the proposed method. The results indicate that this system can fulfil the power demands of the specified area, reduce wind and solar energy curtailment, and achieve efficient resource utilization.

articleTitle: Research on Park-level Optimal Operation Strategy Based on Multi-energy Coupling and Reputation Value-driven Inter-park Transaction Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: At present, the park operation optimisation mechanism is still immature, and the utilisation rates of distributed energy equipments are low. At the same time, the power trading suffers from the problems of strong individual tendency and uncertainty in the output of units. Therefore, their economy and users' participation are seriously affected. To this end, firstly, an optimal operation strategy based on the multi-energy coupling at the park level is presented to improve the economic efficiency of the park; secondly, a mechanism for distributed power transaction based on reputation value is developed, which improves the motivation of users to participate in the market and enhance their autonomy while taking into account the economic efficiency of all entities. Finally, the feasibility and reasonableness of the proposed integrated energy operation mechanism of the park are verified using the simulations.

articleTitle: Damping Control for Drivetrain Torsional Vibration Attenuation of Grid Forming Wind Turbines with DFIG
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Research on grid-forming (GFM) control strategies for wind turbines (WTs) has primarily focused on the electromagnetic characteristics of the WTs, overlooking the impact on the drivetrain. This limitation has hindered the application of GFM control strategies in engineering. To fill this gap, a two-mass drivetrain model is built to assess the influence of the bandwidth of the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control strategy on drivetrain torsional vibration characteristics. A comparison of torsional vibration characteristics between the GFM-WT and traditional grid-following WT (GFL-WT) highlights the need for increased attention to drivetrain torsional vibration in GFM-WT. Then, the inadequacy of the traditional drivetrain torsional vibration suppression strategy (T-DTVSS) when applied in VSG control is examined. Finally, a novel drivetrain torsional vibration suppression strategy named virtual synchronous phase angle compensation drivetrain torsional vibration suppression strategy (VSPAC-DTVSS) is proposed, and the efficacy of this strategy is validated through simulation using PSCAD.

articleTitle: Research on Flux-Weakening Control Strategy of IPMSM Based on Improved Fuzzy PI
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to maximize the efficiency of IPMSM, a control method combining maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control and weak magnetic control is usually used. The traditional PI controller parameters are fixed and cannot cope with changing real-world conditions. By combining the fuzzy control theory with a PI controller, it is possible to change the PI parameters in real time, but the performance of the traditional fuzzy PI controller is still poor in the region where the error is small. In this paper, a fuzzy PI controller is used in the velocity loop, and the traditional fuzzy PI controller is improved to realize better control effect by changing the fuzzy rules and the affiliation function in the region of small error and error change rate. Finally, its effectiveness is verified in MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform.

articleTitle: An Improved Adaptive Control Strategy of Virtual Synchronous Generator for Effectively Utilizing Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) control can replicate the damping and inertia characteristics of traditional synchronous generators. Nevertheless, in distributed generation systems, sudden changes in grid conditions can lead to overshoot and oscillation in the system's output power and frequency. This paper first investigates the impact of varying inertia on the active power control loop of VSG. Subsequently, it analyzes the energy storage requirements under different damping states. Building on these insights, an inertia-adaptive variable damping ratio control strategy is proposed, leveraging adaptive control theory to optimize the energy storage unit while maintaining robust dynamic performance. Additionally, an advanced phase-locked loop-based pre-synchronization algorithm is introduced, ensuring a seamless transition from off-grid to grid-connected operation. The proposed control strategy is modeled and validated through simulations conducted in MATLAB/Simulink. Furthermore, a comparative analysis with existing adaptive control methods reveals that the new control strategy demands lower energy storage output and achieves smaller oscillations.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning-based Real-time Online Energy Management Strategy for Electric Vehicle Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the current "dual-carbon" environment, the transform of transportation electrification has become an important way in the pursuit of the "dual-carbon" target, but the uncertainty of the arrival time and charging demand of electric vehicles (EV) has brought great challenges to the design of charging schemes for charging stations (CSs). To maximize the EV users’ charging demand, the paper proposes a real-time online energy management strategy for CSs based on Deep-Reinforcement-Learning (DRL). First, the control process for EV charging is a Markov decision process, and the Multi-Attention-Actor-Critic (MAAC) algorithm with concentrated training based on a decentralized execution framework is established using the CS as an intelligent. Then, an energy management strategy is proposed to maximize the profit of the CS. Finally, the real-time online energy management results of CSs based on DRL are analyzed. The results show that the strategy proposed in this paper can effectively improve the profit of CSs under the assumption of meeting the charging needs of EV users.

articleTitle: A Compact Interline Power Flow Controller for Power Sharing in DC Microgrids Cluster
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Multiple DC MGs in the vicinity can be linked together to form a DC MGs cluster. Faced with different load conditions, the realization of global power sharing (GPS) in DC microgrid cluster is beneficial to improve equipment utilization and efficiency. The potential of efficient and compact devices to achieve this control objective has not yet been fully investigated. In this paper, a novel power electronic device, DC power flow controller (DCPFC) for a DC MGs cluster with its power management strategy is presented. The system is analyzed through steady-state analysis. Simulations conducted under different operating cases verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Compensation Methods of Time Delay Caused by Hardware Sampling and Stability Analysis for LCL-Type Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: LCL-type grid-tied inverters are widely used in renewable power generation systems and battery energy conversion systems. The output inductor current of the inverter is captured by hardware sampling filtering circuits, which will cause attenuation and phase shift to the signal. Meanwhile, the time delay effect of digital control will reduce the bandwidth of the current controller and weaken the stability of the control system, leading to high-frequency resonance of the LCL filter. Therefore, the resonant frequency of the LCL filter should be designed in the stable region and proper current control strategy must be adopted. This article analyzes the impact of the cutoff frequency of the hardware sampling circuits on the stability of single current loop controlled LCL inverters, as well as considering the delay effect of digital control. It is shown that the stable region of the current control loop narrows down because of low cutoff frequency of hardware filters. Furthermore, three methods are proposed to compensate for phase lag effects, including phase lead network, unit delay feedback, and all pass filter. The system stability using different compensation is analyzed by the root locus analysis in z-plane. Finally, the designing process of the compensator parameters is provided and the validity of the proposed method are verified through simulation.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Base-based Pre Debugging System Level Simulation Joint Debugging System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The secondary system of intelligent substations is complex, with various secondary equipment from different equipment manufacturers. Before conducting on-site debugging, it is necessary to conduct joint debugging at the joint debugging base to ensure that the circuit functions between equipment can be achieved normally and reduce the workload of on-site debugging. Conventional joint debugging is carried out through manual division of labor, which has problems such as single testing equipment, scattered debugging strategies, and long debugging processes, resulting in low efficiency and quality of joint debugging work. The equipment also needs to undergo repeated testing on site, which cannot achieve the expected goals of joint debugging. Research a base based pre debugging system level joint debugging system, which mainly includes a main control module, an expandable interface module, a multi power source module, a hardware testing platform based on interface centralization, and a software testing platform with strategy configurable. Implement a modeling description of the system level joint debugging strategy, and implement system level joint debugging based on a complete hardware platform interface. By applying a base based pre debugging system level joint debugging system for base based joint debugging, it can effectively improve debugging efficiency, reduce manual debugging processes, and reduce on-site repeated testing.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Station Area Distributed Energy Resources Aggregation Method Based on Virtual Battery
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low utilization rate of distributed energy resources and difficulty in absorbing renewable energy sources in the massive, small capacity and dispersed low voltage station area, this paper proposes a method of distributed energy resources aggregation in low voltage station area based on virtual battery. In the method, a Virtual Battery model is first introduced to characterize the adjustable capacity resources in low voltage station area, and a low voltage virtual battery (LVVB) model is constructed considering the operating characteristics of distributed energy resources, network topology and the penalty cost of renewable energy sources abandonment. Finally, the simulation results are verified by using 21 node system in four low voltage station areas. The consequence Indicated that the mentioned method can availably enhance efficient utilization of resources in low voltage station area, and offer aggregation support for the coordination of multiple station area in the optimal dispatching of multi-voltage level distribution systems.

articleTitle: Frequency Stability Emergency Control Method for High Proportional New Energy Power Systems Based on Improved SFR Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the increase of new energy penetration rate and the growth of DC transmission capacity, the frequency characteristics of the power system have decreased, thus existing frequency control measures may not be able to match the original fault types effectively. To solve this problem, an effective method to control frequency stability is proposed in this paper. First, the new energy generation and DC input-and-output links are added to the traditional System Frequency Response (SFR) model, which can obtain an improved SFR (ISFR) model. The relationship between key dynamic frequency indicators and the proportion of new energy is evaluated, deriving the analytical expression of the lowest point frequency change. Then, a frequency stability emergency control method constrained by the frequency deviation safety threshold is proposed to avoid disorderly disconnection of new energy sources. Finally, an experiment using an actual power grid is conducted. The predicted frequency values are calculated, and emergency control measures are taken. The experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Flux Observer for PMSM Sensorless Control based on DSOGI-FLL
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The rotor position of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) is observed using the flux observer, and the low pass filter (LPF) is usually used instead of a purely integrative link to eliminate the initial value error, but the LPF introduces additional amplitude and phase errors. The second order generalized integrator with frequency locked loop (SOGI-FLL) based on PMSM estimation method has excellent steady state performance, but there is 2nd frequency interference in FLL frequency estimation. On this basis, the double second order generalized integrator with frequency locked loop (DSOGI-FLL) method is proposed, which dynamically eliminates the 2nd frequency fluctuations and responds quickly to the angular frequency changes of the system. The effectiveness method is confirmed by establishing a simulation model of the permanent magnet synchronous motor and performing theoretical analysis and simulation verification.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Dispatch of Energy Router Considering the Efficiency of Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As a large-scale, integrated multi-energy network characterized by the prominence of multi-energy microgrids (MG) becomes a major trend in the development of power systems, the energy router (ER) gradually becomes the core component of multi-energy interconnection. In this paper, AC/DC hybrid MG based on magnetically coupled ER are studied, and the operation models of photovoltaic, wind turbine, flexible load and energy storage devices are considered. A multi-objective optimal dispatch model based on ER is established, with operating cost and operating efficiency as optimization objective functions, and an improved non-inferior classification genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) is employed. Through the simulation calculation in different cases, compared with the traditional dispatch scheme, the microgrid scheduling scheme based on ER can reduce the operating cost of MG and also improve its stability on the condition of greatly improving the consumption capacity of renewable energy.

articleTitle: Improving Load Forecasting Accuracy through Data Augmentation and TCNs-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The need for electricity has increased as a result of societal development and industrial transformation. Regularly accurate short-term electricity Forecasting is crucial to maintaining the security, effectiveness, and economy of the power grid. However, conventional forecasting models find it difficult to achieve the load forecast accuracy needed by the current power system because of the volatility and unpredictability of electricity load time series. We suggest a brand-new hybrid load forecasting model with two modules in order to accomplish this. The first is a data augmentation module that, when only load data are used, integrates peak and trend data as auxiliary data into the data from the denoised time series to produce extremely accurate forecasting results. The deep learning module comes in second. In order to improve load accuracy, we have proposed a new deep learning predictive module that combines the Transformer architecture with multi-layer Temporal Convolutional Networks (TCN). Using three load forecasting datasets from Australia, we ran experiments. The findings demonstrate that, when compared to the classical model, our designed framework achieves the highest accuracy in a number of indicators.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Site Selection Method to Enhance System Voltage Support Strength
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy sources, the system voltage support strength (hereinafter referred to as "system strength") gradually decreases, leading to an increased risk of system instability. In order to improve the stability of the system, energy storage systems (ESSs) based on grid-following (GFL) converters have been widely integrated. However, it is still unclear how ESSs affect the system strength of heterogeneous systems integrated with heterogeneous converter-based-renewables (CBRs) (hereinafter referred to as "heterogeneous multi-CBR systems"), leading to a lack of effective optimization site selection methods of ESSs. This paper focuses on the ESS site selection method in the heterogeneous multi-CBR system. Firstly, based on the perturbation theory, we solved and obtained the equivalent single-converter subsystem, which can represent the system strength of the heterogeneous multi-CBR system containing ESSs. On this basis, we reveal the mechanism by which ESSs affect the heterogeneous system strength. Furthermore, an optimization site selection method of ESSs based on a sensitivity index is proposed to better enhance the heterogeneous system strength.

articleTitle: Outlet Dust Concentration Prediction of Electrostatic Precipitator Based on Deep Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Electrostatic precipitator is the main equipment for removing dust in coal-fired power plants, it removes dust by consuming electrical energy. Establishing an accurate prediction model for electrostatic precipitator can provide important scientific basis for reducing pollution and carbon emissions in coal-fired power plants, which is of great significance for achieving the dual-carbon target. This paper proposes a mechanism model, and the variable parameters are trained through Particle Swarm Optimization algorithm. Then a hybrid model is established based on long short-term memory network and Attention mechanism. The historical data of electrostatic precipitator in a 330MW unit are used for training and testing finally. The results show that the Relative Root Mean Squared Error of hybrid model on the training set and testing set are 0.5% and 3.99%, accurate outlet dust concentration prediction has been realized.

articleTitle: Innovative Voltage Regulation Strategy for DC-DC Boost Converters in DC Microgrids Feeding CPLs: Integrating Physics-Informed Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In this paper, a novel composite control strategy, characterized by diminished reliance on parameter calibration, is proposed through the integration of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) and backstepping methodology. By leveraging the synergy of physical constraints integrated into neural network training and the robust design principles of backstepping, this control framework excels in achieving accurate voltage-tracking capabilities. The integration of these techniques augments the transient responses of output voltages across nominal operating conditions, as well as in the presence of reference voltage fluctuations and variable loads. The stability of the system with the proposed control strategy is guaranteed by constructing Lyapunov function and feedback control rate. Additionally, simulations are performed in MATLAB/Simulink software, and the results demonstrate the feasibility and excellence of the control methodology.

articleTitle: Study of the Impact of Large-capacity Compressor Start-up on Voltage Quality in Energy Storage Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The 300MW Compressed Air Energy Storage (CAES) power plant utilizes large-capacity motors to compress air, resulting in significant electrical load fluctuations during start-up. This can potentially lead to voltage deviations and compromise grid voltage quality. To ensure stable voltage operation and maintain grid voltage quality, this paper analyzes the impact of large-capacity compressor start-up on synchronous and asynchronous motor voltage levels during the start-up process. Corresponding countermeasures are proposed.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis for Smart Grids over Knowledge Graph and Abductive Reasoning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Smart grids require structured, precise fault diagnosis knowledge, as well as fast and intelligent fault reasoning methods. This paper proposes a novel fault diagnosis framework for power grids based on knowledge graphs and abductive reasoning. The knowledge graphs for fault diagnosis are first extracted from CIM/XML and IEC 61850/SCD files, containing information on system topology, protection logic, and protection configurations. Temporal constraints are incorporated into the knowledge graph, with graph queries utilized to manage the knowledge effectively. Additionally, an abductive reasoning method is introduced to infer faulted components across the knowledge graphs, involving three key steps: backward reasoning, forward reasoning, and evidence fusion. Finally, a test system featuring multiple faults and protection device malfunctions is examined to illustrate the method's efficacy.

articleTitle: Rearch on an Optimal Design of the Repetitive Controller Based on Series Active Power Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Repetitive controller can track periodic signals without error or suppress periodic disturbances, and have been widely used in many fields. However, the traditional repetitive controller has problems such as poor dynamic response performance and weak robustness. In this paper, a repetitive controller’s optimization design scheme is proposed for its weak robustness. By adding a low pass filter(LPF) as well as amplitude and phase compensation links to the traditional repetitive controller, the stability of the repetitive controller and the suppression of harmonics at non-resonant peak frequencies can be greatly improved, thus enhancing the stability of the system, which can be applied to the dividing frequency control of series active power filters(SAPF). In this paper, the correctness and feasibility of the proposed optimization scheme are experimentally verified.

articleTitle: Application of Protocol Conversion Technology in the Process of Fault Recording Information Collection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Currently, low-resistance grounding protection is used on over 3897 transmission lines within the supply district of Shi-nan Power Supply Company. In this instance, it is hard to locate the fault when the reclosing of protection acted successfully. To reduce the fault's scope, data recorded by a computerized protection device is needed to be transferred for fault analysis. It is necessary to use protocol conversion technology to convert the communication protocol in order to collect the fault recording files in the protection devices, though, because a large amount of imported protection devices use the self-customized communication protocols by the manufacturers, which differ from the protocols used by domestic protection devices. Nevertheless, the fault recording instruments are solely presented in power stations with voltage levels of 110kV and higher, thus failing to comprehensively cover all voltage levels in the near future. This paper presents the utilization of a general protocol analysis technology in developing an integrated analysis platform for various communication protocols. By analyzing and converting various protocol formats into COMTRADE format, the power supply company has the ability to gather fault recording files from all the protection devices independently.

articleTitle: Research on the Fuzzy Enhancement Algorithm for Infrared Images of Power Equipment Based on Membership Function
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The infrared thermal image diagnosis of power equipment represents one of the conventional equipment detection technologies. In order to reduce noise in infrared thermal images and improve their contrast, a fuzzy enhancement algorithm for infrared images is proposed in this paper based on the logistic membership function. First, bilateral filtering was performed on the infrared thermal images of the equipment first. Then, the fuzzy theory based on the logistic membership function was used to fuzzify the images. Subsequently, the resulting images in the fuzzy domain were enhanced and de-fuzzified to obtain an infrared thermal image with a noticeable enhancement effect. Experimental results show that the proposed algorithm outperforms conventional processing algorithms, such as the membership function, in terms of the completeness of preserved edge information and significantly improved contrast. Moreover, the proposed algorithm exhibits high execution efficiency and enables batch processing of infrared thermal images and fault diagnosis of power equipment.

articleTitle: Analysis of Receiving End Power Angle Stability in Hybrid AC/DC Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: the transient voltage stability within an integrated AC/DC power network can be significantly enhanced by escalating the quantity of operational localized generators. However, practical engineering experience has shown that a higher number of operating local generators can actually lead to faster voltage instability. This is because the units accelerate too quickly during faults, causing power angle instability which then triggers voltage instability. Thus, it is crucial to thoroughly investigate the power angle stability at the receiving end of power systems. This paper models and examines the power angle stability characteristics of the receiving end in a hybrid AC/DC power grid, taking into account the two-stage recovery characteristics of DC power and load after a fault. The equal area criterion is then applied to theoretically analyze the factors influencing the power angle stability at the grid's receiving end. Finally, a simplified single-machine case study is used to simulate and verify the theoretical analysis presented in this paper. The research findings can provide theoretical references for the dispatch and operation of actual power grids.

Author Keywords: power angle stability of the receiving end

articleTitle: A Repair Crew Dispatch for Urban Power Grid Under Extreme Weather Considering Social and Economic Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Different from conventional power system faults, the faults of urban power grid in extreme weather often have the characteristics of suddenness, and it is usually impossible to repair all fault lines at the same time. The purpose of this paper is to formulate a repair crew dispatch that takes into account economic and social factors to reduce the losses caused by grid faults in extreme weather. In this paper, AHP analytic hierarchy process is used to weight the social and economic factors. On this basis, the simulation technology is used to fully consider the factors such as energy storage and demand response. The repair crew dispatch strategy of urban power grid under extreme weather is studied, and the reliability of the method is proved by the example analysis of the solver. The results of the example analysis are in line with the theoretical expectations. When the weighting is within a certain reasonable range, the repair crew dispatch strategy proposed in the paper can help reduce the comprehensive loss of power grid faults in extreme weather.

articleTitle: Autonomous Energy Trading for Community-Based Local Energy Market
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Energy Communities (ECs) will play a crucial role in increasing the adoption of renewable energy. To enable efficient and cost-effective energy trading within the energy community framework, this paper proposes an autonomous energy trading platform for ECs to engage in the local energy market. The proposed two-layer market coordination mechanism consists of: 1) a local market coordinator, which will manage energy trading between energy communities and the wholesale electricity market to minimize costs and battery degradation; and 2) an energy community coordinator, which will facilitate autonomous energy trading within the local market by self-learning from historical data using Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL). The effectiveness of this framework is validated using real-world data from the UK energy market.

articleTitle: Application of Topological Modeling and Verification Analysis of Distribution Networks Based on Graph Databases
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In a continuous expanding power grid, the interaction between generation, transmission, distribution, and load has become the new normal. The distribution network relationship model based on traditional relational databases limits the query performance of distribution network data, posing serious challenges to query devices and their topological connections. This paper is based on the "node-edge" graph database model to describe the topology structure of the distribution network and improve query optimization. Furthermore, combining operational data such as distribution network segments, distribution transformer numbers, and segments carrying distribution transformers, the correlation coefficient analysis method is used to verify and analyze the user-substation, substation-substation, and substation-bus connection relationships in the distribution network. Case studies confirm that compared to traditional relational database, the efficiency of the graph database achieves a tenfold efficiency improvement.

articleTitle: Configuration and Operation Model for Integrated Energy Power Stations with Concentrated Solar Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources leads to large power output fluctuations, which brings challenges to the stable operation of the power grid. Considering the unique thermal storage technology of concentrated solar power (CSP) plants, the configuration of integrated energy power stations considering CSP has become a solution for integration of renewable energy. This paper first analyzes the technical features of CSP generation and establishes the energy flow model of wind-photovoltaic-CSP-storage integrated power station. Secondly, it analyzes the costs and benefits of the integrated power station, and establishes an optimization model for the configuration and operation of the station. Finally, an example simulation is set up with electricity market data from Northwest China, and the calculation results show that the integrated power station with a CSP plant outperforms that with an energy storage facility.

articleTitle: Optimization Configuration Method of Synchronous Condensers Considering the Short-Circuit Ratio and Transient Overvoltage of High Penetration Renewable Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The expansion of renewable energy generation is leading to an increased presence of renewable energy in the power system. However, high penetration renewable energy systems, because of the fluctuating and unpredictable nature of renewable energy production, usually face many problems. The issue of insufficient short-circuit ratio can lead to a decrease in the ability of renewable energy stations to resist disturbances, and transient overvoltage may damage equipment and affect the stability of the power system. To address the challenges in systems with a high penetration of renewable energy effectively, this paper introduces an optimization approach for the configuration of synchronous condensers. This configuration method takes into account the operational stability of the renewable energy system and the cost-effectiveness of configuration. By optimizing the capacity of synchronous condensers, it improves the short-circuit ratio and transient overvoltage suppression ability of the renewable energy power system, enhancing voltage stability and disturbance resistance. Firstly, analyzing the causes of insufficient short-circuit ratio and transient overvoltage and their impact on the power system, which provide a theoretical basis for the configuration of synchronous condensers. Secondly, considering the dynamic reactive characteristics of synchronous condensers, analyzing the principal variables affecting the short-circuit ratio and transient overvoltage. Finally, the appropriateness of the configuration method was verified by simulation analysis. The study results that adjusting the configuration of synchronous condensers for renewable energy stations can overcome the deficiencies in short-circuit ratios and transient overvoltage, providing a trustworthy technical foundation for the configuration of synchronous condensers.

articleTitle: Research on Transient Performance of Non-Stop Ice Melting Method for Long-Distance Multi-Feeder Overhead Lines in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Nowadays, the research on ice melting technology primarily focuses on the thermal effect in the steady state process of ice melting, and there is a lack of research on the transient process of ice melting devices. To solve this problem, we takes the online ice melting technology befitting for distribution network as the research object, analyzes the transient performance of ice melting from its ice melting working principle, establishes a mathematical model of the excitation inrush current transient of the grounding transformer, and proposes an excitation inrush current suppression strategy for the grounding transformer. A branch line in the mountainous area of northern Guangdong is used as a pilot line, and the transient characteristics and the feasibility of the excitation inrush current strategy are verified according to the parameters of the icing line. The results show that during the switching period of the ice melting device, the overcurrent transient state will occur in the distribution network system, which bring serious challenges and threats to the security and stability of the system. The excitation inrush current suppression strategy can better suppress the transient overcurrent and ensure the safety of online ice melting method.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Transient Power Angle Characteristics of GFM-VSC Under Different Voltage Control and Current Limitation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Inner-loop control and current saturation strategy significantly shape the P-δ curve and affect the transient synchronization stability. This paper discusses two typical voltage control strategies, i.e., virtual admittance voltage control (VAVC) and dual-loop voltage control (DLVC), and considering two current limitation strategies, i.e., circular limiter and d-axis priority limiter. Transient power angle modeling of the GFM-VSC with those strategies is conducted. Two current-constrained power angle curves (CC-PAC) are drawn and analyzed. The characteristics of the curves are pointed out. Transient stability of the GFM-VSC is discussed using CC-PAC and with the help of the equal area criterion. Results are verified by simulation in MATLAB/SIMULINK.

articleTitle: Research on Single Phase to Ground Fault Line Selection Based on Convolutional Neural Network and Recurrence Plot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: When the convolutional neural network is used for line selection in resonant grounding systems, it not only requires much data sets to determine the parameters of the convolution filter, but also has high requirements on the computing performance of the hardware equipment. To solve the above problems, a single-phase ground fault line selection method based on the fusion of recurrence plot and convolutional neural network(RP-CNN) is proposed. Firstly, FIR filter is used to select the power frequency component of the zero sequence current of lines and generate a recurrence plot. After 90% of the data points in the recurrence plot are set to zero. Then the newly generated recurrence plot is used as the image data to train the model of convolutional neural networks. Finally, the trained model is used to find the fault line and verify the correctness of the lines selection. The simulation results show that because the input image matrix contains a large number of zero matrices, the convolutional neural network only needs a few epochs to complete the training, and it also reduces the requirements for the computational performance of hardware. Not only that, this method can solve the problem of intermittent arc ground fault difficulties, noise interference, and the impact of different data window sizes on the correctness of line selection.

articleTitle: Economic Dispatch Method with Chance Constraints for Power Systems Incorporating Pumped Storage, Wind Power Curtailment and Load Shedding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The paper presents an economic dispatch method with chance constraints for electricity systems, specifically tackling issues related to the unpredictable nature of wind energy generation. The primary goal of this proposed approach is to minimize wind curtailment and load shedding by taking into account the variability of wind power output and reserve shortages. By creating dispatch plans that incorporate pumped storage, the system can operate economically while reducing wind curtailment. Furthermore, a method for reconstructing chance constraints is introduced using conditional and overall risk values, along with dual theory. This approach transforms a bilinear problem into a mixed integer linear programming problem by employing a piecewise linear strategy. Numerical experiments confirm the practicality and efficiency of this method.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of DFIG System Considering Dual-Port Grid-Connected Characteristics During Grid Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With more and more wind energy resources penetrating into the grid, transient stability of wind power systems during grid faults has been widely studied. Existing research typically treats wind power systems as controlled current sources oriented by a phase-locked loop (PLL) and employs a simplified second-order transient synchronization model for analysis. However, this model inadequately represents the transient instability mechanisms of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) systems due to their dual-port grid-connected characteristics. To fill this gap, this article establishes a fourth-order transient synchronization model that accounts for the dual-port grid-connected characteristics. Then, the coupling effect between the two PLLs of the rotor-side converter and the grid-side converter is analyzed using phase portrait methods. Moreover, the influential regularity of the bandwidth and damping ratio of the dual PLL on transient stability is revealed, indicating that the parameters of rotor-side converter’s PLL play a dominant role. Finally, simulations are conducted to validate the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Evaluation on Renewable Energy Accommodation Capability Based on Robust Optimization in Electricity Market
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The proposal of carbon emission reduction strategy makes the operation mode of power system cleaner. The renewable energy (RE) such as wind power and photovoltaics have attracted people's attention due to their clean and low-carbon characteristics. With the promotion of power market reform, renewable energy power generation has different abandonment situations due to different market rules. Therefore, it is of great significance to evaluate the renewable energy accommodation (REA) capability in the market environment. In this paper, the budget uncertainty set of RE output is constructed based on robust optimization. A REA evaluation model is established considering the uncertainty of renewable energy, and it is transformed and solved based on dual theory and McCormick envelope. The example analysis shows that the uncertainty of renewable energy, climbing ability and line safety constraints affect the renewable energy accommodation capability.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch of Integrated Electricity and Heat Systems Considering Hydrogen Mixed Gas Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Compared to traditional energy sources, hydrogen energy has the benefit of being highly efficient, flexible and low in carbon dioxide. To fulfil the requirements of the green low-carbon energy system, the hydrogen mixed gas turbine (HMGT) as a new unit species, provides a significant way to couple the hydrogen energy with the electric energy and heating. This paper focuses on the study of an optimal scheduling strategy for an electro-thermal integrated system with HMGT. The water electrolysis technology and the hydrogen storage tank (HST) supply the hydrogen energy to the HMGT. This paper proposes a combined heat and power (CHP) model of the HMGT. And the validity and feasibility of the model and scheduling method are verified by the test system. We discuss the effect of hydrogen mixing ratio on total cost and wind curtailment under different renewable energy penetration levels. It is concluded that in cooperation with the water electrolysis technology for the hydrogen production, the HMGT can reduce economic costs and better consumes wind power (WP) in the integrated energy system (IES).

articleTitle: Research on Collaborative Phase Testing Method for Gas Steam Combined Cycle Generator Set under Expanded Unit Connection Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the development of new power systems, the demand for reactive power regulation capability of traditional generator sets is becoming higher and higher. The phase leading test of generator sets is the basis for power grid dispatch agencies to regulate the voltage of the power system. However, for gas steam combined cycle units with expanded unit connection methods, the test results of traditional phase leading test methods are significantly different from the actual reactive power regulation capability in operation. Based on the study of voltage operation data of this type of generator set, this article points out the reasons for the poor reactive power regulation capability, and proposes a phase leading depth test method for gas steam combined cycle units under expanded unit connection methods, including adjustment coefficient setting and multi machine coordinated phase leading, based on the reactive power regulation characteristics of gas steam combined cycle units under expanded unit connection methods. And testing and operational performance analysis were conducted on actual units. Practice has shown that the testing method proposed in this article can more accurately measure the depth of unit phase advancement, providing more accurate guidance for reactive power regulation of units.

articleTitle: A High-precision Dynamic Synchrophasor Measurement Method and Error Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This article addresses the issue of insufficient accuracy in DFT class synchrophasor measurement algorithms under dynamic conditions, and analyzes the error mechanism and correction methods. According to definition of synchrophasor measurement, a new synchrophasor measurement algorithm basing on a frequency shifted and multi band low-pass filter framework is proposed. The dynamic modulation error tests specified in the standard and compared with the synchrophasor measured by the on-site PMU device show that under dynamic conditions, the frequency and ROCOF measurement accuracy is improved by 1-2 orders of magnitude compared to the standard requirements. The algorithm proposed in this paper has higher availability in on-site data error verification and grid connection control.

articleTitle: Cooperative Operation of Multi-Operator Hybrid Pumped Storage Cascade Hydropower Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The phenomenon of upstream and downstream hydropower plants in the same river belonging to operators is widespread. When hydraulically connected cascade hydropower (CH) plants develop scheduling plans independently on behalf of their respective operators, it will lead to the decline of the total benefit. A multi-scenario stochastic optimization (MSSO) model for multi-operator hybrid pumped storage cascade hydropower (HPSCH) plants is proposed in this paper, considering the hydraulic coupling of hydropower plants and typical scenarios of electricity prices. The maximum of the total alliance benefit of the HPSCH plants is taken as objective function. The power output of HPSCH plants is adjusted to improve the total alliance benefit. In order to establish a reasonable distribution mechanism, Shapley value is adopted for the distribution of cooperative benefit obtained by the multi-operator HPSCH alliance. The feasibility of the model is verified through example simulation.

articleTitle: Optimization of ACs Cluster Operation Considering Command Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of dual-carbon policy, countries around the world to new energy transition progress accelerated, the traditional power system gradually to a high proportion of renewable energy of the new power system began to change, however, due to the new energy fluctuation and uncertainty, the power grid urgently need to tap the load-side resources to regulate the flexibility. Air conditioning as a typical representative of flexible loads, with a large number, total volume, overall regulation and control difficulties, in order to achieve air conditioning clusters to participate in the optimal scheduling of the power grid, this paper adopts the virtual energy storage model to realize the resources of the air conditioning and to realize the de-aggregation of the control instructions through the consistency of the control decomposition method. Firstly, the virtual energy storage model of air conditioner monolith is constructed to obtain the state transfer process of room temperature state and air conditioner power regulation amount; then, the aggregation and dimensionality reduction process of air conditioner cluster is realized in combination with the consistency control algorithm and the de-aggregation of control methods to realize the optimized operation and instruction decomposition; secondly, the optimized operation method of air conditioner-type virtual power plant is constructed with the lowest energy cost as the objective function; finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the arithmetic example. effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Stacked revenues of pumped hydro storage cooperation with batteries in the energy and regulation reserve market
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As the most extensively installed technology, Pumped Hydro Storage (PHS) is crucial in securing the reliability of the power system. However, most of the installed capacity globally is heavily regulated by power system operators or the grid company. The regulated operating environment poses a dilemma for PHS in retrieving its initial investments. The potential of PHS entering the energy and ancillary service market is studied in this paper. The ancillary services encompass a spectrum of vital functions, including Frequency Containment Reserve (FCR), automatic Frequency Restoration Reserve (aFRR), manual Frequency Restoration Reserve (mFRR), and Replacement Reserves (RR). Further, the cooperation of PHS and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), referred to as Hybrid Energy Storage Systems (HESS), is studied to tap the regulation potential of PHS further. Providing various reserve services increases HESS's profit by 27%, exhibiting HESS's potential to support the power system across various time sectors. The cooperation of BESS significantly improves PHS's regulation capability. With a capacity equivalent to 10% of PHS’s capacity, BESS can enhance the regulation profit by 100%, leading to a 30% increase in sum profits. Based on the evaluation outcome, further political suggestions are given for the long-term development of PHS.

articleTitle: Grid-forming Control of VSC-HVDC Systems Connecting Asynchronous Power Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Interconnecting asynchronous power grids with the VSC-HVDC transmission is an important trend. To enhance the weak grid operation performance and grid frequency response capability of the VSC-HVDC system, a novel grid-forming without using the phase-locked-loop is applied in both ends of the VSC-HVDC system. The DC voltage-Active power droop-based grid-synchronization method is utilized. With the proposed method, the sending and the receiving end MMCs perform like a synchronous motor and a synchronous generator, respectively. When the frequency changes in either grid, the system can automatically response to it and change the active power transmission by VSC-HVDC to achieve primary frequency regulation and active frequency support. Finally, the validity of the dual-end grid-forming control is verified based on the simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC.

articleTitle: Microgrid Low-Carbon Economic Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the rapid growth and application of renewable energy generation, microgrids have garnered widespread attention as flexible and sustainable forms of power systems. However, the intermittency and volatility of renewable energy pose challenges to microgrid operations, particularly in ensuring stability and economic efficiency of energy supply. Concurrently, the escalating threat of global climate change underscores the urgent need to reduce carbon emissions, presenting both challenges and opportunities for microgrid economic scheduling.This paper proposes a comprehensive scheduling model integrating carbon trading mechanisms to address carbon emission management in microgrid economic scheduling. Leveraging theories of power system economic dispatch, the model optimally integrates and schedules various energy resources within the microgrid to maximize energy utilization and economic efficiency. Additionally, by incorporating carbon trading mechanisms, including emission quotas and prices, the model effectively controls carbon emissions within the microgrid while ensuring reliable power supply.This model not only considers the characteristics of various energy sources and supply-demand balance within the microgrid but also addresses practical needs and economic benefits of carbon emission management. Through case studies, the model's validity and feasibility are verified, offering novel insights and methods for microgrid economic scheduling.

articleTitle: Multi-Agents Integrated Energy Systems Optimal Scheduling Considering Carbon Allowance and Green Certificate Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Policy-based quota market shows a high potential in de-carbonization in integrated energy system (IES) operation. This paper proposes an optimal scheduling method for multi-agents integrated energy systems (MIES) considering the interaction of carbon allowance and green certificate. Firstly, a MIES interaction model is established while considering system constraints. Then, a Nash bargaining theory based optimal model is proposed to minimize the MIES operation cost, and been transformed into two subproblems. Additionally, a comprehensive contribute indicator is introduced to promote the fairness of profit distribution. Simulation results verify the feasibility and economy of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Peruvian Territorial Spaces for the Creation of Wind Power Plants According to the AHP Matrix Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The paper presents an analysis of the evaluation of territorial spaces in the province of Junín, Peru, for the implementation of wind power plants using the AHP (Analytical Hierarchical Process) matrix analysis method. Several evaluation criteria are used, such as average wind speed, altitude, roughness length, slope, administrative boundaries, urban areas, power lines and substations, hydrographic units, and environmental and archaeological zones. The results obtained show the percentage weightings for each province of Junín in relation to the different evaluation criteria. According to the AHP analysis, it is determined that the most optimal province for the implementation of a wind farm in Junín is the province of Yauli, followed closely by the province of Chupaca. These provinces meet the selection criteria and present similarities with current wind farm locations.

articleTitle: User Demand Response Modeling and Load-side Resource Collaborative Dispatching Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the proliferations of load-side resources in load-side, such as distributed generator, distributed energy storages and flexible loads, the collaborative dispatching problem for them has been a thorny issue. A collaborative dispatching model for the distribution network, the distributed PV (photovoltaic), distributed energy storage, and flexible load is proposed to manage the distributed resources effectively. The optimal collaborative dispatching model is formulated from the perspective of social welfare with considering the power flow constraints, which can minimize the operation cost and maintain the operation security. Case studies are performed on the improved IEEE-33 bus distribution system and the collaborative dispatching results show that the proposed collaborative dispatching method can coordinate the operations efficiently of distributed resources and reduce the operation cost significantly.

articleTitle: Air Conditioning Load Control Strategy for Substation Considering Demand Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As new power system is built, a large proportion of fluctuating new energy sources are connected, which makes the scheduling and control capabilities of the power system tested. To ensure the flexibility of the power system, it is crucial to fully excavate the demand-side adjustable resources. As an important part of residential loads in the substation, air conditioning (AC) loads have the potential to participate in demand response (DR). How to accurately assess the dispatchable potential of AC loads has become particularly important and urgent. Therefore, the impact of different customers' air conditioning responses on the assessment of the adjustable potential is considered, and a model of AC is established based on the thermodynamic equivalent thermal parameters (ETP) model to assess the adjustable potential of aggregated AC loads by changing the temperature settings. Then, an operation control strategy for AC load control is designed in view of the customers' willingness to participate in the response. The results verify the accuracy of the proposed method to assess the adjustable power of AC loads and the feasibility of aggregated AC loads to participate in system regulation.

articleTitle: A Co-optimization Method for Energy Storage Participating Day-Ahead Energy and Reserve Market
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Recently, the participation of energy storage in domestic and international electricity market transactions has gradually increased. Energy storage has a very good system support role in the reserve market. With the development of batteries and control technology, the installed capacity of electrochemical energy storage has been continuously increasing both domestically and internationally in recent years. Furthermore, many domestic and foreign electricity markets have allowed energy storage to participate in electricity market transactions. On the basis of considering the output characteristics of energy storage system (ESS), a collaborative optimization mechanism considering the participation of ESS in the reserve market have been proposed. It provides the feasibility of market mechanisms for a wider range of energy storage resources to participate in the reserve market, and analyzes the role of energy storage when there is a system congestion. It constructed a multi regional power system and verified the correctness of the proposed scheduling model. In addition, the case analysis verifies the capacity supporting effect of ESS in multi-area grid congestion scenarios.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization Design of Tubular Permanent Magnet Linear Motor Based on Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To improve the driving performance of the motor, increase the average thrust while reducing thrust ripple, a 9-slot 8-pole tubular permanent magnet linear motor is used as the research object to optimize the design parameters. Firstly, several key parameters affecting the average thrust and thrust ripple of the motor were analyzed, and four significance parameters were selected from six main design parameters by combining Taguchi’s orthogonal experimental design and sensitivity analysis. The Box-Behnken experimental design was established to obtain the finite element analysis test scheme of four factors and three levels. Then, according to the response surface method, the fitting model between the optimized target response and the significant variables was established, and the fitting accuracy was evaluated. Finally, multi-objective optimization based on this model. The finite element analysis results indicate that the multi-objective optimization design of the tubular permanent magnet linear motor based on the Taguchi method increases the average thrust after optimization, and the thrust ripple is greatly reduced.

articleTitle: Stability Improvement for Grid-Following Inverter by Virtual Damping Enhancement With Current Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Due to the lack of physical structural support, traditional grid-following (GFL) inverters are prone to grid voltage deviations and resonances. In weak grids, the interplay among multiple control circuits, such as phase-locked loops (PLLs) and current loops, can cause severe instability. To address these issues, this study constructs a model of sequence impedance for GFL inverters to evaluate the criteria for instability and proposes a compensation method for the current loop reference current. By introducing compensation into the reference current, the parallel operation of grid-forming (GFM) and GFL inverters is achieved, reducing the equivalent impedance on the grid side and enhancing the stability of the grid. Simulations confirm the effectiveness of the improved approach, indicating that the proposed strategy performs similarly to traditional control strategies in normal grids and maintains stability in weak grids affected by voltage variations.

articleTitle: A DenseNet Approach to Composite Power System Risk Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the data-driven power system risk assessment, , traditional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are hindered by the issue of vanishing gradients, which compromises their predictive accuracy.
