This paper proposes the integration of the Densely Connected Convolutional Network (DenseNet) into power system risk assessment to bolster the model's generalization capabilities. Additionally, a training data construction algorithm based on cross-entropy technique is presented to increase the proportion of effective samples in the training data. The case study shows that the proposed method can effectively improve the prediction accuracy of neural network model and the accuracy of risk assessment.

articleTitle: Research on Internal Temperature and Humidity Property for Environmental Monitoring Device of Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Low temperature and condensation are significant factors causing the decline in measurement performance of transmission line environmental monitoring devices. This study focuses on the establishing a finite element numerical simulation model to obtain the internal temperature and humidity distribution within the device under the condition of heater installation. The effects of heating on different positions are analyzed, and the corresponding relationship between temperature rise and relative humidity reduction is discussed, providing reference for the better installation of the heater. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that under heating conditions, the average temperature in the upper space of the device is higher than that in the lower space; a 10K increase in internal temperature corresponds to a 30%RH decrease in relative humidity, and condensation within the device can be effectively removed by the heater within 3h.

articleTitle: Research on the Impact of Large-scale Energy Storage System on the Operational Characteristics of Regional Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The increasing integration of new energy and uneven development of load demand may cause transmission pressure of new energy and insufficient power supply capacity for a regional power grid. The energy storage system provides a promising approach to solving those challenges. Thus, this paper studies how large-scale energy storage systems affect the operational characteristics of a regional power grid. Using a case study of a typical regional power grid, it seriously analyzes the changes brought by the energy storage system in short circuit current, power flow distribution, power supply capacity, new energy export, and transient stability. Numerical results validate the benefits brought by energy storage system A, especially in enhancing the power supply capacity of regional power grid A. Furthermore, the new energy absorption can also be promoted with energy storage assistance.

articleTitle: ANN-based Transient Synchronization Stability Monitoring Method for Grid-Following Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Loss of synchronization (LOS) of grid-following converters (GFC) under grid faults can lead to severe impacts on the operation of the rest of power systems. To cope with this issue, either the development of stabilization controls or the proper activation of relay protections is often considered. To better implement those methods, the capability of online monitoring the transient synchronization stability (TSS) of GFC is crucial. To this end, this article proposes an artificial neural network (ANN) based TSS monitoring method, which can be used for online TSS assessment thus laying the basis for control and protection actions. First, TSS model of the phase-locked loop (PLL) synchronized converter considering LVRT control is derived and the correlation between CCT and grid parameters is analyzed. Then the ANN-based critical clearing time (CCT) estimation is obtained by model-based training, resulting in the ANN based online TSS monitoring method of GFC. Finally, effectiveness of the method is verified by simulations in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Virtual Inertia Compensation Strategy for Variable Speed Pumped Storage Hydropower Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This study explores a virtual inertia compensation strategy for Variable Speed Pumped Storage (VSPS) Hydropower Units, focusing on enhancing grid stability amidst the integration of renewable energy sources. Utilizing a Doubly Fed Induction Machine (DFIM), the proposed method employs Virtual Synchronous Generator (VSG) for Rotor side converter controllers to improve the inertial response and frequency control. The research addresses the decoupling control challenge of DFIM, which traditionally hinders its ability to respond to grid frequency changes. Through simulations on the Matlab/Simulink platform, the effectiveness of the inertia compensation strategy is validated, demonstrating improved stability and efficiency in VSPS operations. This work underscores the significance of robust inertia control in maintaining grid stability and facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources into modern power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Analysis of New Energy Integration Based on Time Series Production Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The future power system is characterized by the widespread adoption and significant increase of new energy sources. Taking into account the overall economic performance of society, the relationship between investment in power grid and the high consumption rate of new energy shows discrepancies. A study is carried out on various factors like load through time-series production simulation. New energy, and the incorporation of energy storage at an individual power plant, to examine the optimal utilization rate of new energy transfer while keeping the total national economic cost at a minimum, and to investigate the equilibrium between the abandonment of new energy sources and the rising expenses of the entire system.The validity of such approach was confirmed by conducting calculations on various sizes of installed photovoltaic capacities, the extent of investments in the power grid, and the capacity configurations of energy storage systems. This innovative approach presents fresh perspectives on integrating a high proportion of new energy sources into the power grid, offering theoretical guidance for managing and operating power systems with significant new energy penetration in the future.

Author Keywords: the widespread adoption of alternative energy sources
maintaining a balanced rate of consumption
the management of renewable energy resources

articleTitle: Fault Repair Strategy of Distribution Network After Typhoon Disaster Considering Customer’s Discomfort
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: After typhoon disasters, coastal power distribution networks often encounter widespread physical failures. As high temperature weather often accompanies typhoon, it is essential to develop effective repairing strategies for reducing the discomfort of power consumers. However, traditional repairing strategies are determined based on the importance of loads, ignoring the intensification of discomfort during the prolonged outage event. This paper proposes a decision-making method for fault repair of distribution systems considering consumers’ discomfort after typhoon disasters. First, the discomfort index for different types of consumers is proposed to describe the impact of outage duration on consumers’ discomfort. Then, a distribution system repairing model with a novel objective function is proposed to minimize the consumers’ discomfort during outage. Repair crews are optimally dispatched for fast repair, and microgrids are dynamically formed to supply the loads. The effectiveness of the proposed method is validated using the IEEE 33-bus system.

articleTitle: Improved Pearson-K-means Load Classification Method Based on Dissimilarity Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the continuous development of the intelligent power system, a large number of measurement and control terminals have been installed in the system, generating massive amounts of terminal data. In particular, the power load data of users contains potential value, which can help enhance the efficiency and precision of power supply and guarantee the safe and steady operation of the power grid. Based on this, this paper presents an Improved Pearson-K-means Load Classification (IPKMLC) method based on a dissimilarity matrix for power user load data. First, to better measure the similarity of load curves, Pearson is used as the distance metric for K-means. Next, considering the impact of random cluster centers and cluster numbers in the K-means method, a dissimilarity matrix is introduced to simultaneously ascertain the initial cluster centers and cluster numbers for the clustering algorithm, thereby improving the precision and efficiency of the algorithm. Finally, a case study is conducted on 16 types of commercial load data from the Open Energy Information website of the Department of Energy, further validating the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on a Short term Power Prediction Method for Photovoltaic Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This article studies a short-term power prediction model for large-scale photovoltaic power generation, focusing on short-term prediction of photovoltaic power generation. In this article, the concept of virtual prediction is innovatively introduced, and external influencing factors are comprehensively considered to form a prediction model algorithm library. A new model for predicting electricity consumption based on time series dynamic adjustment algorithms and weight ratios is studied to achieve optimal prediction results. With the goal of minimizing errors, we select the most recent historical data for hypothesis prediction, screen the best models and parameters, and achieve accurate short-term power prediction for large-scale photovoltaic power generation; At the same time, photovoltaic power stations that can obtain complete meteorological data will be used as reference power stations to obtain historical meteorological data with the highest similarity to the current target meteorological parameters, and a similar day dataset will be constructed; Then, the kernel function extreme learning mechanism optimized by particle swarm optimization is used to build a benchmark photovoltaic power plant power prediction model, while comprehensively considering the factors affecting the purchased electricity quantity. Based on the diversity and complexity of the variation patterns of the predicted quantity, and taking into account the impact of historical electricity purchase data and economic, meteorological, holiday and other factors on the predicted quantity, the previous single factor prediction model has been changed. Finally, we will review the commonly used methods for current electricity forecasting models, including univariate linear regression, similarity extrapolation, holiday point-to-point, ratio smoothing, overlapping curves, and other forecasting methods. We will construct a single forecasting model for different types of customers and form an algorithm library for forecasting models to meet the forecasting needs of different types of users.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation Method of AC/DC Distribution System with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The traditional distribution network has gradually evolved into a sophisticated AC/DC distribution system with numerous power electronics components, control equipment, and distributed generation sources. Conducting a comprehensive evaluation of this system using advanced modeling, simulation techniques, and risk assessment theory is of paramount importance. Consequently, this paper establishes a comprehensive evaluation framework for AC/DC networks incorporating distributed generation. Initially, power flow and reliability models were developed to evaluate power quality levels and reliable power supply capabilities. Building upon these models, quantitative evaluation metrics for AC/DC systems were established, forming a layered evaluation index system comprising target, performance, and specific indicators. Furthermore, an integrated assessment approach utilizing fuzzy evaluation techniques was implemented to quantify the impact of distributed generation integration within AC/DC systems. The proposed evaluation model was tested and validated using the modified IEEE RBTS-6 main feeder F4 test case.

articleTitle: Effect of local overheating on the insulation performance of epoxy resin impregnated paper bushings
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To study the internal temperature distribution of epoxy resin impregnated paper (RIP) bushings under load current conditions and the impact of local overheating on the insulation performance of the bushings, a synchronous test circuit for bushing temperature rise and insulation performance was constructed. The study obtained the variation patterns of the bushing hot spot temperature and the corresponding insulation performance under different currents and simulated the process of local overheating fault in RIP bushings. Test results indicate that when the hottest spot temperature in the bushing is below 100℃, the relaxation polarization loss in the insulation medium is evident. The tanδ-frequent variation curve exhibits loss "peaks" and "valleys", and the curve shifts towards higher frequencies with increasing of temperature. When the hottest spot temperature exceeds 120℃, the conductive loss in the insulation medium becomes prominent, and the tanδ-frequent variation curve shows a linear decreasing trend in the logarithmic coordinate system. A hottest spot temperature exceeding 140℃ will damage the internal insulation of the bushing, leading to a sharp increase in tanδ and capacitance while the insulation resistance drastically decreases after returning to room temperature. When the hottest spot temperature exceeds 200℃, a large amount of gas will be generated inside the bushing. Local overheating cause carbonization and cracking of the bushing core, which lead to a sudden increase in tanδ and a sharp decrease in capacitance. This study can provide a reference for the optimization design, testing, and operational status evaluation of bushings.

articleTitle: Optimization of Generator Governor Control Strategy in New Power Systems with Stochastic Power Fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The strong uncertainty of new energy power generation and new load has become a significant problem to power system stability and control, and the control strategy should be optimized in this new power system to guarantee the operation security. In this paper, stochastic power fluctuations caused by new energy power generation are considered in a single machine infinite-bus system(SMIB) model. Then, the system energy is used to obtain an averaging Itô function, where the model variables are transferred from state variables to system energy. The stochastic power fluctuations are associated to system energy change in this function, and the system model dimension can also be simplified. Furthermore, a dynamic programming function is established with a new control objective of new power systems with stochastic power fluctuations, from which the optimal control strategy is obtained. The effectiveness of proposed optimal control strategy is confirmed by simulation that the power angle fluctuation can be significant suppressed.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Transient Modeling and Frequency Response Analysis of The Large-Scale Renewable Energy Base
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: China's wind and solar resources are centrally distributed in the west and north of the country, with the advancing renewable energy industry witnessing the development of large-scale and remote projects. Simultaneously, large-scale renewable energy bases often utilize LCC-HVDC power transmission to connect with the receiving grid. In such cases, relying on traditional AC networking to access the sending grid may lead to insufficient resistance to frequency and voltage disturbances. This paper firstly constructed a full electromagnetic transient model of the renewable energy LCC-HVDC feeder system based on the MMC-HVDC connection, which contains the sending grid, MMC-HVDC, large-scale renewable energy base, LCC-HVDC and receiving grid. Then, the frequency regulation control of the renewable energy unit and MMC-HVDC is designed based on steady-state control. Through the software integration of RT-LAB and HYPERsim as well as the hardware integration of CPU and FPGA, combined with model decoupling, the parallel heterogeneous simulation of the system is realized, which greatly improves the simulation efficiency. Simulation results under load disturbance demonstrate that the frequency regulation control of renewable energy units and MMC-HVDC can effectively enhance the frequency safety level of large-scale renewable energy bases.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow based on Semidefinite Programming Relaxation Considering Wind Power Correlation and Volatility
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the integration of new energy sources into the power system, especially wind power generation, the intermittent and unstable nature of wind power has significantly impacted power flow in power system operations. This paper addresses these challenges by considering wind power uncertainty, wind speed correlation, and load uncertainty. By modeling both the wind power generation and the load, this article transforms the optimal power flow model into a semidefinite programming problem that can be relaxed. This transformation facilitates the handling of complex, non-linear optimization problems inherent in power system operations. The correctness of the proposed method in this paper has been validated using several standard IEEE test cases. These tests demonstrate the capability of the proposed method to manage the uncertainties and correlations associated with large-scale wind power integration, providing a robust solution for future power system optimization and planning.

articleTitle: Aggregation Model of Distributed Energy Storage and Its Optimal Revenue Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Owing to the benefits of resilience and flexibility, the distributed energy storage plays an important role in the demand-response of the modern power grids. In this paper, two typical resilient distributed energy storage sources, namely, the electric vehicle (EV) and user-side energy storage (UES), are considered. The scheduling potential models of the individual EV and the aggregate EVs are developed from the perspectives of power and energy. Moreover, the parameters of EVs and the stochastic factors such as time instants of grid-connection and off-grid are all revealed in the developed models. Similarly, the scheduling potential models of the individual UES and the aggregate UESs are also developed. For the purpose of maximizing the revenue in the electricity market, a optimal scheduling model is designed by taking the aggregators of EV and UES as well as the parameters of electric market into account. Finally, simulation studies are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed models.

articleTitle: Generation Method of Typical Operation Scenarios of High-proportion New Energy Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The conventional manual extraction method employed by operators for identifying typical operation scenarios can no longer adequately address the demand for refined management in high-proportion new energy grid operations. Consequently, this study proposes a data-driven approach for generating typical operation scenarios within high-proportion new energy power grids. Initially, power grid operation data is collected to establish a comprehensive set of power grid operation scenarios. Subsequently, principal component analysis (PCA) is utilized to identify the primary characteristic parameters of the operation scenarios. Next, the K-means algorithm is applied to cluster the set of power system operation scenarios across all time periods, resulting in the derivation of typical time-point operation scenarios. Lastly, through the transformation of operation scenario types at each moment of the day, daily scenarios undergo dimension reduction and clustering to derive typical daily operation scenarios. The efficaciousness of the proposed method is validated using data from a provincial power grid.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Optimization Model for Power System Considering CCES
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Driven by the dual-carbon target, the conversion of power system to low carbon is imminent. Energy storage technologies, especially compressed carbon dioxide energy storage (CCES), have shown great potential in power system due to their advantages of environmental friendliness and flexibility. However, few studies have taken CCES into account in power system optimization models. Therefore, this paper proposes a multi-objective optimization model for power system considering CCES. The model integrates the interactions of factors such as power and air pressure within the CCES, aiming to achieve multi-objective optimization such as reducing operating costs and voltage fluctuations. It also adopts an advanced multi-objective optimization strategy based on NSGA-III and combines the TOPSIS method to dynamically determine the weight allocation of each objective. Through experiments on an IEEE-33 network system, validity and practicality of the proposed method is verified in this paper.

articleTitle: Assessment of Cascaded SVG Performance using RTDS Based Hardware in Loop Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to verify the performance of the cascaded SVG (Static Var Generator) control system, this paper proposes a hardware-in-loop testing scheme, based on the RTDS (Real Time Digital Simulator). Firstly, the basic structure and operating principle of the SVG are briefly introduced. Multi-step simulations are adopted to satisfy the simulation requirements of the high-frequency switching power electronic devices of the SVG, so as to provide a reliable circuit model for the hardware-in-loop testing. GTFPGA and Aurora communication protocol are used instead of the traditional I/O ports to achieve high rate transmission of digital signals. Communication and coordination control functions of the SVG controller and RTDS are verified by using a purpose-building hardware-in-loop pre-test system. Finally, the steady-state and transient performances of the SVG controller is verified in according with the relevant testing requirement. The test results confirm that the hardware-in-loop testing scheme proposed in this paper is effective and reliable. The SVG controller satisfies the technical requirement for the design.

articleTitle: Safety Evaluation of Electric Vehicles Carried in Waterway Foreign Trade Container Transportation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to evaluate the safety of electric vehicles carried in waterway foreign trade container transportation and solve the problems of insufficient evaluation data and poor data quality, gray cloud safety evaluation model for electric vehicles in waterway foreign trade container transportation is proposed based on gray theory and cloud theory. Firstly, evaluation index system is constructed. Sequence relationship analysis method (G1), entropy method and game theory are used to calculate combination weights of each indicator. And then gray cloud model is used to calculate gray cloud clustering coefficient of each indicator. Comprehensive clustering coefficient is obtained. Finally, safety level is determined. Case study is carried out using gray cloud method. The results show that safety level of electric vehicles carried in waterway foreign trade container transportation is general level, which is in line with the actual situation. Countermeasures and suggestions are proposed for indicators with general and poor level. The case study shows that gray cloud evaluation model has good applicability and feasibility in the safety evaluation of electric vehicles in waterway foreign trade container transportation.

articleTitle: Research on Secure Transmission System Based on Data Encryption of New Energy Station
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of the new energy industry, the safe and reliable transmission of data at new energy sites has become crucial. In this paper, a new energy station data secure and reliable transmission system is studied. The encrypted graph is obtained by converting the number into a graph, which provides a unique identity for each data packet, increases the concealability of the encrypted data, and makes the encrypted data more difficult to identify and crack. Further through image recognition and complex numerical conversion, the difficulty of data encryption is increased, thus improving the security of data transmission. The use of on-site images as part of the encryption process can make the encrypted data different from the original data in form, increase the concealment, provide multi-dimensional feature analysis for the data, and increase the complexity of the encryption process.

articleTitle: Multi-Time-Scale Scheduling Strategy Considering the Operational Characteristics of Hydrogen Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Given the operational characteristics of hydrogen energy storage and the uncertainties in energy sources and loads in hybrid energy storage microgrids, a three-stage multi-timescale hybrid energy storage scheduling strategy is proposed. This strategy incorporates day-ahead, intraday, and rolling-real-time adjustments to optimize microgrid operations and minimize operating costs. The strategy leverages the unique charging and discharging characteristics of hydrogen storage, along with the operational behaviors of battery and flywheel storage systems. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy effectively optimizes microgrid operations, achieving economic efficiency. Furthermore, the strategy's performance improves significantly in terms of both economy and stability compared to a traditional day-ahead-real-time two-stage scheduling strategy as prediction accuracy decreases. Specifically, at 50% prediction accuracy, the proposed strategy reduces economic costs by 38%.

articleTitle: RiscV-based Edge Intelligence Application for Securing Power Automation Device
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: For the power automation system, which is literally a cloud-edge collaboration system, the cybersecurity topic is becoming the top priority. The power automation device as the edge intelligent device of automation network does not only play the role of data acquisition, analysis and interaction with the cloud but also undertakes responsibilities for security leveraging trusted core chip, secure operation system, and secure application mechanism. Meanwhile, the trusted chip core is fundamental to implement the secure power automation. This paper presents an Edge intelligent device prototype based on the RiscV core chip because the RiscV architecture significantly mitigates the security risks due to the open source core. And the operating system and application mechanism for the edge intelligent device is also addressed to secure all the power automation system. For the operating system, it should be able defend against all kinds of cyberattacks leveraging AI machine learning algorithm. On the other hand, for application mechanism, the communication between devices and control center should be protected according to the existing standard IEC 62351 series. In addition, verification results at lab compared with others are shown in the last section.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheme of STATCOM Parameters for Temporary Overvoltage Suppression
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The temporary overvoltage (TOV) issue arises more frequently in modern power system as the access of electronic power equipment nowadays. One main reason is the reactive power surplus generated by reactive power compensators such as STATCOM. Due to the inherent delay of control and measurement in STATCOM, its reactive current output during the low-voltage ride through (LVRT) period cannot be withdrawn in time after fault clearance, resulting in surplus reactive power that raises the terminal voltage. To improve the voltage support capability of STATCOM, this paper first established the equivalent impedance model of STATCOM, then analyzed the influence of control parameters on TOV based on the dynamics of the current controller and filter. On this basis, the parameter range is determined according to the TOV and stability constraint, so as to form a parameter optimization scheme. The simulation results show that the proposed scheme can effectively suppress TOV.

articleTitle: Energy Storage Scheduling for Multi-Energy Complementary Systems Based on Nonlinear Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimization and scheduling method of energy storages in a multi-energy complementary system (MECS) based on nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC). First, a mathematical model of a MECS with various energy storage technologies is established considering the characteristics of different energy storage units. The global long-term optimization is performed in CPLEX to determine the optimal energy storage allocation strategy. Then, the NMPC method is used for real-time optimization and control of the system, with the objectives of minimizing the operating cost and carbon emissions. NMPC can perform real-time scheduling of various energy storage units based on real-time load demand, electricity prices and renewable energy fluctuations, further optimizing the short-term operating cost. Case study results demonstrate that the suggested approach significantly reduces the MECS’s total costs of operation.

articleTitle: Adjustable Potential Estimation of Electrical Vehicle Aggregation Considering Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the proposal of double carbon goal in China, it is inevitable that vast new energy with adjustable flexibility are connected to the power grid. However, the inherent randomness and volatility of new energy also bring great challenges to the real-time power dynamic balance and operation of the power grid. As a typical representative of flexible load, it is of great significance to accurately evaluate the adjustable potential of electric vehicle (EV). Therefore, this paper proposes an assessment method of the adjustable potential of EV aggregation taking demand response into account. Firstly, the travel rules and operation characteristics of EVs are studied. Secondly, considering the factors such as state of charge, adjustment amount and electricity price, a quantitative demand response model of EVs is established based on Takagi-Sugeno-Kang fuzzy method, and the adjustable potential of EVs is evaluated. Finally, the validity and rationality of the model is verified by the simulation analysis of the dynamic vehicle data in Wuxi.

articleTitle: Resilience Evaluation Method of Urban Power Grid Under the Influence of Typhoon
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: At present, the southeast coastal areas of China have been repeatedly attacked by typhoons from the Pacific Ocean, causing partial damage to the urban power system, which has seriously hindered the development of the local social economy. Therefore, it is very important to prevent typhoon disasters by evaluating the resilience of the local power grid. This paper mainly describes how to evaluate the resilience of the local power system in the southeast coastal area under the influence of typhoon. Firstly, the visual path wind field model of typhoon is established by using the simple prediction method and Batts wind field model. Then, the resilience evaluation index is determined, and the multi-dimensional resilience evaluation system in the form of matrix is established. Finally, the only index that can measure the resilience of power system is obtained, and the purpose of resilience evaluation is achieved.

articleTitle: A Study on Digital Grid Standard System and Implication Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to build the digital power grid and support the construction of new type of power system, it is necessary to update the power grid standard system. Referring to the smart grid architecture model developed by the International Electrotechnical Commission, a digital grid standard architecture model is proposed. A combination of top-down and bottom-up methods is put forward as the overall idea to construct the standard system. Based on the use case methodology, a power grid standard system implementation approach is formed by summarizing the business and technical requirements of digital grid, carrying out top-level design of the standard system, and sorting out and diagnosing the current relevant standards. In order to demonstrate the methods in a specific scenario, the primary and secondary collaborative planning of distribution network is taken as a business case, from which typical business use cases and system use cases are parsed out. The source side fields of some data in this scenario are compared with the relevant current standards. The results show that the method can effectively analyze the completeness, adequacy and compatibility of the standards, and provide guidance for the construction of digital grid standard system.

Author Keywords: primary and secondary collaborative planning of distributed network

articleTitle: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Energy Management in Community Energy Trading
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Considering the differentiated characteristics of prosumers in new power systems, the high importance of privacy in energy trading and the limitations of traditional model-based optimization methods within multiple uncertainties, this paper proposes a multi-agent reinforcement learning method with differentiated characteristics and privacy preservation for energy management. Firstly, the differentiated characteristics of prosumer are analyzed and corresponding typical prosumer models are established. Secondly, based on the community market structure, a community energy trading model based on the mid-market rate pricing is constructed. Finally, taking market benefits and operating costs as optimization objectives, the energy trading optimization of prosumers participating in community energy trading is constructed into a partially observable Markov decision process. Aiming at the non-stationary problem of multi-agent environment, this paper proposes to approximate the central Q function of the soft actor-critic algorithm by the mean-field approximation mechanism. The proposed algorithm is then employed to obtain the prosumers’ energy management decision. Results of case study show that the proposed algorithm has outstanding advantages in aspects of convergence, efficiency and economy in energy management within community market considering differentiated characteristics and privacy preservation.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Unit Commitment Based on Deep Graph Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources such as wind and solar energy has led to the widespread replacement of traditional power sources, significantly reducing the short-circuit capacity of the power grid and increasing the risk of transient voltage instability. Current research utilizes short-circuit ratios or capacities as constraints to optimize start-up strategies, ensuring sufficient voltage support strength in the system. However, short-circuit ratios or capacities can only estimate the system's voltage support capability and cannot accurately characterize the transient voltage insecurity risks at various nodes. Therefore, a method based on deep graph reinforcement learning for optimizing unit start-up strategies is proposed. This approach combines graph-based deep learning methods with reinforcement learning. By integrating the feature extraction capabilities of deep learning with the policy-solving capabilities of reinforcement learning, the method enables rapid online acquisition of start-up strategies after offline training completion.

articleTitle: The Study of MPPT Control Strategy Based on Chaotic Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: When the PV array is shaded, the conventional maximum power tracking strategy cannot effectively track the maximum power point. Firstly, the equivalent model of photovoltaic cells is established, and the essential features of photovoltaic cells output are then examined under various lighting and temperature scenarios. Then, in view of the shortcomings of the particle swarm MPPT control strategy, the core parameters of PSO were dynamically improved and the initialization link was optimized, in order to optimize the improved particle swarm MPPT algorithm, it is crucial to enhance its capacity to track the maximum power of the photovoltaic array under any shadowing conditions and to significantly speed up the time needed to reach the optimal operating point. Finally, the MPPT control strategies based on P&O, PSO and IPSO are simulated and compared in Simulink, and the findings indicate that the method proposed in this paper successfully tracks the maximum power in a variety of environments. This approach also ensures a reduced number of oscillations and a superior convergence speed.

articleTitle: An Inverter-based Harmonic Oscillation Suppression Strategy with Active Damping
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the use of large amounts of secondary clean energy, it has increased burdens for the power grid and brought more serious harmonic problems. The network resistance composed of multiple grid-connected inverters and local loads is very complex, and their mutual coupling even causes harmonic resonance, which will bring abundant harmonic disturbances. To address the above problems, this paper proposes a control method of active damping for grid-connected inverters, which effectively suppresses harmonic components by separating the harmonics of voltage and current at the grid-connected point and controlling them through feedback, thus introducing virtual resistance and conductance to the harmonic circuit model. The device only performs feedback suppression for harmonic currents, so its capacity is low and it is flexible to use without affecting the work of other grid-connected inverters. The validity and correctness of the approach as presented in the paper has been preliminarily demonstrated by using the MatLab software.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Design of Uninterrupted Ice Melting Device for Overhead Lines of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The icing of overhead lines caused by ice and snow disasters seriously affects the normal power supply of the power grid. In this paper, an optimal design scheme of the device is proposed for a non-stop ice melting technology based on zero-sequence current, which optimizes the grounding transformer based on the special characteristics of the high overload transformer to reduce the redundancy of the device’s capacity, and designs a non-stop ice melting device with high leakage resistance to reduce the total weight and volume of the device and enhance the integrity of the device. Through the above improvements, the lightweight of the online ice melting device can be effectively realized, which is convenient for the subsequent promotion and application of the device.

articleTitle: A Novel Control Forecasting Method for Electricity-Carbon Dioxide Based on PID Tracking Control Theorem
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This study presents an innovative approach for predicting carbon emissions utilizing a PID tracking control mechanism. The proposed method incorporates past CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission prediction discrepancies and employs electricity consumption data in a feed-forward strategy to improve forecast precision and reduce response delay. A comparative evaluation against pre-trained models, including LSTM and ARDL, reveals that this approach significantly lowers prediction errors and offers a considerable reduction in computational time when compared to LSTM models. These results serve as a useful guide for policy-makers and academics in enhancing CO2 prediction techniques and in the development of effective CO2 reduction strategies.

articleTitle: Optimization of Shared Energy Storage Operation Model with Multi subject Participation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the gradual exposure of the shortcomings of the independent ESS(energy storage system) and the further development of the sharing economy, SES(shared energy storage) has begun to be explored and paid attention to. This paper proposes a SES operation model that mainly considers the participation of SES operators, power grids, and user entities, in response to the research on the operation mode of SES with the participation of multiple entities. Firstly, based on the proposed operational model, net profit models for all participating entities were established; Secondly, in order to maximize the earnings of SES operators, considering the constraints of various interests and ESS operation control, a mixed integer convex programming model is processed through quadratic fitting, M-envelope, and T-envelope methods; Finally, a numerical simulation was conducted on three users in a certain region, and the Gurobi toolkit was applied to solve the operation plan of SES, verifying the effectiveness of the operation mode.

articleTitle: A Novel Distributed Resilient Control Strategy for HVACs under FDI Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Utilizing variable load resources to their fullest potential is crucial in mitigating the power fluctuation in the power grids brought about by the high percentage of renewable energy integration. The heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) loads account for a large portion of the total electricity consumption, which offer considerable regulatory potential. To achieve effective control of such numerous and dispersed HVACs, distributed control has been widely used due to its flexibility and scalability. However, distributed control is susceptible to cyberattacks like false data injection (FDI) attacks, which could compromise the safe operation of the grid and impede HVAC power regulation. This paper suggests a novel Distributed Resilient Control Method(DRCM) for HVACs under FDI attacks. First, a distributed control framework of HVACs is established to regulate their power and offer the power grid adjustment capacity. Then, FDI attack models of different units in the distributed control framework are established. Using the FDIAs models, The detrimental effect of FDI attacks is measured mathematically. Based on this, a novel DRCM for HVACs under FDI attacks is proposed to ensure the smooth progress of the demand response process under cyberattacks. Moreover, the efficacy of the suggested approach is demonstrated by the application of Lyapunov stability theories. Finally, simulation experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed resilient method.

articleTitle: Considering the Adjustment of Template Inverters in Distributed Photovoltaic Automatic Generation Control Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To meet the urgent needs of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems to participate in power grid peak load management and frequency modulation, this paper proposes an automatic power generation control method suitable for distributed PV. Firstly, considering the differences in type, quantity, capacity, and geographical location of inverters used in distributed PV systems, a standard communication network architecture for PV inverters and other equipment is proposed to ensure rapid data exchange and responsiveness to scheduling commands. Secondly, an automatic power generation control method for model inverters involved in power regulation is introduced. This method is based on meeting the power control requirements for distributed PV participation in grid dispatching and fully accounts for the variability in inverter capacity configurations and minimum continuous output constraints, among other factors. Finally, the efficacy and accuracy of the proposed method are corroborated through case studies.

articleTitle: Energy efficiency evaluation of desulfurization system based on AHP-EWM and DBO-RF
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Energy efficiency evaluation of desulfurization system refers to assessing the energy efficiency level of the system through the data generated in the production process. For the problem of coexistence of subjective and objective information in the desulfurization system of coal-fired power station, this paper proposes the AHP-EWM evaluation model with random number combination assignment. For the high complexity of the traditional comprehensive evaluation model, this paper adopts the DBO-RF algorithm to avoid the subsequent real-time evaluation step. Dung beetle optimizer solves the problem of the model being trapped in the local optimal point due to too many hyperparameters of random forest. The experimental results show that there is a great overlap between the model derived from the DBO-RF training and the results obtained from the evaluation model of the AHP-EWM with combinatorial assignment, and the energy efficiency evaluation of the FGD system can be realized using the DBO-RF algorithm.

articleTitle: Low-carbon Economic Operation of Micro-energy Network Based on LCA Carbon Trading Mechanism and Natural Gas Pressure Energy Utilization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The influence of natural gas pressure energy (NGPE) on carbon emissions and operating overhead of micro-energy grid (MEG) are clearly studied in this paper. Firstly, it proposes a multi-energy coupling microgrid architecture that incorporates NGPE. Subsequently, the study analyzes the power generation and refrigeration output characteristics associated with this energy source. Next, the method of the life cycle assessment (LCA) is applied to analyze the actual carbon emissions from new energy equipment, specifically calculating those of photovoltaic units, wind turbine units, and expansion generator units. Finally, in order to build microgrids, the society is constantly optimizing low-carbon economic model and incorporating a step-type carbon emissions trading mechanism from the LCA. The model is primarily designed to minimize the daily operating overhead of the microgrid. Case analysis demonstrates that the operation model developed in this study reduces the total daily operating overhead by 22.73% and cuts carbon trading expenses by 38.9%. This confirms that integrating the LCA carbon trading mechanism (LCA CTM) and NGPE improves system carbon emissions while ensuring cost-effective operation.

articleTitle: A Non-invasive Method of IGBT Voltage Rise Time Detection Considering Cable Length
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Power electronic devices are developing to high-frequency operating mode because of the fast growth of power electronics technology. As the core switching device of modern industrial inverters, the Insulated gate bipolar transistor (IGBT)’s reliability greatly impacts the system’s stability. Therefore, monitoring the condition of power electronic devices in inverters is necessary. To realize the non-invasive detection of IGBT device status during the operation of the inverter, based on the corresponding relationship between the output current high-frequency response time of the inverter and the IGBT voltage rise time, the paper considers that in practical industrial applications, the location of the inverter and the motor is different. The cable used has different lengths, which will affect the high-frequency current. A non-invasive method of voltage rise time detection for a three-phase output parallel RLC detection circuit of the inverter is proposed, whose potency and accuracy are verified in the SABER simulation platform.

articleTitle: Digital Modeling of Power Grid Engineering Driven by Information Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The application of digital modeling driven by information flow in power grid engineering has attracted increasing attention. As an important part of the power system, power grid engineering requires a large amount of data support and information exchange in all stages of planning, design, construction, operation and maintenance management. The purpose of this paper is to explore the application of digital modeling technology driven by information flow in power grid engineering, and to realize information management and data exchange in the whole life cycle of power grid engineering by constructing a digital model. Through digital modeling driven by information flow, the planning, design, and construction processes of power grid engineering can be optimized and coordinated, thereby improving the efficiency and quality of engineering construction.

articleTitle: Analysis of Strategic Bidding Behavior of Renewable Energy Participation in Electricity Spot Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the development of power spot market in some provinces of China, and the way of renewable energy to participate in the power spot market, and proposes a bidding model considering the uncertainty of renewable energy output, and trains the SAC algorithm on the new energy bidding behaviors of renewable energy considering different output expectations and prediction error variance, to get the results of the renewable energy in different cases for improving their own The second step is to analyze the behavioral tendency of renewable energy under different circumstances. Secondly, we analyze the impact of renewable energy on power abandonment through their own strategic reporting behavior in different situations, including the way renewable energy can improve their own income by reducing their own daily reporting volume and improving their own transaction price through intra-day arbitrage and formation of blocking, so as to provide a certain reference for the rule makers of the electricity spot market under the participation of renewable energy, and to reduce the phenomenon of renewable power abandonment and to improve the efficiency of the renewable energy in the power system. For reducing the phenomenon of renewable energy power abandonment and improving the rate of renewable energy consumption in the power system, it has a certain positive impact.

articleTitle: Time-Sequential Reactive Power Optimization Method for Large-Scale Complex Distribution Networks Based on the CloudPSS-DSLab Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the massive integration of distributed energy resources and energy storage, the operation of power distribution systems has become increasingly complex, with the modeling granularity for analytical computations now encompassing the entire voltage levels range from 0.38kV to 220kV. Traditional reactive power optimization methods have shown inadequacies with such large-scale power grids, for instance, mathematical programming methods considering nonlinear constraints and objective functions have poor computational efficiency and stability. This issue also persists with conventional heuristic search algorithms. Meanwhile, the computational accuracy of linear programming or mixed-integer programming methods, which are used after linearizing the model, is hard to guarantee in large-scale power grids. In this paper, we propose a heuristic reactive power optimization algorithm by constructing the scope of each shunt capacitor based on the principle of prioritizing local compensation. The algorithm is driven by the efficient time-series power flow engine of the CloudPSS-DSLab platform, achieving long-period time-series reactive power optimization. The algorithm has been validated on the IEEE 8500-node test case, and the results show that it can effectively control the bus node voltage levels within a reasonable range and possesses high computational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Method for Estimating Interharmonic Harmonics Based on S-Transform and TT Transform
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This research introduces an innovative approach to estimating phasors, capable of precisely identifying and quantifying harmonics and interharmonics in power systems. A novel technique is presented for measuring steady-state harmonic and interharmonic parameters. By leveraging signal spectrum characteristics derived from the TT transformation, and incorporating windowed interpolation to mitigate spectrum leakage and fence effects, this method effectively tackles the challenge of detecting low-amplitude, high-frequency harmonics and interharmonics in the power grid. The performance of the proposed approach is assessed using M-class phasor measurement units conforming to the IEEE standard C37.118.1 in a simulated environment. The test findings demonstrate that the suggested approach is feasible and effective for analyzing steady-state, dynamic harmonic, and interharmonic situations.

articleTitle: Distributed Resource Uncertainty Trading Model under Typhoon Spatio-Temporal Evolution
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Addressing the challenge of ensuring safe and reliable electricity consumption during typhoon conditions in distribution networks, this paper presents a distributed resource trading model. It incorporates scenario probability, considering the spatio-temporal evolution of typhoons on distribution network lines and the analysis of distributed resource failures in the affected area. Initially, a spatio-temporal evolution model of typhoon weather is constructed based on meteorological data. Quantitative analysis of distribution network component failure rates is conducted by establishing a wind field model. Subsequently, Monte Carlo simulation is employed to generate failure scenarios for lines, wind turbines, and photovoltaic units under typhoon conditions. To address uncertainty in wind and solar power output during typhoons, the k-means algorithm is utilized. A distributed resource trading model is then formulated, aiming to minimize the economic dispatch cost of the distribution network during typhoons while considering uncertainty. Finally, a system model is implemented using the Matlab 2023a simulation platform to validate the proposed model's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Research on the Power Sharing Strategy of Islanded Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid under Master-slave Control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Under the operation of AC/DC hybrid microgrid in islanding mode, giving full play to the advantages of mutual support and mutual aid of subgrids on both sides is the key to realizing the system's long-term stable operation. Accordingly, a power sharing control strategy based on master-slave mode (MSM) is proposed. After the energy storage of the AC and DC subgrids on both sides is used as the master control unit to suppress system power fluctuations, all or part of its power is proportionally shared with the dispatchable distributed generators (DPDGs) in the system according to the settings and passed to the other subgrid through the bidirectional interlinking converter (BIC) to realize the effective global power sharing and balancing, and to improve the available capacity and fluctuation suppression capability of the master control unit. Finally, the simulation model is constructed by MATLAB/Simulink to confirm that the control strategy can achieve the autonomous power distribution of the master control unit and the microgrid's power equilibrium.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Transformer Based on SWO and SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Given the inherent difficulty of support vector machines (SVM) in accurately diagnosing transformer fault types, this paper proposes a transformer fault diagnosis method based on spider wasp optimizer (SWO) with SVM. Firstly, the analysis of the dissolved gas present in transformer oil is carried out through the application of the uncoded ratio technique. The amount of dissolved gas in transformer oil is then measured and provided as an input feature for the SVM classifier. Secondly, The SWO algorithm is employed to optimise two crucial parameters (the kernel parameter and the penalty factor) that significantly influence the diagnostic accuracy and performance of the SVM model. Finally, the transformer is fault diagnosed using the method proposed in this paper. The simulation results demonstrate that the SWO algorithm-optimised SVM outperforms the whale optimisation algorithm-SVM (WOA-SVM) and ant colony optimisation-SVM (ACO-SVM). Furthermore, comparing to the WOA-SVM and ACO-SVM, SWO-SVM has the advantage of faster convergence, greater accuracy in detecting system faults, and greater stability compared. The average diagnosis correctness of the latter three methods is 93.52%, 88.89%, and 87.96%, respectively, wihch verifies the superior performance of the SWO-SVM method.

articleTitle: Organizational Description System for Digital Twin of Distribution Network Equipment Based on Object-oriented Equipment Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Digital twin is a mathematical model of a physical object that can accept real-time data and evolve in real time. The fundamental technology underlying digital twin technology is modeling and simulation. For a distribution network with complex structure and numerous devices, the construction of digital twins is of great significance for equipment management and system analysis. This paper first introduces the object-oriented modeling method and presents an object-oriented equipment model (OEM). Subsequently, an organizational description system for digital twin of distribution network equipment based on object-oriented equipment model is designed, and the concrete implementation method is introduced. Finally, by comparing with the simulation results of PSCAD software, the accuracy of the electromagnetic transient (EMT) simulation program, one of the applications of the proposed system, is verified.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization of Hydrogen Energy Storage-involved Interdependent Energy-Transportation System under Multiple Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The integration of energy system field and transportation field is an important development way of energy transition and low-carbon promotion. In order to realize the better energy, environmental and economy performance of the energy-transportation integrated system under multiple uncertainties, which would have effects on system capacity and operation if neglected, this paper proposed a collaborative optimization of the integrated system based on robust optimization model. The results showed the effectiveness of this model and provided reference for designer with system optimization.

articleTitle: Online Gate-oxide Degradation Monitoring of SiC MOSFETs Based on the Turn-on Current Increasing Rate Maximum
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: A new SiC MOSFET gate-oxide degradation precursor, the turn-on current increasing rate maximum, is proposed in this script, and an online monitoring method is developed based on this precursor. The turn-on current increasing rate maximum with the gate-oxide degradation mechanism of SiC MOSFET is first analyzed, then a high electric field experiment is conducted to accelerate the gate-oxide degradation of the device under test. The proposed precursor is compared with the existing precursors, the gate-plateau voltage and the turn-on current increasing rate. Subsequently, the extraction circuit of the proposed precursor and online monitoring system are designed. Finally, the proposed online monitoring method is verified.

articleTitle: An Additional PSS Design for Grid-Forming Converters Tied to Stiff Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With integration of a large number of power electronic devices into the grid, stability issues are continuously occurring. In this paper, a design method for an additional stabilizer specifically for the instability issues caused by grid-forming converters under stiff grid conditions is proposed. Firstly, a detailed model and a simplified model of the grid-forming converter tied system are established. Borrowing the phase compensation method of power system stabilizer (PSS) for synchronous machines, an additional stabilizer for grid-forming converters is designed. The impact of introduction of additional stabilizer and the variation of parameters on the critical short-circuit ratio (CSCR) of grid-forming converters are analyzed. Finally, the above analysis is verified in Matlab/Simulink. The results show that the proposed design method for the additional stabilizer can effectively increase the CSCR of the grid-forming converter tied system, and enhance the static synchronous stability under stiff grid conditions.

articleTitle: Blade-YOLOv8:Improved YOLOv8 for Wind Turbine Blade Defect Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the task of using drones to detect defects in wind turbine blades, there are challenges such as missed detections due to the small size of the defects and their random, varying scales. However, the existing model’s detection speed is slow, rendering it unsuitable for deployment on edge devices. To address these problems, this paper introduces Blade-YOLOv8, a lightweight edge detection algorithm based on the YOLOv8 model. Firstly, the Global Multi-scale Fusion-Space Pooling Pyramid-Fast (GMF-SPPF) module is introduced, which captures global perspective information and mitigates the impact of varying scales on detection results. Secondly, a new C2f_EMA structure, based on Partial Convolution (PConv) and Efficient Multi-Scale Attention (EMA) mechanisms, is employed in the backbone and neck networks to make the network lightweight while enhancing the detection ability for small targets and reducing the number of model parameters. Experimental results show that, compared to the original YOLOv8s model, the improved algorithm reduces the number of parameters by 21.6%, while increasing detection accuracy, specifically mAP50 and mAP50:95, by 4.3% and 7.5%, respectively. And the speed on an NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano edge computing platform reaches 38 FPS. Consequently, the improved algorithm is well-suited for practical applications and deployment in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Power Equipment Condition Detection Method Based on Voiceprint Compression and Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Voiceprint detection technology can assist inspection personnel in detecting and evaluating the condition of transformers. This paper proposes a transformer condition detection and evaluation method based on voiceprint compression and recognition. The method first extracts the voiceprint features of the transformer audio, then filters and compresses the voiceprint features in the frequency dimension, and finally uses a convolutional neural network to evaluate the transformer condition. Using a 35kV transformer as the object, a transformer audio dataset is obtained through on-site audio collection, simulation experiments, and sample augmentation. Test results show that the proposed method reduces the voiceprint dimension from 1025 to 80, reducing the computation and GPU memory to 8.1% and 7.7%, respectively, while achieving a voiceprint recognition accuracy of 83.5%.

articleTitle: A CT Disconnection and High Impedance Fault Identification Scheme Based on Branch Zero Sequence Current Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: High-resistance faults on the bus may be misjudged as current transformer (CT) disconnection faults by the protection system, leading to protection refusal and further development of the fault. Conversely, CT disconnection may be misjudged as a high-resistance bus fault, causing false tripping of the protection system. To accurately distinguish between these two faults, this paper uses a double bus double-section model to analyze the characteristics and differences of differential current, restraining current, and branch zero-sequence current under both fault conditions. Based on these differences, corresponding criteria are proposed and integrated into a complete identification scheme. Finally, PSCAD is used to simulate different fault scenarios to verify the accuracy of the identification scheme. The results show that this scheme can effectively identify asymmetric CT disconnection faults and high-resistance faults (HIF) on the bus.

articleTitle: AC Power Flow Constrained Allocation of Energy Storage Systems for Large-scale Renewable Energy Collection and Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: One of the key challenges of large scale integration of renewable energy is the intermittent and uncertain nature of renewable energy generation, which can lead to difficulty in the consumption of renewable energy as well as voltage and frequency fluctuations within the collection grid, threatening system stability and reliability. To address these challenges, energy storage systems (ESSs) have emerged as promising solutions to provide flexibility and balance supply-demand variations in power systems. This paper focuses on the optimal allocation of ESSs for a large-scale renewable energy collection and integration system, to enhance voltage and frequency regulation capabilities while maximizing the utilization of renewable energy resources. A model that considers voltage and frequency constraints to determine the rated power and capacity of ESS as well as identify the most suitable location for deploying ESS is proposed. Due to the large resistance-reactance ratio of the transmission line in the collection network, node voltage is closely related to active power, for which AC power flow of the connection network is constrained in the model. The model is formulated as a single-level mixed-integer programming problem, which can be solved effectively by commercial solvers. A case study is conducted to verify the effectiveness of the model. Allocations with and without AC power flow constraints are considered and the latter results in violation of network limitation, demonstrating the necessity of AC power flow constraints.

articleTitle: A Markov Chain Based Method for Driving Cycle Segment Prediction of HEVs
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Because the limited energy, how to enhance the power utilization efficiency of hybrid electric vehicles has always been a key technology. Accurately predicting the driving cycles of vehicles in advance is the main method to solve this problem. A Markov chain based method is adopted to predict the driving cycle segment in this work. Firstly, a composite case is constructed using several standard driving cycles. After that, the composite driving cycle is segmented and a feature selection is performed. Then, the processed data is clustered into four categories with a fuzzy K-means clustering method. At last, a Markov chain method is adopted to predict the sequence of driving cycle segment. Simulation results indicate that the Markov chain method is more efficient than a ARIMA based method.

articleTitle: Research on Optimization Operation Method of Integrated Energy Microgrid Considering Alternative IDR
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The application of integrated energy systems that integrate multiple energy sources is becoming increasingly widespread, and the participation of multiple energy sources in demand response in integrated energy systems is of great significance. This article proposes an integrated energy microgrid (IEMG) optimization operation method considering alternative IDR. Firstly, an IEMG optimization operation model is constructed, including the cost of purchasing electricity and the cost of purchasing natural gas, the operating income by selling electricity and the cost of demand response. Secondly, establish alternative IDR models, including heating and cooling substitution and electrical substitution. Finally, simulation analysis was conducted to verify the effectiveness of the optimization operation method.

articleTitle: Research on the Collaborative Transition of the Building and Power Sectors for Carbon Peaking and Neutrality Goals in China
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The building is one of the primary sectors for energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions. It is of great significance for achieving carbon peak and neutrality goals through deep coupling between the building and the power industry. Based on the National Energy Strategy and Planning Model (NESAP), this paper provides a detailed analysis of the collaborative energy conservation and carbon mitigation paths between the building and power sectors from the cross-departmental cooperation perspective. The motivation of this study is to clarify the synergistic energy transformation benefits between the building and the power industry, and provide strategic support for the national energy transformation. The results indicate that the building sector energy demand will continue to grow in the future, with an expected peak around 2040, reaching 930 million tons of standard coal equivalent (Mtce). The energy demand for public service buildings in China will continue to rise. Electricity is expected to take center stage as the key energy consumption medium, with its proportion reaching 84.5%. The building sector’s carbon emissions are exhibiting a progressive upward trend and will peak around 2025 at 1.04 billion tons. By 2050, green buildings will be widely distributed, electrification levels will steadily improve, and carbon emissions will decrease by 35.2% compared to 2035. The building sector's indirect power emissions have exhibited a pattern of rising initially before declining. By 2035, carbon dioxide emissions are expected to peak at 1.26 billion tons. Within the framework of a profound decarbonization of the power system, negative emissions are expected to be achieved by 2060.

articleTitle: Practical Identification Method for PV Unit Frequency Regulator
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Establishing a photovoltaic (PV) unit model consistent with actual frequency regulation response characteristics is a prerequisite for analyzing frequency security and stability in high-ratio renewable energy power systems. Existing research on PV unit frequency simulation modeling is relatively limited. Most research uses intelligent algorithms to identify regulator parameters based on the known structure of the frequency regulator, which lacks versatility and engineering practicability. This paper establishes a universal electromagnetic transient model covering the mainstream types of PV units, including de-loading control, virtual inertia control, and droop control. Then, based on the correspondence between the frequency regulation response characteristics and control strategy, a practical identification method is proposed to identify the frequency regulator by using measured frequency response curves of the unit. The comparison of response characteristics between the "black-box" model of actual units and simulation models under various frequency disturbances reveals that the frequency response of the PV unit electromagnetic transient model, derived from the proposed practical identification method, closely matches those of the packaged "black box" model. This validates the effectiveness of the frequency regulator identification method proposed in the paper.

articleTitle: Multivariate Load Short-term Forecasting Method Based on PSO-VMD-GRU-AdaBoost
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The accurate prediction of multi-load of energy system is the basis for promoting the development of the system. In the paper, multivariate load short-term forecasting method based on PSO-VMD-GRU-AdaBoost is proposed based on the consideration of the coupling characteristics of multivariate loads. Firstly, the VMD decomposition model is utilized to obtain the multimodal components of the multivariate load data, and the modal component dataset is constructed; secondly, the AdaBoost algorithm is utilized as an enhancement framework, and the combination of several weak learners, GRU, is combined to form a strong learner, GRU-AdaBoost. Secondly, using the AdaBoost algorithm enhancement framework, multiple weak learner GRUs are combined into a strong learner GRU-AdaBoost, and based on the modal component dataset, the combined GRU-AdaBoost model is trained to obtain the values of the prediction performance evaluation indexes; finally, the improved PSO algorithm is used for parameter optimization of the VMD-GRU-AdaBoost model, to obtain the parameters of the model under the optimal combination of prediction performance evaluation indexes, and then to obtain the accurate prediction results. The results show that the prediction accuracy of the proposed model is improved by 60 %.

articleTitle: Oscillation Suppression Method of Power Electronic Based AC Distribution System Based on Weak Point Location
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The oscillation issues have recently become a main concern in AC power distribution systems, which are mainly caused by high-penetration power electronics. The sub/super-synchronous oscillation phenomena have been frequently observed in practical systems, which seriously affect the safe and stable operation of AC distribution systems. In this paper, an oscillation mitigation scheme based on weak point location for power electronic-based AC distribution system was proposed. By establishing the frequency-domain node admittance matrix model of the AC distribution system, the oscillation stability of the system was analyzed using frequency-domain modal analysis method. Then, the weak points of the system were identified through participation factor matrix and node coupling degree. On this basis, an active damping method based on DC-link voltage feedback was proposed to enhance the stability of the system. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed method was validated by both time-domain simulations and frequency-domain modal analysis.

Author Keywords: power electronics based AC distribution system

articleTitle: Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Approach for Power Command Response Combining Fast and Normal Charging Piles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The rapid growth in the number of electric vehicles (EVs) is conducive to promoting green development. The combination of fast and normal charging can fully leverage the collaborative ability of different types of charging devices. Therefore, a decentralized collaborative charging strategy combining multiple fast and normal charging piles considering power command response based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning (MADRL) is proposed. First, a framework is proposed including power command generation by the distribution system and power command response by multiple charging piles. Then, Minkowski summation is used to build energy boundary model for EV cluster, which can help MADRL algorithm to constraint charging power. Moreover, two Markov Decision Process (MDP) is built, one is built for distribution network system optimization, another one is built for fast and normal charging piles. Finally, case studies are conducted on the training stability, control effect of collaborative objectives, and scalability of the proposed method in different scenarios with multiple fast and normal charging piles of different scales, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed method.

Author Keywords: electric vehicles (EVs) fast and normal charging piles

articleTitle: The Fine Deodorization Experiment of Pulse Corona Discharge Technology on the Odor of Food Waste
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The odor of food waste was a major factor that endangers the body of the masses. The existing process did not completely control the odor. In order to achieve the purpose of fine deodorization, a food waste treatment station in Hangzhou was chosen. The pulsed electropulsing treatment process was introduced at the end of the existing biofilter process to treat the odor, and the effects of the end fillers of different corona discharge plasma on the odor treatment were tested.
