After testing, the single-stage corona discharge plasma can remove 81.72% of the odor concentration and 65.12% of the NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> without fillers. The odor removal rate of the corona discharge plasma system filled with activated carbon reached 89.99%, and the average NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> removal rate was 75.57%. The corona discharge plasma system filled with honeycomb ceramic fillers removed the most odor and NH3, which removed 94.04% and 81.48% respectively, achieving the purpose of fine deodorization.

articleTitle: Dynamic Response Analysis of High Voltage Transmission Tower-Line Coupling System Under Ice and Wind Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Investigating the dynamic characteristics of high-voltage (HV) transmission line coupling systems under ice-wind loads is crucial for bolstering the system's resilience to ice and snow disasters, thereby ensuring power supply safety. Currently, developing an effective analysis method is a focal point in this research domain. This study selects a representative HV transmission line as the subject of investigation and constructs an ice-wind loads coupling model. Using the 220kV ice-covered HV transmission line of the Fujian power grid as a case study, the comprehensive effects of ice thickness, wind attack angle and speed are considered based on the coupled finite element model (FEM). The response characteristics of the HV transmission line ice-wind loads are analyzed, and key parameters such as stress response and displacement response are evaluated. The findings indicate that the ice-wind response of the tower-line system can be effectively analyzed. The simulation calculation model of the transmission line under the tower-line coupling factors presented in this paper aligns more closely with actual working conditions, making it a valuable reference for the design, mechanical analysis, and operation and maintenance of HV transmission lines in specific regions.

articleTitle: Active and reactive power optimization control of photovoltaic and energy storage based on grid forming inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Currently, grid forming inverters are used to support frequency and voltage in distribution networks. Hence, grid forming inverter is very important for active and reactive power optimization control. This paper first introduces the virtual synchronous generator control method. The Successive Quadratic Programming (SQP) algorithm and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm are respectively used to optimize the active and reactive power control parameters. The simulation results validate that the optimization algorithm can improve the frequency and voltage dynamic performance of the system.

articleTitle: SO2 emission prediction model based on the combination of autoregression and GRU-AM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Currently, thermal power generation still dominates in China, but it emits a large amount of pollutants such as SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. To reduce emissions, most power plants adopt the limestone-gypsum wet desulfurization technology. However, empirical control strategies are commonly used for desulfurization systems in coal-fired power plants, which often lead to high operational costs. Therefore, it is very important to establish an accurate prediction model for desulphurization system to achieve the goal of low carbon operation and environmental protection standards, so as to improve the operation economy of unit desulphurization system. In this paper, a prediction model for the outlet SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration in WFGD was developed based on the Gated Recurrent Unit with Attention Mechanism (GRU-AM) network, which utilizes autoregressive features. Unlike most existing modeling methods that neglect the time factor, the GRU method extracts temporal relationships from the past and current states of the desulfurization system. Additionally, by introducing an attention mechanism, the model can better adapt to different parts of the sequence. Using data from a specific power plant as an example, experimental results demonstrate that the proposed prediction model can continuously and precisely forecast the outlet SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> concentration in flue gas desulfurization, providing operators with an accurate reference for controlling the desulfurization process.

articleTitle: The Study on Grid Stability of Doubly Fed Induction Generators with Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Doubly fed wind turbine technology plays a crucial role in wind power generation. To lower the cost of wind power generation and minimize the impact of wind power output fluctuations on the grid, it is necessary to combine optimized energy storage strategies with wind power generation technology. Supercapacitor energy storage has emerged as an effective solution for addressing grid integration issues and enhancing the stability of power systems in wind energy applications. This study proposes a scheme to stabilize wind turbine fluctuations by integrating SVG (Static Var Generator) with supercapacitor energy storage in the doubly fed wind turbine system, based on reactive power flow in wind power systems. Through the construction of a simulation model of the doubly fed wind turbine grid-connected operation and subsequent simulation analysis, the results confirm that this combined strategy significantly improves the stability of the entire wind power system.

articleTitle: Location and Capacity Determination of Distributed Photovoltaics in Distribution Networks Considering Multi-Substation Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Amidst the swift escalation of photovoltaic power generation technology and subsequent implementation of encouraging policies in China, distributed photovoltaic (DPV) power generation has shown a trend of high-density network connection, presenting novel issues and obstacles to the functioning of distribution networks. To safeguard the secure operation of these networks and enhance DPV utilization, this article proposes a method for the location and capacity determination of DPV in distribution networks considering multi-substation coordination. Firstly, the characteristics and modes of the coordination of multiple distribution substations are scrutinized. Secondly, a mathematical optimization model is formulated to determine the optimal DPV placement and sizing in distribution networks considering the multi-substation coordination, and solved to get the best result according to the characteristics of the model. Finally, the validity of the proposed model and the employed algorithm are confirmed through simulations in an enhanced IEEE 33-node distribution network.

articleTitle: Data-driven Linearization for Real-time Decision-making in Emergency Control of Power System Transient Stabilization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Emergency control is crucial for ensuring the stable operation of the power system following a fault, and its essence is a large-scale dynamic optimization problem. The traditional way of offline computation and real-time matching has the risk of mismatch in complex power grids. Real-time decision-making is crucial for maintaining the transient stability of the system, but it requires extremely high decision-solving speed. Based on the artificial intelligence method to mine the correlation between emergency control measures and sensitivity offline, this paper proposes a data-driven linearized real-time decision-making method for emergency control. Firstly, the stability constraints within the optimization model of emergency control are linearized using the EEAC (Extended Equal Area Criterion) and sensitivity methods. Then, the BP neural network model is established to fit the mapping relationship between the transient power angle stability control measures and the sensitivity of the control measures based on offline data. Finally, according to the constructed sensitivity mapping network, the sensitivity of different control measures under the current operation mode and fault is calculated in real time, and the linearized constraints are substituted to solve the emergency control optimization problem. The simulation analysis is carried out in the 10,000 node standard test system, and the results show that the quantified results of system stability under different control measures based on the sensitivity mapping network have high prediction accuracy, and the emergency control strategy developed on this basis effectively adapts to operational changes and restores system stability.

articleTitle: Reducing Renewable Energy Output Deviation Using Demand-Side Flexibility
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The number of renewable energy providers in electricity markets is growing. As the renewable energy resource outputs can not be accurately predicted in day-ahead stage, renewable energy providers need to reduce the energy output deviation between day-ahead and real-time markets in real-time stage. This paper proposes a framework to reduce this deviation. Firstly, renewable energy providers determine the energy outputs to be settled according to the day-ahead bids and real-time output. Then, a two-level game is used to model the energy settlement process between energy providers and flexible users. In the upper level, energy providers compete to set electricity prices to make profits. In the lower level, flexible users respond to electricity prices and adjust energy usage by playing an evolutionary game. Simulation results prove the practicality of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: Research on the Control Strategy of Electric-Hydrogen-Thermal Coupled Multi-Source Heating System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The-multi-source heating system has the advantages of low operating cost and good stability compared with the single heat source system, and this article mainly focuses on the research of heating control strategy for a set of electric-hydrogen-heat coupled systems composed of fuel cell and air source heat pump. Under the premise of meeting the stable operation of the system, a suitable control strategy is formulated for the ratio of the power output of the heating equipment and the order of priority of the power output during the operation of the coupled system, to determine the start-up sequence of each heat source and the respective heat loads borne by each heat source under different outdoor temperatures.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis and Enhancement of an Islanded Microgrid with Grid-forming Converters and Grid-following Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The rising integration of renewable energy through power electronic converters has heightened the susceptibility of islanded microgrids to transient instability under large disturbances, primarily due to the converters’ low inertia and high nonlinearity. For an islanded microgrid with multiple converters, this paper estimates its transient stability based on Takagi-Sugeno method and introduces a phase compensation-based control strategy to enhance its transient stability. By incorporating angle difference between grid-following converter and grid-forming converter into current controller of grid-following converter, the balance between the system’s equivalent input and output torques can be accelerated. Simulation results validate the analysis and effectiveness of this strategy.

articleTitle: Integrated Modelling Approach for CCES Grid Connection and Fuzzy Logic Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Accelerating the energy transition and expanding the application of renewable energy have become international trends in the face of the urgent need for global sustainable development. However, the uncertainty of new energy sources brings multi-dimensional challenges to power system such as power balance and stability control. Compressed carbon dioxide energy storage(CCES), as a new large-scale energy storage technology, shows great potential for application. Although there have been studies focusing on the thermodynamics and system design of CCES, the studies on grid-connected adaptation and frequency regulation are still insufficient. To this end, this paper proposes an integrated CCES grid connected and fuzzy logic frequency regulation modelling approach, intending to enhance the applicability and frequency regulation capability of CCES in the power grid through refined modelling and innovative frequency regulation strategies. Through simulation experiments, the practicality and superiority of the proposed method are demonstrated, providing technical support for the application of CCES in new power system.

articleTitle: GIS External Partial Discharge Identification Algorithm Based On Multi-sensor Joint Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: A conventional gas insulated switchgear (GIS) online monitoring device cannot eliminate the interference from the external partial discharge. To address this issue, this paper proposes an anti-interference technology against GIS external partial discharge based on multi-sensor joint diagnosis. First, it is pointed out that the transmission attenuation of UFH signals is the cause of the difference in spectrum characteristics, by comparing the difference in signal spectrum characteristics between the external partial discharge and the internal partial discharge. Then, an algorithm for identifying external discharge signals is proposed. This algorithm can help determine whether the partial discharge signal comes from the outside of GIS or not by comparing the spectrum similarity between the partial discharge signal received by the sensor receiving the partial discharge and that received by multiple adjacent sensors. The field experiments and case study results show that this algorithm can effectively identify the GIS external partial discharge, thereby excluding any wrong alarm caused by the external partial discharge.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning Based Robust Control Strategy for Power Sharing and Voltage Regulation in DC Grid-Forming Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Grid-forming energy storage systems (ESSs) have been portraying an increasingly important role in modern DC power system. ESSs cannot only help to balance the power generations and consumptions, but are capable of flexibly adjust overall system dynamic responses given the presence of intermittent renewable sources. However, in a DC system enabled by grid-forming ESSs, numerous constant power loads (CPLs) with negative incremental impedances pose challenges to system stability, resulting in system not operating reliably at the desired operating point. In this paper, a model-free controller based on deep reinforcement learning (DRL) is proposed for a grid-forming ESS with CPL, which will improve the stability of the system and achieve current sharing among parallel converter modules. By constructing a Markov Decision Process (MDP) model, this control problem is transformed into a sequential decision-making problem. Notably, the controller can adaptively learn the optimal control strategy without any prior knowledge or mathematical modeling. The proposed controller not only maintains the stability of the system with time-varying CPL, but also presents rapid dynamic response with accurate tracking over a wide operating range. The effectiveness of the proposed controller is confirmed through simulation results.

articleTitle: Decentralized Collaborative Pricing and Shunting for Multiple EV Charging Stations Based on Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The extraordinary electric vehicle (EV) popularization in the recent years has facilitated research studies in alleviating EV energy charging demand. Previous studies primarily focused on the optimizations over charging stations’ (CS) profit and EV users’ cost savings through charge/discharge scheduling events. In this work, the random behaviours of EVs are considered, with EV users’ preferences over multi-CS characteristics modelled to imitate the potential CS selection disequilibrium. A price scheduling strategy under decentralized collaborative framework is proposed to achieve EV shunting in a multi-CS environment, while minimizing the charging cost through multi-agent reinforcement learning. The proposed problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) with uncertain transition probability.

articleTitle: Eigen-analysis and Coordination Control of Joint Frequency Regulation for Small Signal Stability in Hybrid Pumped Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To further enhance the reliability and regulatory flexibility of power systems, hybrid pumped storage systems (HPSSs) with variable-speed pumped storage units have been widely researched and applied. This work aims to conduct foundational research on the parameter coupling effect and coordinated control method for the small signal stability of HPSS. Firstly, an equivalent frequency regulation system model for conventional and variable-speed pumped storage units is established, and the response characteristics of the two units in dynamic regulation are compared. Moreover, a frequency coordination control method based on amplitude-frequency characteristics for HPSS is designed. The results show that the designed control strategy compresses the minimum damping ratio of the system, reduces its sensitivity to damping features, thus significantly improving the frequency regulation performance of the system. This study elucidates the advantages and improvement mechanisms of variable speed units in the joint operation of hydroelectric energy systems.

articleTitle: Bi-Level Optimal Allocation Method of Distributed Energy Resources in Medium and Low Voltage Distribution System Considering Source-Load-Storage Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Large-scale distributed energy resource access brings opportunities and challenges to the flexibility of distribution systems. Currently, multiple voltage levels coexist in distribution systems, research on optimal allocation for the flexibility improvement of distribution systems mainly focus on single voltage level systems, and the collaborative optimization potential of flexibility resources across voltage levels is not fully exploded. Therefore, a two-level optimal allocation method of distributed energy resources for the medium and low voltage distribution system considering source-load-storage coordination is proposed in this paper. First, the influence of distributed renewable energy acceptance is analyzed from the perspectives of flexibility, voltage distribution and topology of different voltage levels. Secondly, a two-level optimal allocation model of distributed energy resources in medium and low-voltage distribution system is formed, the multi-objective model is solved by the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II. Finally, an improved medium and low voltage distribution system is used for simulation verification. Results show that the proposed method can reduce voltage deviation and network operating loss, and improve the system economy and flexibility.

Author Keywords: medium and low voltage distribution systems

articleTitle: Carbon Reduction Assessment of Power Grid Projects Based on Improved Entropy Weight Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Power is a major industry for fossil energy consumption and carbon emissions, and the power grid, as a link between power production and consumption, can effectively promote the power industry to achieve synergistic effects in reducing pollution and carbon emissions by improving the carbon asset management capabilities of grid enterprises. Based on grid construction projects, this article designs an evaluation index system that can cover the entire process, and combines standard specifications to set differentiated evaluation criteria to construct an evaluation method that focuses on evaluating carbon emission levels while also considering guidance evaluations. This article uses an improved entropy weight method to more scientifically set the weight of carbon emission levels in grid projects, and constructs a quantitative evaluation model for carbon emissions in grid projects based on carbon emission analysis. Finally, by evaluating the carbon emissions of actual grid project plans, analyzing the weight ratio of each indicator in the transmission project, and verifying the scientific nature of the evaluation method proposed in this article, it provides an policy tool for grid enterprises to reduce pollution and carbon emissions in new construction projects.

articleTitle: Multi-resource High-frequency Control Requirements for Weak Power Grid to Cope with Short-term and Permanent Disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the multiple large-scale UHVDC operation in high altitude areas, the weak-sending power grid with a high proportion of new energy access brings the complexity of high-frequency problems under short-term and permanent disturbance, which makes the control effect of power grid security and stability defense line more demanding. The measures to cut the generator set under the traditional high-frequency defense line of the power grid may cause the problem of "cutting out non-online units" or "over-cutting units", so the targeted consideration of multi-resource coordination control participation in grid fault events becomes an effective means to trigger frequency exceeding limits. This paper proposes a method for screening high-frequency scenarios based on the actual transmission grid structure, combined with the disturbed power amount, comprehensive load amount and the power amount of new energy access, and defines a quantitative evaluation index for discriminating the disturbed system frequency. Suggestions are provided for the traditional defense line to consider coordinating the power modulation measures of new energy units, hydropower, and DC to deal with the high frequency problem of weak power grids. Finally, the feasibility is verified by simulation examples.

articleTitle: A Synchronized Sampling Algorithm for Differential Protection based on Measured Parameters under 5G/B5G
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Existing distribution networks are often characterized by multiple segments, multiple power sources, and bidirectional power flow, which diminishes the selectivity and sensitivity of traditional three-segment over current protection. Differential protection methods can effectively distinguish internal and external faults of protected line, but traditional differential protection relies on fiber optic communication, which poses difficulties in construction and high costs, making it difficult to be widely used. 5G/B 5G, with its characteristics of large bandwidth, low latency, and high reliability, can support communication functions of fault location and protection actions in distribution networks. However, wireless communication introduces latency and jitter of time, which cause serious problems for the synchronous sampling between different protection devices. Existing 5G/B5G-based distribution network differential protection device relies on the installation of GPS module at both ends for synchronous sampling. Due to the large scale of distribution networks, the cost of GPS modules severely affects their promotion, morever some distribution network terminals are placed indoors, making it difficult to install GPS-receiving antennas due to site condition. To address the above issue s, this paper analyzes the requirements of transmission delay in differential protection devices and proposes a synchronous sampling calibration algorithm using scalar parameters measured by protection devices. This method solves the wireless synchronous sampling problem of dual-end devices under different power loads. Simulation verifies the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, which can effectively solve the synchronous sampling problem in differential protection devices based on 5G/B5G communication.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Equivalent Impedance of Renewable Energy Considering Relay Protection Setting Calculations
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The substantial incorporation of renewable energy sources into power grids has profoundly influenced the setting calculations and accurate functioning of relay protection systems. Presently, the primary forms of renewable energy generation encompass photovoltaic (PV) systems, energy storage systems, direct-drive wind turbines, and doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) wind turbines. Different types of power sources exhibit distinct fault characteristics and equivalent impedances, generally categorized into inverter-based sources and doubly-fed induction sources. Due to differences in control methods, the fault characteristics of various renewable energy generation devices vary. When performing relay protection setting calculations, it is essential to consider the characteristics and control methods of renewable energy generation devices. Given that their fault current characteristics differ from those of traditional generation equipment, different setting methods are required to ensure that protection devices can accurately identify faults and respond promptly. To ensure the reliability and stability of relay protection systems under various operating conditions, it is crucial to thoroughly study the fault characteristics and equivalent impedances of renewable energy generation devices. Through simulation studies and experimental analysis, reasonable relay protection setting calculation methods can be developed, providing a basis for the optimization of protection devices and thereby ensuring the safe operation of power systems.

articleTitle: A Novel Reliability Evaluation Method for Distribution Networks with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the advancement of smart grids, renewable energy generation, and energy storage technologies, traditional distribution networks have gradually developed into new power distribution systems, incorporating a large number of distributed generations, electronic power devices and control equipment. To evaluate the impact of distributed generations on system reliability, a reliability evaluation method of distribution network with distributed generations is proposed. First, the system topology is identified using graph theory, which helps in determining its connection relations and power supply paths. Then a matrix operation relationship between the impact of equipment failure on load point power outages and the power outage time was established combined with the failure mode and impact analysis method. Finally, an island partitioning scheme and model solution method are developed to refine the reliability calculation indices for load points within the island. The effectiveness and practicability of the proposed algorithm are validated using a modified IEEE RBTS Bus 6 feeder F4 test case. The results demonstrate that reasonable grid connection schemes of distributed generations can effectively reduce the average power outage duration and enhance the overall power supply reliability of the system.

articleTitle: Optimization of Demand-Side Load Dispatch with Consideration for Dynamic Response and Reliability Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: At present, demand response methods dominated by the seller's market exhibit high reliability and feasibility. With the primary objective of maximizing grid-side benefits, this paper undertakes optimization of demand-side load scheduling. In pursuit of mitigating the impact of user behavior randomness on scheduling reliability, this paper establishes various response reliability models for different types of demand-side load. To further enhance the users' motivation to participate in demand response, this study has developed dynamic reliability assessment models for different users. Finally, a scheduling model was developed with the objective of maximizing scheduling capacity reliability and minimizing operational costs on the grid side, taking into account the minimum clearing benefit of users as a constraint. With the goal of maximizing grid benefits while enhancing user response enthusiasm, the demand-side resource scheduling operation mode is intended to be achieved. Additionally, the rationality and effectiveness of the proposed scheduling optimization model were validated through case study analyses.

articleTitle: Unified Modeling of Diverse Resilience Resources for Resilience Assessment of Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the context of low-carbon development of distribution systems, as the variety of resilient power supply resources (RPSRs) continues to grow, their complex modeling poses challenges for further expanding resilience-related research models. A key challenge is to develop a unified modeling method for diverse RPSRs. This paper proposes a resilience assessment method for distribution systems considering the unified modeling of RPSRs. By computing the power and energy boundaries of RPSRs, the key parameter attributes are summarized, and a method for transforming commonly used RPSRs into a unified model is provided. Subsequently, combined with the node survival expectation evaluation, a resilience assessment method for distribution systems is proposed. The test results show that the proposed modeling method effectively simplifies the modeling process and greatly improves the efficiency of resilience assessment.

articleTitle: A Way to Quickly Assess the Effectiveness of Typical Energy Saving and Carbon Reduction Technologies in Targeted Buildings
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Introduces the total amount and proportion of building energy consumption in China at the current stage, as well as the total amount and proportion of building operation energy consumption, to clarify the significance of reducing building operation energy consumption for achieving the national dual-carbon goals. Focuses on how to quickly select energy saving technologies and set emission reduction targets for target scenarios, proposing the necessity of establishing a building energy-saving and carbon-reduction engineering model mainly based on sub-metering data. Firstly, from the perspective of sub-metering, the typical building energy-saving and carbon-reduction technologies are sorted and classified. Through examples, it is illustrated how to use various data elements of energy saving technologies to build engineering models for calculating energy-saving amounts in conventional and complex situations. Secondly, from the perspective of data sources, various data elements are classified to form key data sets, providing a data foundation for the construction of engineering models. Finally, from the perspective of project implementation, it is emphasized that the engineering model needs to be continuously expanded in aspects such as the difficulty of implementation on-site and the investment payback period.

articleTitle: Large Language Model for Low-Carbon Energy Transition: Roles and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The low-carbon energy transition is a pressing global challenge that requires innovative approaches and technologies to achieve sustainable development. This paper explores the potential applications of the Large Language Model (LLM) in facilitating the low-carbon energy transition from an artificial intelligence perspective and summarizes the LLM roles in three directions: simulator, decision-maker, and expert. LLM can simulate low-carbon power scenarios, carbon market dynamics, climate risk assessments, and urban planning strategies. They can also operate power system, integrate renewable energy sources, predict demand patterns, and improve energy efficiency. Furthermore, LLM can serve as an expert in carbon accounting, satellite data interpretation, database management, and sustainable supply chain management. The paper also discusses challenges and future outlooks, including data quality and accessibility, cybersecurity, LLM training costs, interdisciplinary collaboration, and evaluation benchmarks. In conclusion, applying LLM in the low-carbon energy transition holds significant potential for driving innovation and sustainability, and further research is needed to maximize their impact.

articleTitle: Research on Robust Optimization Based Strategy for Enhancing Power Grid Consumption Capacity under Uncertain Wind Power Output
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: According to the uncertainty inherent in wind power output, robust optimization is employed to manage this variability. An uncertainty set is defined to represent wind power output, and a robust parameter is used to adjust the set's size. To simplify the calculation, the system's power flow equation is linearized. This involves approximating the cosine function, which relates voltage amplitude and phase angle to active and reactive power, using multiple linear segments for linearity. The wind power consumption model is established taking into account the system constraints impacting the absorption rate of wind power, and various factors influencing the capacity for wind power absorption are thoroughly investigated. The main factors affecting wind power consumption are the technical capabilities of grid connection, the system's peak regulation capacity, and the grid's transmission capacity. Finally, using the IEEE-39 system, a model is created with yalmip programming to analyze how the grid's transmission capacity limits wind power consumption rates.

articleTitle: Study on Enhancing the Total Factor Assurance Capability of Energy Internet Enterprises
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The construction of the energy Internet ecosystem and the enterprise's all-factor guarantee capability is an important development direction of the future energy and power industry, and the complete and mature all-factor guarantee can effectively promote the stable and healthy development of energy Internet enterprises. Therefore, there is an urgent need to carry out research to improve the all-factor guarantee capacity of energy Internet enterprises. This paper proposes a method for analysing the total factor guarantee capacity of energy Internet enterprises in the light of the construction and development of energy Internet enterprise ecosystem. First, the value demands of different subjects in the energy Internet ecosphere are analysed, and the total factor productivity of China's strategic emerging industries is measured and decomposed by the non-parametric Malmquist index method based on data envelopment analysis. On this basis, the evaluation system of total factor importance of energy Internet enterprise construction is constructed, and the basic principles of evaluation based on the four aspects of objectivity, fairness, timeliness and comprehensiveness are determined. Finally, with the orientation of activating the factor power to promote the enterprise's total factor high-quality development, we explored the path of total factor development of energy Internet enterprises from the four aspects of technological upgrading, management mode improvement, data mining, and talent construction, so as to improve the enterprise's ability of total factor development.

articleTitle: Benefit Evaluation System and Method for Integrated Generation-grid-load-storage Projects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: To promote the local consumption of new energy and reduce the cost of energy use on the load side, the integrated generation-grid-load-storage project (IGP) has received widespread attention. Since it involves many interested parties and flexible resources, the traditional evaluation method is no longer applicable to the IGP. This paper proposes an evaluation system and benefit assessment method based on the characteristics of the IGP. Firstly, key indicators describing the characteristics of the IGP are proposed, and a comprehensive evaluation index system is constructed. Secondly, the subjective and objective weights of each index are calculated by the hierarchical analysis method and entropy weight method respectively, and the combined weights obtained by the two methods are solved based on the principle of game theory. After that, the rank-sum-ratio comprehensive assessment method is used to assess the benefits of different cases. The results of the case study show that the proposed method is reasonable and can effectively reflect the characteristics of the IGP.

articleTitle: Research on Closed-loop Collaborative Linkage Mechanism and Typical Scenarios based on Effective Price Verification of Power Grid Planning and Investment
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In the current process of the New Power Systems construction, the power grid, as a key hub platform connecting power sources and loads, plays a critical role in ensuring the access and consumption of renewable energy and promoting the safe and reliable operation of the power system. For a long time, Chinese power industry has adhered to the important principle of planning and leadership. The power industry development planning is generally the responsibility of energy authorities. Power grid enterprises make investment plans in accordance with the power development plan and are responsible for implementing the power grid investment projects. In actual implementation, the preliminary work of power grid projects usually requires investment approval by industry authorities such as the National Development and Reform Commission (NDRC) and National Energy Administration (NEA) or their provincial affiliations’. As the only channel to effectively guide the investment of power grid enterprises, the determination of power transmission and distribution prices is the responsibility of the price authority such as the Price Department of NDRC. The current three links of power grid planning, investment approval, and electricity price determination are relatively independent, which objectively results in the weakening of the synergistic effect of all parties when planning changes, investment changes, price constraints, etc. occurs. Therefore, this article conducts an in-depth study of the current status of Chinese power grid planning investment, proposes a closed-loop collaborative linkage mechanism to ensure effective channelization of power grid planning investment, and proposes a linkage operation model for typical scenarios such as planning adjustments, investment changes, and price constraints, providing guidance for the power industry and the optimization mechanism design of the price authority provides decision-making reference.

articleTitle: A novel estimation and apportion method of frequency modulation mileage cost
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In order to solve the unreasonable problem of frequency modulation mileage cost allocation in traditional methods and better adapt to the requirements of new energy development, a novel method of frequency modulation mileage cost estimation and allocation is proposed. The traditional frequency modulation mileage allocation method is introduced, and the unreasonable factors of compensation cost calculation and allocation mechanism are analyzed. The effective frequency modulation mileage index is proposed to evaluate the frequency modulation contribution rate of the frequency modulation power supply. The refined fluctuation deviation index is also proposed to evaluate the frequency modulation demand generated by the fluctuation of generation output or electricity load of market members. A refined frequency modulation mileage cost estimation and allocation method is proposed by more detailed statistics of effective frequency modulation mileage and fluctuation deviation. The method calculates the effective frequency modulation mileage and the fluctuation deviation of market members by time period, realizes the statistics and apportion of frequency modulation mileage cost by time period, and solves the unreasonable problem of cost calculation and apportion in traditional apportion method. Finally, a numerical example based on the actual data of a provincial power grid was constructed to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. The numerical example results show that the proposed method can more effectively calculate the frequency modulation mileage cost and change its allocation result, which is helpful to promote new energy to improve its regulation strategy and reduce the burden of power grid frequency modulation.

articleTitle: The Application of Deep Peak Load Regulation Technology in Newly-Built Coal-Fired Power Units
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the advancement of the "dual carbon" strategy, the installed capacity of clean energy such as photovoltaics and wind power continues to increase. Due to their instability in power output, they have brought impacts on the safe and stable operation of the power grid. Therefore, the importance of traditional coal-fired power units in providing peak load regulation resources and integrating clean energy into the grid has become increasingly prominent, making them an indispensable part of serving the "dual carbon" strategy in the power industry. In the context of deep peak load regulation, this article introduces the construction of two new units for the Huadian Shidongkou First Power Plant's 2×650,000-kilowatt capacity coal-to-electricity replacement project, including the manufacturing of main equipment such as boilers, steam turbines, and auxiliary equipment, optimization of key parameters and structures, as well as optimization control technologies for deep peak load regulation, including wide-load automatic control technology. It also discusses the experiences in commissioning and operation of deep peak load regulation, which enhances the flexibility of unit operation after commissioning, adapts to the needs of power dispatch situations, and strengthens the competitiveness of thermal power enterprises.

articleTitle: Multi-type Energy Storage Planning Method for A High Proportion of New Energy Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The "dual carbon" goal promotes large-scale integration of new energy into the grid. Energy storage plays an important role in the integration of new energy into the grid due to its functions such as peak shaving, frequency regulation, and system support. However, energy storage faced a chaotic situation of small scale, scattered distribution, and lack of unified planning and layout in previous applications. In addition, energy storage could not recover investment due to not participating in scheduling operations. Therefore, it is necessary to gradually plan the scale and layout of energy storage based on the characteristics and functions of energy storage, combined with regional energy storage needs, in order to improve the efficiency of energy storage application, play a regulatory role, and further ensure the safe and stable operation of a high proportion of new energy power systems. Previous studies have mostly focused on a single type of energy storage planning, and there is a lack of comprehensive benefit evaluation. This article proposes a multi-type energy storage planning method for power systems based on basic routes of demand analysis, technology selection, capacity planning, energy storage layout, operation mode, and comprehensive benefit evaluation. In capacity planning, a power system model including new energy output was established, and a multi-type energy storage scale optimization method with the goal of minimizing system energy consumption cost was proposed. Finally, the feasibility of the planning method was verified through an example.

articleTitle: Framework for Optimal Planning of Multi-Energy Systems in Active Distribution Networks Considering N-1 Generator Contingency
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the growing awareness of environmental issues globally, there is a shift towards converting fossil energy systems into multi-energy systems powered by renewable energy resources. Establishing multi-energy systems in active distribution networks is considered an efficient approach to reducing carbon emissions, which in turn demands the development of innovative planning methodologies to ensure their cost-effectiveness and reliability. This paper establishes a novel mixed integer linear model to optimize the capacity allocation, equipment selection, placement, and corresponding operation plan for the active distribution networks incorporating multi-energy microgrids and demand response. Compared with traditional static reserve constraints for N-1 generator contingency, we propose a set of novel linear equations to dynamically allocate reserve in the active distribution network, which greatly reduces the computation time and improves the robustness against potential generator failure. Several case studies demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed optimal planning model and give valuable insights into the low-carbon design for multi-energy systems in active distribution networks.

articleTitle: Low-carbon Operation Optimization Strategy For Electric-thermal Sharing In Multi-microgrid Based on Nash Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Against the backdrop of dual carbon objectives, promoting the effective use of new energy sources and achieving low-carbon operation in power systems are critical goals for power system reform. This paper begins by developing a model for multiple microgrids and integrating carbon capture and power-to-gas systems in combined heat and power (CHP) to minimize carbon emissions. Then, a cooperative model for multi-microgrid electricity and heat energy sharing is formulated using Nash game theory, decomposed into subproblems for maximizing cooperative alliance benefits and redistributing cooperative benefits. Finally, the subproblem of maximizing cooperative alliance benefits is further decomposed into two linearly solvable subproblems, solved using alternating direction method of multipliers. In the subproblem of redistributing cooperative benefits, analytic hierarchy process is employed to evaluate the contribution of each microgrid in electric-thermal sharing, ensuring fair distribution of cooperative benefits. Case studies validate that the proposed approach effectively enhances economic benefits for each microgrid and significantly reduces carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Simulation and Optimization of a Techno-economic Virtual Power Plant Using CloudPSS DSLab
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of renewable energy and flexible loads, such as electric vehicle, the structure of the power supply and load demand has undergone significant transformations. These changes have gradually shaped a new type of power system that primarily relies on renewable energy, integrates source, network, load, and storage synergistically, features active networks, and complements multi-energy systems. This shift has stimulated extensive research into virtual power plants (VPPs), which are capable of flexibly coordinating source and load resources. In this paper, a VPP is designed to optimize scheduling for a regional distribution network experiencing source-load imbalance. Initially, the CloudPSS DSLab platform is utilized to model distributed energy resources and the distribution power system. Subsequently, the DSLab SDK is employed to obtain the distribution system's boundary conditions, including forecasted load and tariffs. Finally, considering both technical and economic objectives, an intraday optimization model for the VPP is established, and optimized to derive an optimal scheduling strategy for power sharing and interaction among multiple VPPs, and feasibility of the operation strategy is verified through simulation. The optimization results demonstrate that the flexible scheduling of VPPs effectively reduces reverse transmission and increases the accommodation of the renewables in the distribution network, enhances the network's reliability, improves power quality, and amplifies economic performance.

articleTitle: Construction Methods of Power Graph Based on New Generation Scheduling Technology Support System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In response to the evolving demands of the construction process for the new generation scheduling technology support system, which includes more comprehensive data attribute mining, intricate device connection relationships, and an increased need for real-time data sharing, this paper proposes the introduction of a unified power graph model. This model harnesses the capabilities of graph databases to effectively eliminate data silos and achieve seamless topology fusion among power objects across the entire network. Consequently, it offers a more intuitive visualization of the intricate connection relationships within the power grid. Furthermore, to ensure the reliability and efficiency of this power graph model, this paper has devised strategies for both online and scheduled updates. These strategies are geared towards establishing a power graph model that is not only real-time but also highly accurate, safe, and readily available. Taking a practical approach, this paper has started by focusing on the topology connection relationships within the station equipment and the broader main grid and distribution network. Through this implementation, this paper has successfully realized various power grid topology application scenarios. This, in turn, serves as a solid foundation for enhancing the management and analytical decision-making capabilities within the new generation scheduling technology support system.

Author Keywords: main grid and distribution network splicing

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Optimization Scheduling of Integrated Energy System Considering Carbon Emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: This paper presents a distributionally robust optimization scheduling approach for a park integrated energy system (PIES), targeting at carbon emissions reduction and uncertain renewable energy mitigation. With the historical data of renewable energy generations, the ambiguity set is generated using Wasserstein ball, without the assumption about probability distribution. Demand response of interruptible and schedulable loads is implemented to respond to the varying carbon emission intensity of the main grid at different times of a day. The proposed approach could flexibly adjust the scheduling strategies to balance economic efficiency and environmental friendliness. Simulation results validate the approach and reveal the influence of carbon emission constraint on operating cost and emission.

articleTitle: Cost Assessment of New Energy Transmission Lines Based on AHP-EWM-COPRAS Methodology
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Cleaner and lower carbonization is the direction of national energy development, but large-scale new energy grid connection is accompanied by a large number of grid-connected transmission line engineering project investment. Firstly, the basic characteristics of new energy transmission lines are sorted out, including line length, transmission capacity, transmission voltage level, etc., and the economic evaluation attributes system of new energy transmission lines is constructed, including natural factors, technological factors and cost factors, etc. Then, the hierarchical analysis method AHP , the entropy weight method EWM are used to intelligently identify the factors affecting the cost of new energy transmission lines, and calculate the attribute weight of each key factor; finally, taking the actual case as an example, COPRAS Combined Multi-Attribute Rating Analysis based on Ranked Score method is used to quantitatively assess the economics of new energy transmission lines. The cost utility of different schemes is analyzed through comparative analysis and sensitivity to provide decision makers with a scientific and reasonable basis for decision making and to promote the sustainable development of new energy transmission lines.

articleTitle: High-power Analog Hydrogen Production Electrolyzer Based on Multi-module Carrier Phase-shifted Current Source Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The combination of renewable energy generation and electrolytic hydrogen production is one of the important pathways to achieve carbon neutrality and peak carbon emissions. The electrolysis power supply is a key device for electrolytic hydrogen production. However, the use of real electrolytic cells as the load for electrolytic hydrogen production test systems faces many difficulties due to their high cost, low efficiency, and the difficulty of hydrogen storage. Simulating the electrolytic cell using power electronics converters can help reduce system losses, improve safety, and lower testing costs. The topology of the simulated electrolytic cell requires the power electronics converter to have characteristics such as low input voltage, high input current, low input current ripple, and low grid current harmonics. Therefore, this paper proposes a high-power simulated hydrogen production electrolytic cell based on a multi-module carrier phase-shifted current source converter, and proposes a phase-shifting strategy to improve harmonics. The proposed simulated electrolytic cell not only accurately simulates the characteristics of the electrolytic cell, but also can feed back electrical energy to the grid. Its modular design is beneficial for simplifying control and capacity expansion. This paper verifies the advantages of the proposed simulated electrolytic cell device through simulation.

articleTitle: Power System Capacity Expansion Considering Electric Hydrogen Production and Hydrogen Mixed Gas Turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Hydrogen has the characteristics of zero pollution and easy conversion, which is significant to realize the low-carbon transformation of the energy system. At present, the method to improve the flexibility for the large intermittent renewable integration is mainly to install enough energy storage in the power system. However, to install the conversion equipment between electricity and hydrogen energy for flexibility has not been studied totally. Especially, the hydrogen mixed gas turbine is rarely considered in the capacity expansion of the power system. Therefore, this paper proposes a power system capacity expansion method considering the electric hydrogen production and hydrogen mixed gas turbines. Based on the dynamic hydrogen mixing characteristics and the unit grouping technique, a capacity planning model of the hydrogen mixed gas turbine is established, in which complete a set of flexibility constraints are considered. The optimal investment capacity and its total cost of the power system are obtained under different renewable energy penetration levels. Finally, the proposed method is simulated and verified by a practical system. The results show that the mode based on the renewable energy, the water electrolysis technology for the hydrogen production, as well as the hydrogen mixed gas turbine can contribute to the renewable energy integration and the total cost reduction of the power system.

articleTitle: A Sub-synchronous Oscillation Suppression Method for Direct-drive Wind Farms Connected to VSC-HVDC Systems Based on Hybrid Passivity/Small-gain Theorem
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The direct-drive wind farms connected to voltage source converter-based high voltage direct current (VSC-HVDC) transmission systems are easy to cause sub-synchronous oscillation (SSO), which seriously endangers the stability of the system. Based on the hybrid passivity/small-gain (HPS) theorem, an SSO suppression method is proposed. Firstly, the HPS theorem is reviewed, and the stability evaluation method is obtained by analyzing the properties of the two subsystems of the feedback loop. Secondly, wind farm side admittance and sending side impedance are modeled, and the HPS properties are analyzed, respectively. It is pointed out that the gain greater than 1 in the frequency band that does not satisfy the passive property is the main reason for the SSO. Thirdly, a method is proposed to suppress the SSO by reducing the gain of the target frequency band through the admittance compensation control of the converter. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by simulation. The designed controller can effectively suppress the SSO and improve the stability of the system.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Operational Benefits of Energy Storage Plant Participation in the Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The analysis of how energy storage power plants contribute to the spot market is vital for developing energy storage projects. The development of new types of energy storage mainly based on electrochemical energy storage and pumped storage power plants in mechanical energy storage is an important step to enhance the regulation capacity, comprehensive efficiency and safety and security of energy and power systems as well as the operational benefits of the spot market. By establishing comprehensive models for both the lifecycle costs and potential revenues of energy storage, and analyzing the market operations benefits within a specific province using economic metrics like unit cost and unit income, valuable insights can be offered for guiding the development of energy storage projects and making investment decisions.

articleTitle: Fault Diagnosis Method of Power Transformer Based on Historical Case
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Power transformer is an indispensable key component in power systems. The accurate and reliable fault diagnosis is crucial to ensure the safe and stable operation of the power grid. Traditional diagnosis methods suffer from issues such as rule conflicts, high data quality requirements, and a lack of historical case analysis, leading to suboptimal performance in practical applications. Therefore, this paper proposes a historical case-enhanced oil chromatography diagnostic method. Firstly, building upon multiple improved ratio methods and incorporating fuzzy processing, the method calculates the fault pattern membership degrees. Secondly, a neural network is employed to analyze gas content data and historical case texts, determining the weights for the ratio methods. Lastly, based on the weights and the membership degrees of various ratio methods, the final fault probability is computed. Experimental validation demonstrates that the proposed method effectively provides equipment diagnostic results, showing an improvement of 8.21% to 24.25% in F1 values compared to traditional methods.

articleTitle: A Power System Optimization Planning Model Considering Renewable Energy Time Synergy
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: As a consequence of the exponential growth in renewable energy production, the issue of its consumption has become increasingly salient, with a concomitant rise in instances of wind and light abandonment. As research progresses, scholars are increasingly aware of the temporal complementarity between renewable energy generations. This phenomenon presents an opportunity to enhance the power system's overall consumption capacity. However, the input data for capturing this complementarity is characterized by a lengthy time span and high resolution, which presents a significant challenge in optimization model. In this paper, a Markov chain model-based time synergy model for renewable energy is proposed as a means of reducing the computational complexity. The proposed model is capable of accelerating the processing of time-dependent information from historical records, thereby facilitating the generation of representative series. Case studies show that the proposed time synergy model markedly diminishes the discrepancy and the computational burden associated with the approximate solution of the full-time span optimization model, when compared to the traditional models.

articleTitle: Research on Optimal Selection of Submarine Cable Cross-Section Considering Ampacity Matching in All Laying Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Submarine power cable systems commonly utilize uniform specification cables for the transmission of power. However, these cables exhibit significant variations in heat dissipation capabilities along different laying sections. Inadequate ampacity in a specific laying section can adversely impact the overall ampacity of the transmission system, leading to underutilization of the cable's transmission capability. Therefore, for the purpose of maximizing the utilization of the transmission capability of submarine cable, it is crucial to identify the thermal bottleneck positions of submarine cable lines and propose the measures to improve the heat dissipation environment of thermal bottleneck positions. This paper presented a finite element simulation-based approach to calculate the ampacity of the cable in each laying section. The simulation results reveal that the thermal bottleneck sections of the cable are the J-tube section and the landing section. To address these thermal bottleneck points, measures based on high thermal conductivity materials and heat pipes were proposed. The mechanisms of proposed measures to enhance the cable ampacity was also analyzed based on the cable's thermal model. Furthermore, the benefits of these ampacity enhancement measures for the improved utilization of existing cable systems and the cross-sectional selection of new cable systems were discussed. The research presented in this paper holds significant importance in the design of offshore wind farm operational and maintenance strategies.

articleTitle: Research on the Frequency Dynamic Stability Characteristics of High-proportion New Energy Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The increase in installed renewable capacity reveals a power grid with a higher proportion of renewables and extensive use of power electronics, necessitating advanced grid management solutions, the DC cross-region transmission capacity continues to increase, and the transmission network characterized by hybrid AC-DC connection is more prone to frequency overrun or instability. This study examines the frequency dynamic stability of power grids with a high proportion of renewable energy, aiming to address the challenges and solutions for maintaining grid reliability. Primarily, a simplified model of high-proportion new energy grid is constructed, and a frequency stability evaluation index suitable for DC blocking fault is proposed. Then, considering variables such as the proportion of renewable energy, start-up capacity of thermal power, total load, and level of renewable energy involvement in frequency modulation, grid frequency comparison diagrams are generated for multiple scenarios involving DC bipolar block faults. These diagrams are utilized to analyze the frequency stability patterns of grids with significant proportions of renewable energy. Finally, the key characteristic parameters which can reflect the difference of frequency stability characteristics of high- proportion renewable energy grids in different scenarios are extracted, and their effectiveness can be verified in different scenarios.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Islanded Hydropower Plant Sending Terminal Frequency Limit Control Support Capability Considering Frequency Security
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Frequency stability is a critical issue for modern power systems characterized by low inertia and weak damping due to the large-scale integration of renewable energy sources. Addressing the challenge of reasonable quantification and effective evaluation of the frequency recovery support capability provided by frequency limit control (FLC) in hydropower plants at ultra-high voltage direct current (UHVDC) sending terminals, this paper proposes novel evaluation indicators for FLC support capability considering frequency security. The rapidity and continuity of the FLC support capability are evaluated through multiple dimensions, including the rate of change of frequency support contribution, maximal frequency deviation support contribution, and frequency recovery time support contribution. By calculating and comparing these indicators under various dead zone and control parameter settings, the variation patterns are clarified. Furthermore, a method for FLC control parameter division that integrates these three indicators is proposed, providing a reliable basis for selecting FLC parameters.

articleTitle: Distributed Electricity Pricing Strategy for Prosumers Considering Carbon Cost Transmission Chain
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: With the construction of new power systems and the increasing proportion of distributed energy, complex distributed transactions have led to redundancy in carbon trading calculations and increased information security risks in the market. Currently, the electricity market mechanism is still not perfect, and the pricing strategies for distributed energy have not been well integrated with carbon trading. In this context, a distributed energy pricing strategy that considers carbon price factors is proposed. First, a carbon cost transmission chain is constructed based on the interpretative structural modeling method, and a carbon cost transmission rate model is established, considering the degree of its own carbon price transmission changes and their impact relationships. Then, based on the Ramsey theory, production and consumption surpluses are considered to determine the market quotation that maximizes social benefits. Thus, a distributed energy pricing strategy is proposed on the user side that accounts for carbon costs. Finally, the proposed pricing strategy can reasonably allocate the electricity prices and enhance user benefits.

articleTitle: Distributionally Robust Chance-Constrained Optimization Dispatch Method for New Power Systems with Virtual Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Addressing the issue of renewable energy integration caused by large-scale wind power grid connection, a novel electric power system distributed robust joint chance-constrained (DRJCC) optimization dispatch model incorporating captive power plants with virtual energy storage (VES), wind, thermal, and hydropower units is proposed. Initially, considering that high-energy-consuming enterprises' self-provided power plants (SPPPs) can accept the unified dispatch of the public grid, three operational modes for the SPPPs as VES participating in the main grid interaction and their call costs are presented, and a two-stage stochastic optimization model for the new power system including VES is constructed. Subsequently, a data-driven DRJCC approach is utilized to address the uncertainty in wind output, constructing a fuzzy set of probability distributions for uncertain variables based on the Wasserstein distance, and expanding the original stochastic optimization model to a W-DRJCC optimization model. Further, by applying strong duality theory, Bonferroni inequality, and Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) approximation, the proposed distributed robust model is transformed into a mixed-integer linear programming problem for solution. Finally, case analyses on an improved RTS-24 power system demonstrate that the proposed method can balance economic efficiency and robustness, offering significant insights for the construction of operational modes for enterprises' SPPPs to participate in grid interaction.

articleTitle: Research on Core Development Capability of Energy Internet Enterprises Based on Complex System Synergy Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: At present, China's economy has been transformed from a stage of high-speed growth to a stage of high-quality development, and power grid enterprises are no longer confined to the traditional way of development and are gradually moving closer to electricity-based energy Internet enterprises, and enterprise construction is in a critical period of economic structure optimisation, development mode change, and change of growth momentum, so there is an urgent need to study the core development capability of the enterprise that covers enterprise construction, support business and emerging business development, ecosystem construction, and the enterprise core development capability of all-factor guarantee. This paper proposes research on the core development capability of energy Internet enterprises based on the composite system synergy model. Firstly, based on the composite system synergy model, it builds a synergy evaluation model of the core development of energy Internet enterprises, establishes the indicator system of each development capability system and specifies the weight of the indicators; secondly, it carries out a comprehensive synergy evaluation of the core development level of energy Internet enterprises. Finally, the main factors affecting the core development of the enterprise are analysed through the arithmetic example, which opens up the construction path for promoting the core development of the energy Internet enterprise.

articleTitle: Optimal Planning of Zero-Carbon Off-Grid Ammonia-Hydrogen-Based Microgrids Considering Hybrid Types of Electrolyzer Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: The off-grid ammonia-hydrogen-based microgrid is recognized as a promising paradigm for industrial decarbonization. In this paper, we propose a novel planning model for off-grid ammonia-hydrogen-based microgrids, where the hydrogen is produced in a distributed manner and the ammonia is synthesized in a large-scale energy-intensive plant. In specific, the proposed planning model considers hybrid types of electrolyzer modules and systematically investigates the operational constraints of distribution networks and hydrogen storage equipment, enabling distributed flexible hydrogen production. To seamlessly bridge distributed hydrogen sources and centralized ammonia production site, the delivery of hydrogen through the transportation network is structured as a vehicle routing problem. Eventually, the effectiveness of the proposed model is validated through case studies. Simulation results show that the proposed model lowers the total system cost by 11.8% compared with the simplified scenario which uses one single type of electrolyzer.

articleTitle: Multi-Criteria Dynamic Partition Modeling Approach for State Estimation in Complex Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Partition modeling serves as the basis for distributed state estimation in complex active distribution networks. Considering the dynamic and complex nature of distribution network operational states, this paper proposes a multi-criteria dynamic partition modeling approach for state estimation in complex active distribution networks, providing a foundational partition model for state estimation. Firstly, based on the configuration analysis of real-time measurements, virtual measurements, and pseudo measurements in active distribution networks, a multi-criteria comprehensive indicator system for state estimation is established. Secondly, a genetic algorithm is employed to determine the optimal comprehensive indicators for each region. The dynamic partition model is constructed by integrating optimal indicators, operational states, and control requirements, and the triggering mechanism for partition structure updates is designed. Finally, the proposed dynamic partition modeling method is validated through improved IEEE 118-node simulation examples, demonstrating its ability to achieve rational dynamic partitioning in complex active distribution networks.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Capacity Adequacy and Flexibility Capability of Energy Storage Systems in New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Under the development requirements of the 'dual carbon' goals and the new power system, renewable energy is rapidly expanding. However, challenges such as the uncertainty of renewable energy output, frequent extreme weather events, and the increasing peak load of current electricity demand pose significant obstacles to the secure and economical operation of the power system. Energy storage can effectively mitigate peak shaving and fill valleys over certain time scales, thereby smoothing the uncertainty of renewable energy. Evaluating the adequacy of energy storage and its flexibility in adjustment is crucial for optimizing its planning and rational deployment. This paper addresses uncertainties in both supply and demand, along with the seasonal variations in renewable energy availability.to establish a capacity adequacy assessment framework for new power systems across different time scales. This framework aims to provide references for determining the reasonable capacity requirements of the power system. Starting from marginal benefits and saturation effects, it investigates quantitative evaluation methods for the multi-time-scale, multi-type energy storage capacity value and flexible regulation capabilities, laying a foundation for fully assessing the various values of multi-type energy storage and leveraging their complementary advantages.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Sequence Impedance Characteristics of Doubly Fed Induction Generator (DFIG) on the Operation Characteristics of Sudden Variable Distance Protection (SVDP)
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Sudden Variable Distance Protection (SVDP) has been utilized in power systems due to its extensive protection range and strong resistance to transition resistance. An in-depth study examined the fault characteristics of Doubly Fed Induction Generators (DFIG) under short circuit conditions. Special focus was given to the disparity between the positive and negative sequence impedances of DFIG and how this affects the operational performance of power frequency SVDP. In wind power systems, when a fault occurs, the positive and negative sequence impedances at the wind farm side are unequal, with the positive sequence impedance being significantly higher than the negative sequence impedance. This disparity significantly diminishes the effectiveness of the sudden variable relay. A thorough analysis was conducted on the protection operation characteristics under various conditions (including no-load and loaded scenarios), revealing that factors such as increased wind power system impedance, higher system load, and improved reliability coefficient broadly impact the protection range of SVDP. Simulation verification was performed to confirm these findings. The study's conclusions offer a theoretical foundation for enhancing the protection range of SVDP and improving its operational characteristics in wind power grid-connected systems.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Energy Communities with Blockchain Technology: Opportunities, Challenges, and Future Perspectives
publicationTitle: 2024 4th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: Blockchain technology, characterized by its decentralization, transparency, and security, is poised to significantly transform energy communities worldwide. Within the context of the energy sector, blockchain presents a groundbreaking opportunity to address longstanding inefficiencies and barriers to sustainability. This paper explores how blockchain technology can revolutionize energy communities by enabling peer-to-peer energy trading, enhancing grid management, and facilitating the integration of renewable energy sources. It identifies key challenges faced by energy communities, including the lack of transparency in energy transactions, difficulties i n managing distributed energy resources, and the high costs associated with energy trading and grid management. The main contributions of this paper include a comprehensive analysis of the potential of blockchain to democratize energy access, ensure transparent and secure energy transactions, and promote the adoption of renewable energy. Moreover, it examines the technological, regulatory, and market challenges that must be addressed to realize the full potential of blockchain in revolutionizing energy communities. Through a blend of theoretical insights and practical examples, this paper aims to provide a holistic view of the opportunities, challenges, and future perspectives of leveraging blockchain technology in the energy sector, offering a blueprint for a more sustainable, efficient, and equitable energy future.
